listings.name: 3D Pinball for Windows: Space Cadet (SpaceCadetPinball)
listings.summary: Space Cadet on modern desktop systems using your own Windows or Full Tilt game resources. The official Windows player is a ZIP; upstream or you provide updates.

steps.title: Keep the player and your game resources together
steps.instruction: For the modern Windows x64 player, extract the complete SpaceCadetPinballx64Win.zip into a separate folder you control. Keep SpaceCadetPinball.exe, SDL2.dll and SDL2_mixer.dll together. Add your own original Windows Space Cadet or supported Full Tilt resources to that folder; the port download does not include them. The x86 and Windows XP packages are different alternatives. There is no installer or converter to finish.

steps.title: Save the player, then choose Play
steps.instruction: Select SpaceCadetPinball.exe with that folder as its working directory, save launch details, then choose Play separately. If the game reports missing resources, follow its folder search message and the upstream guide. macOS application packages and Linux distribution/Flatpak or source-build routes keep their own upstream installation instructions; a Windows ZIP does not establish their native qualification.

steps.title: Keep the intended table and its scores together
steps.instruction: For Release 2.1.0, use a separate working folder for the table data you intend to play. The player searches the working folder before its executable folder and user profile; it normally tries Full Tilt CADET.DAT before Windows PINBALL.DAT, then DEMO.DAT. Its Prefer 3D Pinball data option changes that file preference. Keep the matching resource set together rather than mixing editions. The same imgui_pb.ini stores options, controls and high-score names/scores; preserve it as a complete file with its verification value, not selected score lines. Other player copies can share that profile. Changing the runtime folder does not isolate it, and original Windows registry scores are not automatically imported.

warnings: Close the game and preserve your original/custom resources, any chosen external font, and the SpaceCadetPinball user profile before changing versions.

listings.name: 40 Winks / Faderz48
listings.summary: Build and play 40 Winks on Windows or Linux with upstream’s setup tools and your own clean USA Nintendo 64 ROM.

steps.title: Get the upstream setup for your platform
steps.instruction: Open the v0.1.7-alpha release linked below and pick the Windows x64 setup EXE or Linux x86-64 AppImage. Check the file against its SHA-256 sidecar before opening it. Both paths need a clean big-endian USA .z64 from your own game. Setup checks SHA-256 057232ef7618e25f5645df50d3cd45f08cb5a2cccb3e2fdf48faa8755c4ddb1a. Keep that original available for later launches.

steps.title: Build the playable copy once
steps.instruction: On Windows, open the upstream setup, select the matching ROM and choose a folder for the generated player. On Linux, install the development dependencies from the build guide, then open the upstream self-building AppImage, select the ROM and choose where to save the playable AppImage. First setup needs Internet access and builds locally. On later Windows launches open 40-Winks-PC-Port.exe from the output folder. On Linux reopen the original AppImage to start the locally built player.

warnings: The Windows setup is unsigned. Follow your usual executable trust settings.
Keep the original outside the build and player folders. Replacement builds and player data are managed through upstream.

references.title: Keep Windows settings and Controller Pak saves
references.instruction: Preserve %LOCALAPPDATA%\40-winks-pc-port when changing the player. The separate %LOCALAPPDATA%\40WinksBuild stores build tools and generated files.

references.title: Linux build requirements and launcher paths
references.instruction: Follow the tagged build guide for Git, Python, CMake, a C++20 compiler, SDL2 development files, Vulkan and the runtime dependencies. The builder tracks the selected ROM and playable AppImage under the 40-winks-pc-port directory in XDG_CONFIG_HOME. The first-run launcher suggests ~/Applications/40-Winks-Recompiled-x86_64.AppImage for the playable copy. Its build cache is under XDG_CACHE_HOME. Preserve the game data under XDG_DATA_HOME/40-winks-pc-port (normally ~/.local/share/40-winks-pc-port), or the data directory you explicitly chose.

steps.instruction: Use an independently permitted complete The Sims original-Xbox Windows player, separate from any desktop, handheld or other console edition. steps.title: Prepare your own game files with the project’s tools
steps.instruction: Complete the supported upstream build from your own Ace Combat 5: The Unsung War USA SLUS-20851 original. Its extracted SLUS_208.51 must be 3634092 bytes, SHA-256 c3594227605307806592416dbd723bf5771952e279ee281a40da305426667385. Keep the ISO or extracted disc files for runtime reads. Upstream GCC 15+, MSYS2 UCRT64 SDL3, Python, CMake/Ninja and Vulkan SDK preparation remains outside Portcove. Retain all documented overrides/hooks during generation; the shorter diagnostic CMake command is not the supported complete recipe.

steps.title: Select the completed game player
steps.instruction: Select the completed build/gcc/ac5.exe, with its creating project root as working directory. Use --data followed by the absolute generated directory containing ps2_image.bin, --disc followed by your absolute own ISO or extracted-disc directory, and --watchdog 0. That is the documented normal play command: the upstream watchdog otherwise abandons a no-field interval during the normal initial black screen. Do not select gsreplay, a compiler or a generator. Keep the adjacent shaders, SDL3.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll, with the driver Vulkan loader available.

steps.title: Allow the game to finish normally
steps.instruction: The normal player stays open for the game session until exit; --vblanks 0 is the documented default. A short diagnostic loop in the source does not establish a gameplay time limit. Portcove has not observed startup or gameplay for this route.

steps.title: Review launch details, then choose Play
steps.instruction: Review and consent to the selected game executable, working folder and launch arguments, then choose Play separately. You and the project manage setup, version changes and recovery. Removing the registration leaves all external files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, migration or deletion for this copy. Before changing versions, close the game and all companions and keep the complete working copy and every data location. Review and select the executable again if its files change.

warnings: Use only a copy and components you are permitted to use. Preserve originals, required player files, saves, settings, mods, caches, logs, backups and custom locations; another executable may share them. Source inspection and test fixtures do not confirm gameplay, real saves or behavior in the installed app, or establish Supported status or protected acceptance.

references.title: Keep the working game and every data location
references.instruction: Keep the entire creating project, original ISO/extracted data, generated C/image and matching native runtime. Saves and mods are relative to the chosen working directory; PS2_SAVE_DIR overrides saves. ac5_settings.ini, ac5_pipelines.cache and ac5_pipelines.keys live beside ac5.exe. These are this runtime’s memory-card format, explicitly not PCSX2 cards. Preserve every save, setting, mod, Lua/native plugin, cache, log, backup and custom root with the creating version. Apache-2.0 project code and separate ImGui/Lua/dependency notices do not license your original game or arbitrary mods.

listings.name: Ace Combat 6 Recomp
listings.summary: Explore Ace Combat 6 Recomp and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Use your own files, or let Portcove unpack your disc image
steps.instruction: Play without choosing anything: put your own Ace Combat 6 Xbox 360 disc image beside ac6recomp.exe as AC6.iso, or your own extracted game files in assets with assets/default.xex. Nothing is asked of you. Or choose your own disc image once, and Portcove checks that it is the one reviewed image, then unpacks it into the assets folder. Unpacking replaces everything in assets with the verified copy, so files you added to assets by hand are not kept when it unpacks. AC6.iso, dlc, your settings and bindings, logs and saves are never touched by unpacking. A disc image you choose is used from the next runtime update of Ace Combat 6. Only that one reviewed image, labelled USA and Japan, is accepted for unpacking; other editions and regions, including Europe, are not supported. Keep your original copy separately. Choose Play after the files are ready; this portable package has no installer. Optional own DLC belongs in dlc; title-update data is a separate upstream input, not a runtime update.

warnings: Only the one reviewed image is accepted for unpacking; other editions and regions, including Europe, are not supported.
Keep a separate backup of the Windows Documents/ac6recomp folder before changing versions. Close the game before changing runtime files; older versions may not read newer saves.

Upstream requires Windows 10/11 x64, AVX2 and a Direct3D 12-capable GPU. This experimental release has known performance and rendering limits; Portcove gameplay and minimum-system observations remain unqualified.

references.title: Save locations, settings and custom data
references.instruction: Saves and the default texture-mod profile use your Windows Documents/ac6recomp folder. Runtime settings and keyboard bindings sit beside the player in ac6recomp.toml and ac6_input.toml; use forward slashes in TOML paths. Runtime caches and logs also appear beside the player. If Windows cannot resolve Documents, the upstream relative ac6recomp fallback stays beside the player. Custom data, disc, DLC, log, mod and diagnostic locations remain yours to preserve separately.

Shadow of the Colossus (2018) (PlayStation 4, US 1.00, CUSA08034)

steps.title: Prepare the PS4 remake with upstream first
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. The reviewed 0.70 Windows route is the Bluepoint2018 PS4 remake: CUSA08809 EU1.01 or CUSA08034 US1.00, with your own decrypted game folder containing eboot.bin, sce_module and sce_sys. PS2/PS3 releases are different inputs. Sound additionally needs your own console-dumped decrypted libSceNgs2.sprx and libSceUlt.sprx; those Sony modules are not supplied by this guide or covered by the runtime license. Follow upstream setup outside Portcove, select the correct game/modules and save settings before attachment.

steps.title: Keep the complete Windows package together
steps.instruction: The inspected0.70 SotC-PC.zip contains SotC-PC/SotC.exe, bin/bb-probe.exe, companion DLLs, _internal, scripts and launcher resources. Keep the entire extracted SotC-PC directory together in a writable location. SotC.exe is the frozen native frontend; selecting an internal probe, Python executable, DLL or original eboot.bin bypasses its saved setup. This registration does not download, extract or run setup.

steps.title: Select saved-settings play explicitly
steps.instruction: Select the prepared package’s SotC.exe, set its complete SotC-PC directory as working directory, and use the single argument --play. Review the exact selected intent, then request Play separately. With a valid saved game folder, this route waits for its --run child, which in turn waits for bin/bb-probe.exe. If setup is missing it opens the GUI instead: finish setup and close that attempt before retrying. No native run or child-cleanup observation is claimed by source inspection.

steps.title: Preserve all actual data locations
steps.instruction: The current package keeps launcher_settings.json in its user directory; the ordinary save/cache/log root is also user beside SotC.exe unless the saved user_dir or existing SOTC_USER_DIR selects another location. Keep the complete effective tree, sotc.ini, any legacy %APPDATA%/sotc-launcher/settings.json, original game/update/DLC folders and your console modules. The source can discover neighbouring -UPDATE/-patch folders and established source/data overrides. This guide sets no new override, moves no saves and promises no cross-copy or cross-version compatibility.

steps.title: Leave maintenance and shutdown with their owners
steps.instruction: Complete upstream updates, setup changes and repair outside an attached game session; the GUI updater can start an applier/successor. Close the actual game and all helpers before replacing files, retain independent recovery copies, then review/relink changed executable bytes. Let ordinary play end through the game before closing the tracked player. Forced termination is not proof of save flush or child quiescence. Portcove does not adopt updater successors or own runtime replacement.

steps.title: Check this release’s limits and required notices
steps.instruction: Preserve the project GPL notice and all component/NVIDIA notices; runtime licensing grants no rights to the original game or console firmware. Upstream performance, ending and GPU reports are attributable upstream claims. Maximum-texture crashes, some AMD GCN graphics problems and experimental frame generation/60FPS limitations remain in the selected upstream instructions. No Portcove gameplay, save/reload, installed-app or Supported acceptance is claimed. Removing registration preserves every external file; managed installation, update, rollback, backup and deletion are not offered.

warnings: Use only the independently permitted PS4-remake installation and console modules; retain all external player data and complete maintenance upstream.

listings.name: Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition (GemRB)
listings.summary: Use your installed Baldur’s Gate II: Enhanced Edition data with GemRB. Upstream marks this edition playable and completable with experimental polish. It uses a separate data layout from the original edition.

steps.title: Get the complete GemRB player
steps.instruction: On Windows x64 use the official SourceForge Windows ZIP and keep gemrb.exe with its companions. On Linux x86-64 use the official GemRB AppImage and provide the host libjack.so.0 library. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac use the intact Universal 2 GemRB application from Mac Source Ports.

steps.title: Prepare your own Enhanced Edition data
steps.instruction: Keep a complete working copy of your installed Baldur’s Gate II: Enhanced Edition. Point GamePath at the folder with chitin.key. Set GameType=bg2ee and configure GameLanguagePath for the language you installed, such as lang/en_US. The upstream player reads the prepared data.

steps.title: Use separate game data folders
steps.instruction: Set CachePath to an empty folder dedicated to this edition because GemRB clears it. SavePath is the parent that contains save/. Keep saves, settings and mods for the original edition in separate folders.

steps.title: Register the player and play
steps.instruction: Choose gemrb.exe on Windows, the executable AppImage on Linux, or Contents/MacOS/gemrb inside the intact Mac application. On Windows, choose the complete GemRB installation folder as the working folder. On Linux and Mac, choose the private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute configuration path as separate arguments. If the official Linux AppImage cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run before -c. Review and save the selection, then choose Play.

steps.title: Keep your working copy and saves
steps.instruction: The player owns the runtime, working data and profile. Back up the actual configuration, saves and mods before replacing the upstream player. Removing the registration preserves your external files.

warnings: Enhanced Edition support is experimental upstream. Keep the original installation, configuration and prior saves.

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use a complete installed original Baldur’s Gate II: Shadows of Amn working copy, with Throne of Bhaal only if you own and installed it. Enhanced Edition files and the trivial demo do not supply the original edition. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=bg2. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
steps.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/baldurs-gate-2, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate baldurs-gate-2.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. Back up the sandbox config and actual saves separately. To register the standalone x86-64 AppImage, allow the downloaded file to run and select the AppImage itself in Portcove. Choose your private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines, then review and save the selection. If the official AppImage reports that it cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run as the first separate argument. Keep -c and the config path on their own lines. Play starts the upstream player. For Flatpak, use the command above.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Mac build
steps.instruction: Use the Mac Source Ports Universal 2 DMG at https://github.com/MacSourcePorts/MSPBuildSystem/releases/tag/GemRB_0.9.5. Its v0.9.5 build uses macOS 10.15 or later on Intel and macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon. GemRB’s SourceForge release directory also offers separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Keep the bundle complete. Use this game’s own configuration and point GamePath to the prepared original game folder. Keep this title’s saves, config and working data together when replacing the bundle. To register the Mac Source Ports bundle, copy the complete gemrb.app from the DMG and open it normally once. Select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb in Portcove. Choose your private working folder, then enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines. Review the selection and choose Play.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

warnings: GemRB clears its cache directory. Use a dedicated private CachePath, separate from original files, saves and profile roots.

GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.

steps.title: Prepare this PS4 collection upstream first

listings.name: Bio Menace (ReflectionHLE)
listings.summary: Play Bio Menace through ReflectionHLE with the matching original DOS game files.

steps.title: Use the matching original DOS edition
steps.instruction: Use the complete matching original DOS episode data. Episode1 has separate shareware, registered, freeware and Gold Medallion revisions; episodes2/3 have their own registered/freeware revisions. Most use BMENACE1.EXE, BMENACE2.EXE or BMENACE3.EXE, while Gold Medallion uses BM1GM.EXE. The tagged source also recognizes the BioHazard1992 beta with BHAZARD1.EXE. Keep every companion for that exact revision. The launcher lists supported sets with exact names, sizes and CRCs. BioMenace Remastered is not established as interchangeable. Select legally obtained originals without moving them; a DOS executable is input, while reflectionhle.exe is the Windows player.

steps.title: Choose a fresh managed runtime or keep your external player
steps.instruction: For a fresh Portcove-managed runtime, use Install and then explicit Play. Keep the ordinary upstream launcher: choose this entry’s exact game/version and its complete matching original-data folder there. No automatic title dispatch or original authentication by Core is promised. The managed definition passes four separate literal arguments, -datadir, ., -cfgdir, ., with the actual player's parent folder as working directory (reflectionhle.exe on Windows, reflectionhle on Linux). On Mac, the official universal app runs with the same arguments from the folder containing reflectionhle.app. Upstream creates its version-specific writable directories after accepting the originals; no setup marker or helper is fabricated. For your separate existing external player, keep the original upstream route: Extract the official Windows 64-bit ZIP and keep reflectionhle.exe, SDL3.dll and libspeexdsp-1.dll together. Select reflectionhle.exe inside its wrapper folder and use that same folder as the working directory. Leave launch arguments empty to use the game/version picker. Complete original-file selection in the upstream launcher after explicit Play. Registration does not start it; Portcove discovery runs no original EXE, helper or game.

steps.title: Preserve the shared profile and each game version
steps.instruction: Windows normally stores ReflectionHLE settings and per-version writable data beneath %APPDATA%/reflectionhle. Preserve that whole profile, your original game folders and any custom data/config/mod locations with all copies closed before changing runtimes. Several game entries share settings; version-specific writable folders remain distinct. Changing a data/config argument redirects storage and does not migrate it. Retain the working runtime for existing saves; no cross-version or cross-engine save compatibility is established.

steps.title: Keep new private progress separate from old profiles
steps.instruction: The fresh managed runtime stores ReflectionHLE configuration, controller mappings, original-location references and per-version progress in the declared paths beside the player on Windows and Linux, or beside the app bundle on Mac. It imports no AppData, DOS or existing-player saves/configuration and adopts no populated external folder. Core manages that separate runtime and its declared data through the existing install/update, retained-runtime, backup/recovery and reviewed removal contracts. Keep originals and every external profile outside it unchanged. Existing user-selected registrations retain their creating runtime and old external ownership; they are not converted by this offer. Runtime rollback does not certify save compatibility. Preserve the creating runtime and actual progress before older-version use. Customized original/data/config argument overrides require separate upstream/external handling.

warnings: The ordinary upstream launcher still requires explicit matching game/version/original-folder selection. Fixed -gamever skips that picker and is not used.

listings.name: C-Dogs SDL
listings.summary: Play C-Dogs through your Linux distribution or a permitted existing desktop copy.
listings.download_block_reason: Portcove downloads are held for the bundled Wolfenstein 3D shareware data. Debian-derived packages supply the C-Dogs campaigns without that bundle.

steps.title: Install from your Linux distribution
steps.instruction: On Debian or Ubuntu, use your package manager to install cdogs-sdl. It brings in the matching C-Dogs data package and SDL libraries. Debian provides x86-64 and ARM64 packages. Start C-Dogs SDL normally from your applications menu or run cdogs-sdl. Your distribution handles software updates.

steps.title: Use a permitted Flatpak copy
steps.instruction: Flathub provides C-Dogs SDL for x86-64 and ARM64 as io.github.cxong.cdogs-sdl. Open it from your application menu. Flatpak owns its updates. The package includes the Wolfenstein 3D shareware files.

steps.title: Use an existing copy you have permission to play
steps.instruction: Keep the full copy, including bin, graphics, data, missions and libraries. On Windows, the publisher ZIP uses the 32-bit bin/cdogs-sdl.exe player. On Linux x86-64, the publisher tarball needs glibc 2.34 or later, SDL2 and SDL2_mixer. Open a terminal in bin and run ./cdogs-sdl so it finds the data in the parent directory.

steps.title: Register your existing Windows player
steps.instruction: In Portcove, choose bin/cdogs-sdl.exe from your permitted Windows copy and choose its bin folder as the working directory. Review the selected player and folder, then choose Play. Keep backups of the complete package and your actual C-Dogs profile. Removing this registration keeps those external files; you and upstream still own updates and backups.

warnings: The publisher Windows, Linux and Mac packages bundle Wolfenstein 3D shareware. The Debian-derived data package excludes that bundle. Use only originals and additional campaigns that you have permission to use.

references.title: Resume a backed-up campaign
references.instruction: With C-Dogs SDL closed, restore autosave.json to the profile folder for the copy you use. Leave the saved campaign available in the game. Open Start, choose Continue, and after selecting your players choose Continue with the saved mission number. Start campaign begins from the first mission.

references.title: Use a permitted Apple Silicon copy
references.instruction: The publisher disk image contains an Apple Silicon player targeting macOS 11 or later. Keep the complete cdogs-sdl folder and its SDL frameworks together. The executable is bin/cdogs-sdl. Intel Macs need a separately prepared source build.

references.title: Register an existing Linux portable copy
references.instruction: Use absolute paths to bin/cdogs-sdl and its bin folder. For c-dogs-sdl, run external select-preview with the executable path and --working-directory for the folder. Repeat both paths with external select and pass the preview SHA-256 to --expected-preview. Start the game with portcove exec c-dogs-sdl.

references.title: Keep your settings, campaigns and progress
references.instruction: Keep autosave.json, options.cnf and your custom campaigns. The standard Windows ZIP uses C-Dogs SDL under %APPDATA%. The Linux and Mac archives normally use ~/.config/cdogs-sdl. Flatpak uses ~/.var/app/io.github.cxong.cdogs-sdl/config/cdogs-sdl. If you set XDG_CONFIG_HOME, use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cdogs-sdl. steps.title: Complete the supported Xbox 360 preparation
steps.instruction: Use your own Modern Warfare 2 (2009) Xbox 360 USA/Europe disc version 1.0.557, not the PC release, remaster or another Call of Duty. Complete upstream installation and its required title update 6 before attachment. The native player hashes game/default.xex or game/default_mp.xex against the exact SHA-256 compiled into that build; title/version text alone does not replace this check. The selected release’s literal build-time hashes are not independently reproduced here. Do not bypass a mismatch or register an incomplete install that redirects to setup.

steps.title: Retain the complete matching Windows release
steps.instruction: Keep the full official v0.8.3 Windows package, both native players, mw2-launcher.exe, game/, renderer resources, shader caches, libraries and notices. The documented host requires 64-bit Windows, SSE4.2 and Vulkan 1.2. Use an independently permitted prepared player; project GPL-3.0-only applies to its own runtime/tools/patches, not Activision originals or original-derived generated C++. Separate title-update, Steam/network, custom-map and shader/component rights remain separate.

steps.title: Choose the upstream frontend or retain a direct player
steps.instruction: For normal setup/profile/mode controls, select mw2-launcher.exe in the complete existing package directory, use that directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready and use the upstream frontend. It supplies its own settings, preparation and selected SP/MP context. The existing direct choices remain valid: mw2-sp.exe for campaign/Special Ops or mw2-mp.exe for multiplayer, same directory and empty arguments, after upstream preparation. Portcove observes whichever program you selected, not detached successors; its activity may finish while a game or switched mode continues. Use actual game/upstream controls to quit.

steps.title: Preserve the complete save and settings unit
steps.instruction: Retain saves/, game/, .env, profile/settings files, logs, shader caches and all original/backup copies together. Saves are beside the executables, not inside read-only game/: the runtime represents content packages as directories, including saves/savegame.svg/savegame.svg, and this is not an Xbox STFS container or a promised console-save conversion. Preserve separate profiles and upstream shared SP/MP progress. Keep existing environment overrides; copying only an EXE or replacing .env with defaults can change behavior or separate progress.

steps.title: Keep maintenance and remaining acceptance upstream
steps.instruction: Use the upstream frontend for preparation, title updates, shader compilation, profile/network configuration, custom maps and runtime replacement. Close actual SP/MP games and helpers before making changes, even after Portcove’s selected-program activity ends. Re-select/review changed player bytes as needed. No credentials, network/server participation, full-game/controller/real-save acceptance, managed install/update/backup/rollback/migration or external-file deletion is supplied.

warnings: The native mw2-launcher.exe frontend preserves ordinary upstream setup and mode choices; existing direct mw2-sp.exe/mw2-mp.exe registrations remain available. Portcove tracks only the selected program. Preserve game/, saves/ and .env, close actual games/helpers before changes.

steps.instruction: The official Windows EXE is the upstream installer. Run setup deliberately, choose its data destination and complete the campaign/data layout, then register the installed OpenFodder.exe with its installation folder as working directory. Do not select the installer, bundled VC runtime setup or uninstaller as the player. The Campaigns data pack is required even when original retail data is present. Use the upstream campaign menu to select this game.

steps.title: Prepare the Linux source build
steps.instruction: Use upstream’s tagged Git checkout with its submodules, SDL2 and SDL2_mixer. Also install your distribution’s Vorbis development library, because linking the player can fail without it. Follow the supplied build instructions. The supplied Makefile puts the player in Run/OpenFodder. Set up the separate upstream campaign data pack and your own Cannon Fodder 2 inputs. Use your own Cannon Fodder 2 AmigaDOS files and an appropriate ADF extraction tool. The first game’s DOS data and SOS Unpacker do not supply this sequel. The engine first checks its working directory, then XDG_DATA_HOME/OpenFodder and each XDG_DATA_DIRS/OpenFodder, followed by ~/.local/share/OpenFodder and /usr/local/share/OpenFodder. Keep the actual data, Campaigns, Saves and configuration roots together. On Linux x86-64, select the native Run/OpenFodder executable from your completed upstream build and its Run folder as the working directory. Keep the upstream data pack and the full Scripts, Data and Campaigns layout there. Review your selection and save it, then choose Play and select this game’s campaign upstream. The separate Flatpak instructions use its own launcher.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

warnings: Preserve the actual chosen root, Saves, campaign/mod files and configuration with the player closed before upstream replacement.

steps.instruction: Use your own The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker GameCube USA GZLE01 revision 0 disc image in the supported ISO/GCM representation. steps.instruction: Retain the complete BlueWake folder, BlueWake.exe, game module, DLLs, resources and notices. The inspected selected release is v0.10.0; some README/build-page links still name v0.9.0, so do not combine their files or treat that older text as a second artifact selection. Windows 10/11 x64, Direct3D 12 and the release CPU requirements apply; the normal game module uses x86-64-v3 features including AVX2, FMA and BMI2. steps.instruction: Select BlueWake.exe in the complete BlueWake folder, use that containing folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. RVZ and other compressed formats require their separate upstream conversion/preparation; Portcove does not acquire originals, run a converter or supply keys. steps.title: Preserve the active memory card and configuration
steps.instruction: Keep the whole %APPDATA%/BlueWake folder, including GZLE01.card, sram.bin, settings.ini, logs, caches, texture/mod data and existing backups. An existing portable.txt beside BlueWake.exe instead selects its adjacent user folder; preserve that marker and populated folder. Do not create a new portable marker to add the reference or assume data moves automatically. Wind Waker Recomp 0.4 can share the same Windows data root; preserve a separate copy before switching upstream builds. Renaming a Dolphin .gci to .card is not a save conversion, and Dolphin save states are not game saves.

steps.title: Keep maintenance and observations separate
steps.instruction: Close the actual game and helpers before upstream replacement, rebuild, save import or recovery. Use upstream’s documented save tools on retained copies; Portcove does not migrate or repair cards. Review/select the executable after changes. listings.name: Warcraft III / OpenRealm
listings.summary: Try the upstream Warcraft III alpha with your own classic MPQ archives.

steps.title: Add your own Warcraft III files
steps.instruction: Copy war3.mpq and War3Local.mpq, plus War3x.mpq and War3xLocal.mpq for The Frozen Throne, and any loose Maps folder from your own classic Warcraft III installation into one data folder for OpenRealm. Keep your original installation separately.

steps.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
steps.instruction: Extract the upstream alpha and keep its libraries and share directory. Start openwarcraft3.exe on Windows or bin/openwarcraft3 on Linux and Intel Mac with -data followed by the quoted path to your Warcraft III files, then -tft for The Frozen Throne or -roc for Reign of Chaos. Linux needs SDL2, glibc 2.38 or later and your distribution’s OpenGL, VA-API, VDPAU and OpenCL loader libraries. The Intel Mac executable needs macOS 15 or later and SDL2 compatibility libraries under /usr/local/opt/sdl2-compat.

steps.title: Use the publisher’s x86-64 Flatpak
steps.instruction: On Linux you can install the packaged OpenRealm Flatpak with the publisher’s instructions and the Freedesktop 25.08 runtime. Open it and select your Warcraft III folder through the file chooser. Choose whether to add an optional Steam shortcut when asked.

warnings: This guide covers Warcraft III. The alpha package also includes development resources for other Blizzard games.

The Windows alpha includes SDL2, libepoxy and zlib libraries without their licence notices. The Windows and Linux alphas include the Epic Online Services SDK with the publisher’s online-service configuration for optional online play.

references.title: Keep the profile before replacing the player
references.instruction: Keep config.cfg, autoexec.cfg and saves from %APPDATA%/warcraft-3 on Windows or $XDG_DATA_HOME/warcraft-3 on Linux and Mac (usually ~/.local/share/warcraft-3). Keep any explicit -config location and the share/warcraft-3 fallback if used. Flatpak saves and its selected folder setting live in the Flatpak app profile.

references.title: Keep a separate copy's data setting in mind
references.instruction: OpenRealm saves the data folder it last used in config.cfg in the shared profile. After a run with -data data, a Windows copy started without -data looks for that relative data folder instead of searching for a Warcraft III installation; pass -data with your own folder for that copy. If the profile folder cannot be written, OpenRealm keeps config.cfg and saves under share/warcraft-3 beside the program instead.

listings.name: Crackdown (Crackdown Recompiled)
listings.summary: Add a prepared Crackdown copy from the Windows package or Linux AppImage, preserving its exact original-data requirements, upstream-owned updates and separate base/TU6 save generations.

steps.title: Finish exact original-disc setup upstream
steps.instruction: Use the complete Windows package or Linux AppImage and your own original, unupdated Crackdown Xbox360 retail disc: title4D5307DC, Default.xex14,270,464bytes, SHA-256 7AAA7A8920D1C3C737E58CF583DEBAFE6013BE0A96BEC3EC136E5DE7E3377E5A. Complete upstream ISO/extracted-folder validation and installation until Ready to play; game/ is adjacent and $SystemUpdate is unnecessary. No disc extraction, original acquisition, compilation or installer is invoked by this registration.

steps.title: Select the prepared native game entry
steps.instruction: Select crackdown.exe, its complete containing writable package directory and no arguments for ordinary Play. Keep the matching SDK/runtime/GPU DLLs, launcher resources, game data, configuration and notices together. The embedded launcher calls the native ReXApp game path in-process. Review and consent to the exact executable/CWD/arguments, then request Play separately. Windows10/11 x64, Direct3D12 and the applicable VC++ x64 runtime remain upstream prerequisites. On Linux, select the CrackdownRecompiled AppImage itself, with its folder as the working folder and no arguments; it needs no Windows runtime.

steps.title: Complete restarts and updates outside attachment
steps.instruction: Window size, monitor, VSync or adapter changes can make the next launcher Play start a successor window/process; upstream restart explicitly relaunches and quits the selected process. Finish settings/setup/restart and upstream updater work separately, close every actual game/helper/successor, then attach the resulting prepared player. Do not register trg-updater.exe or rely on automatic successor adoption/termination. Upstream/user is the sole runtime-replacement owner; Core offers no external update or rollback.

steps.title: Retain upstream save switching and cleanup boundaries
steps.instruction: Normal startup selects base or the separately installed TU6 guest and can recover an interrupted save switch, snapshot/swap live profile and campaign/header slots, then remove completed .switch-* staging under save-versions. These are upstream-owned writes, not Portcove migration or cross-version compatibility promises. TU6 and Four-Play/Free-for-All DLC are optional separately owned inputs with their own exact source checks; Free-for-All requires TU6. Do not remove/update content through this guide. The updater constructor may remove %TEMP%/trg-update-* directories older than24hours; ordinary exit may remove non-crash session logs unless detailed logging is enabled. Preserve recovery/diagnostic copies separately before startup/maintenance.

steps.title: Manage this copy yourself
steps.instruction: Removing registration preserves external files; no external backup/restore, deletion, save conversion or managed maintenance is offered.

Register devilutionx.exe inside its wrapper, using that same folder as working directory. Use the documented single argument --diablo to select this entry’s game even when both games’ files are present.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: The Windows data/profile location is normally %APPDATA%/diasurgical/devilution, with upstream portable/path overrides depending on the selected setup. Preserve the actual configuration, character saves and MPQ locations as well as the working copy, with all players closed before changing versions. Diablo and Hellfire modes have different original-data and save semantics. No automatic character conversion or cross-version save guarantee is supplied by registration.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions. The Linux reference below separates managed installation from upstream setup. Use the upstream application for the Mac and mobile instructions.

references.title: Choose a DevilutionX route on Linux
references.instruction: A new managed x86-64 installation uses the official tar.xz and the original-file chooser. Install your distribution’s SDL2 and SDL2_image libraries first. Existing managed AppImages keep their own runtime and profile. For a new managed copy, use a separate library and keep your old originals and saves. For a separate upstream-owned x86-64 copy, make the complete AppImage executable and keep it outside the Portcove library. Place your matching MPQ in $XDG_DATA_HOME/diasurgical/devilution (normally ~/.local/share/diasurgical/devilution). For shareware, use spawn.mpq and add the literal argument --spawn. Keep the default data path because an explicit --data-dir can hide the engine archive bundled in AppImage 1.5.5. Open the prepared copy upstream first. Then select the AppImage and its containing folder for external registration. Review the arguments and choose Play separately. For the x86-64 tar.xz, extract it into a new setup folder with Portcove Download or your archive tool, keep the complete package and start devilutionx.sh. On Linux ARM64 use the separate AArch64 tar.xz, install the needed SDL2 and SDL2_image libraries, and start devilutionx from the extracted folder. Use the game mode that matches your original data.

references.title: Prepare DevilutionX on Mac
references.instruction: Use the upstream macOS-universal DMG on Intel or Apple Silicon. Copy devilutionX.app out of the image and keep the complete bundle. Put the matching MPQs in ~/Library/Application Support/diasurgical/devilution unless you already use a custom directory. Select Diablo in the upstream game mode if Hellfire data are also present. On either desktop platform, preserve the actual config, character saves and original files, including overrides. The upstream license governs use of the external copy.

references.title: Prepare DevilutionX on Android, iPhone or iPad
references.instruction: On Android, install the upstream 1.5.5 APK or use Google Play. Use Import Data in the app to choose your files. Import your full Diablo DIABDAT.MPQ and select Diablo if Hellfire data are also present. The app copies the selected files into its external files directory, usually Android/data/org.diasurgical.devilutionx/files. Keep your originals and preserve that directory’s actual game data, saves and settings before replacing or removing the app. Use the same distribution channel for updates so the Android package signer remains compatible. On iPhone or iPad, use the official 1.5.5 IPA with your own sideloading and signing setup on iOS or iPadOS 13 or later. Open the app once, then close it. Use Finder or iTunes file sharing to copy your owned DIABDAT.MPQ to the app’s Documents folder. Select Diablo in the app. Keep the Documents folder, including .sv characters and stashes and the configuration, before changing the installation.

listings.name: ClayFighter63andOneThird: ClayFighter64 fusion edition (djultra64 ClayFighter64)
listings.summary: Windows x64 ClayFighter 64 fused product: 63⅓ gameplay with Sculptor's Cut donor characters, requiring both exact USA ROMs. Complete upstream asset installation first, then register clayfighter64.exe with its documented ROM and fused-asset arguments. Keep local/, probe-output/ and complete runtime dependencies. The title announcement’s source is unknown; use a complete copy you already have.
listings.download_block_reason: Portcove downloads are paused because the package’s in-game title announcement comes from an audio file of unknown origin, possibly another ClayFighter game. They can resume when upstream identifies that audio’s source or publishes a package without it.

steps.title: Supply both exact owned games
steps.instruction: This combines ClayFighter63⅓ gameplay with Sculptor's Cut donor characters; it does not recreate all of Sculptor's Cut. Supply your own ClayFighter63⅓ USA and ClayFighter:Sculptor's Cut USA ROMs. After normalization to big-endian z64, their SHA256 values must be 357f26c6cd72559c5c05e8c2df46369624630dbcb1c02b3b6f3338f6ac79af07 and 9ccebc317b7ee892be3bdc0d1c8ae46687995908ed51ebd58d6855e5e25abd7f, respectively. Keep both originals separately. Other regions, revisions and modified ROMs are unsupported. Upstream preparation handles supported byte orders or a single-ROM ZIP.

steps.title: Complete upstream asset installation
steps.instruction: Use a complete v2.1.1 Windows x86-64 copy you already have. The GPL licence for authored port code does not cover packaged branding, depicted original characters or the title announcement, whose source is unknown. On Windows 10/11 x64 with an SSSE3/SSE4.1 CPU and current Vulkan drivers, run Install Assets.vbs outside Portcove and finish asset installation. The included Python runtime checks both inputs and creates local imported files. Keep all supplied DLLs, configuration, notices and assets together.

steps.title: Select the prepared native player
steps.instruction: After successful installation, select clayfighter64.exe in the complete portable package root, set that root as working directory and use literal arguments --rom probe-output/base.z64 --sc-assets local/sc_roster/asset-image-roster.z64. These are the same native arguments used by the upstream Play wrapper. Do not select VBS/CMD/Python installers or unfinished data. The native player owns the game window and normal game loop. Saving launch details and requesting Play require separate consent.

steps.title: Keep portable custom profiles inside the game
steps.instruction: Display, native game options, P1/P2 controls and training settings live in local/settings/ by default; graphics caches live under local/cache/. The executable locates its installation from its own directory/config and changes CWD to it. Optional --data-dir or --user-data selects a profile only inside that installation; outside paths and escaping symlinks are rejected. --controls imports a profile but subsequent edits save inside the installation. Preserve every selected in-root profile, temporary/recovery copies and any custom source controls before maintenance.

warnings: Portcove downloads are paused because the title announcement audio is of unknown origin. You need your own original game files.
You can add a prepared complete copy you already have; extraction, updates and recovery remain upstream-owned.
Before first prepared startup, moves or updates, close the game and keep a separate complete recovery copy of local/, probe-output/, config and all original ROMs.

references.title: Preserve imported files and settings
references.instruction: Before first prepared startup, moves or updates, close the game and keep a separate complete recovery copy of local/, probe-output/, config and all original ROMs. Imported files include probe-output/base.z64, local/sc_roster/asset-image-roster.z64, local/sc_bios/bios.bin and local/import-manifest.json. Upstream installation replaces its generated outputs; reinstallation requires both originals. Keep current player settings separate from an older runtime backup.

references.title: Keep maintenance upstream-owned
references.instruction: The player and upstream own asset extraction, runtime replacement, settings and recovery. Portcove registers the explicitly selected prepared native copy; it does not acquire the originals, run extraction, update or delete external data. Finish upstream maintenance outside a tracked session, retain a complete previous runtime and current player data, then revalidate the selected executable. Do not infer compatibility between fused data, other editions or different builds.

references.title: Respect component and edition boundaries
references.instruction: Retain the GPL authored-code licence and individual SDK/RT64/SDL/Python/Microsoft notices. NOTICE explicitly excludes the branding and supplied replacement announcement from the code licence; obtaining another full package needs an applicable independent grant for those components. The optional title announcement falls back to the original ROM audio when absent, but this guide does not prescribe modifying a package or bypassing its grants. Both-ROM fusion identity and upstream claims do not establish full gameplay or save compatibility.

Before first Play on Windows, preserve both the existing Documents/My Games/dhewm3 profile and its creating runtime as well as any dude profile. If the dude profile is missing, this upstream Windows build silently copies the existing dhewm3 tree into it. A private original/runtime copy does not isolate that profile behavior. Decide whether to allow this before choosing Play.

Review its source and licence before approving it. Supply the mod data separately. Set com_allowModDownload 0 in DUDE to disable mod-library downloads. Optional graphics packs are separate. Check the upstream renderer and hardware requirements for your chosen mode; dhewm3 test results do not apply to this fork. steps.title: Prepare your original game
steps.instruction: Before Play, copy base/pak000.pk4 through base/pak008.pk4 from your own classic Doom 3 installation patched to 1.3.1 into base beside dude.exe on Windows or dude on Linux. Also copy your own classic Resurrection of Evil d3xp/pak000.pk4 and d3xp/pak001.pk4 into d3xp; the base game is required and the maintained arguments select the expansion. Keep the originals separately. BFG Edition is a different product. Portcove does not verify original-game identity. Keep the complete official platform package and all its own DLLs and resources together; do not overwrite them with old engine files. Optional graphics packs and custom mods stay upstream-owned. Use custom mods in a separate external copy outside the managed library. Check upstream renderer and hardware requirements for your selected mode; this fork does not inherit dhewm3 qualification.

steps.title: Review first-launch profile copying
steps.instruction: Windows normally stores saves and settings under the actual Documents/My Games/dude profile, with base/d3xp scopes. Explicit fs_savepath or mod paths can redirect writes. Preserve the actual profile, originals and creating runtime. Before first Play on Windows, preserve both the existing Documents/My Games/dhewm3 profile and its creating runtime as well as any dude profile. If the dude profile is missing, this upstream Windows build silently copies the existing dhewm3 tree into it. A private original/runtime copy does not isolate that profile behavior. The game copies that profile without moving the original. Portcove does not manage the copied profile, and save compatibility has not been confirmed. Decide whether to allow this before choosing Play.

steps.title: Keep an existing prepared copy
steps.instruction: Keep the complete official package and its libraries and resources together. Register dude.exe on Windows or dude on Linux in its containing runtime folder. Point to the folder containing base and d3xp with three separate argument lines: +set, fs_basepath, then the absolute data-root path. Add three more literal lines: +set, fs_game, d3xp. DUDE can offer to download or replace a mod code library. Review its source and licence before approving it. Supply the mod data separately. Set com_allowModDownload 0 in DUDE to disable mod-library downloads. Optional graphics packs are separate. Check the upstream renderer and hardware requirements for your chosen mode; dhewm3 test results do not apply to this fork. This is an external registration: you and upstream own its runtime replacement and all files. Removing its registration preserves those files. It does not migrate or adopt the copy into a managed installation.

warnings: First Play can copy an existing dhewm3 profile into a missing dude profile. Preserve both and decide before continuing.

references.title: Choose your Linux setup
references.instruction: Choose the DUDE x86-64 Doom 3 game tarball. The separately named dude-q4 package is a Quake 4 add-on. Extract the complete folder and keep its game libraries and bundled Vulkan loader. The reviewed executable needs glibc 2.34, SDL2, OpenAL and the OpenSSL variant of libcurl. Place your classic Doom 3 v1.3.1 base/pak000.pk4 through base/pak008.pk4 and Resurrection of Evil d3xp/pak000.pk4 and d3xp/pak001.pk4 in matching folders. Start ./dude with +set fs_game d3xp from the prepared directory. Preserve ~/.config/dude and ~/.local/share/dude or their XDG equivalents, plus any custom paths. DUDE can copy the legacy dhewm3 config on first run. Preserve both config trees before opening DUDE. The managed Linux x86-64 copy reads your PK4s from its own runtime and starts with its packaged modules. Use a separate upstream copy for custom paths, native mods or a custom library search path. If a managed first launch would copy a legacy profile, complete that setup in an upstream copy first.

listings.name: Doom / DOOM Retro
listings.summary: Play Doom or Freedoom with DOOM Retro’s lighting, display and gameplay options.

steps.title: Choose your game data
steps.instruction: Use the IWAD from your own Doom installation or a freely available Freedoom IWAD. Pass -iwad followed by the quoted path if you start the engine from a terminal. Keep doomretro.wad in the engine resources directory.

steps.title: Start DOOM Retro on Windows
steps.instruction: Extract the complete official x64 ZIP. Start doomretro.exe from that directory and choose your game data. Keep the support files with the executable. In the game console, discordpresence off disables the Windows Discord Rich Presence feature.

steps.title: Build DOOM Retro on Linux
steps.instruction: Use tagged upstream source, CMake and the SDL2 and SDL2_mixer development packages. Install the result into a local prefix so bin/doomretro and share/doomretro stay together.

steps.title: Find the Mac source build
steps.instruction: The upstream source includes a macOS build target. The v6.3 release supplies no Mac binary. Intel and Apple Silicon builds and runtime behavior still need verification.

warnings: The upstream package or your external build owns runtime updates. Keep your game data separate and preserve the active profile before replacing the player.

references.title: Keep your actual configuration and saves
references.instruction: The Windows ZIP stores settings and saves beside the executable. An installed Linux build writes to ~/.config/doomretro, with saves grouped by IWAD under savegames. If your Linux home lacks ~/.config, create it before the first run so the player can make its profile. A portable build can write beside the executable.

listings.name: Doom / DSDA-Doom

steps.title: Choose your game data
steps.instruction: Use the IWAD from your own Doom installation or a freely available Freedoom IWAD. Pass -iwad followed by the path to that file. Keep the supplied dsda-doom.wad with the engine. steps.title: Start DSDA-Doom on Windows
steps.instruction: Extract the complete publisher x64 ZIP. From that directory, run dsda-doom.exe with your IWAD.

steps.title: Start DSDA-Doom on Linux
steps.instruction: Use your distribution’s dsda-doom package if available. If you already have the publisher’s x86-64 AppImage, make it executable and run it with your IWAD. Without FUSE, extract it with --appimage-extract and run AppRun from the complete extracted directory. Install your distribution’s JACK client library if the player reports libjack.so.0 missing.

steps.title: Start DSDA-Doom on a Mac
steps.instruction: The publisher’s v0.30.1 universal ZIP has a Terminal executable for Intel and Apple Silicon. Both slices require macOS 26 or later. warnings: The package manager or your external installation owns updates. The player owns its save and settings files.

references.title: Keep the profile and matching runtime
references.instruction: On Linux preserve $XDG_DATA_HOME/dsda-doom, normally ~/.local/share/dsda-doom. It holds dsda-doom.cfg and per-IWAD saves and statistics in dsda_doom_data. Keep the engine version, IWAD and any add-ons used by a save or demo when changing packages.

listings.name: Doom II (Crispy Doom family)

steps.title: Supply the matching original game files
steps.instruction: Supply DOOM2.WAD from your original PC Doom II copy; the separate French edition uses DOOM2F.WAD. Doom shareware does not provide Doom II. Keep your originals and edition identity; renaming another game’s WAD does not convert it. Originals are not included or authenticated by Portcove. Use a recognized upstream installation, or deliberately copy matching files into the originals subfolder (named exactly originals) of this entry’s fresh private data folder; keep your original copies.

steps.title: Use the upstream setup and launch controls
steps.instruction: Play opens crispy-doom-setup.exe. Configure controls and use F2 Warp for single-player launch; choose the matching detected IWAD there. The main-menu launch command forwards its existing arguments. The PWAD/mod browser is not an original-IWAD browser. Keep different title entries separate. Do not switch this entry’s original edition in place: its retained runtime versions share data. Use a separate Portcove library or independently owned upstream copy for another source variant. No automatic switching or cross-variant save compatibility is established. An upstream setup exit does not establish that the game loaded or ran successfully.

steps.title: Keep the declared private data scope
steps.instruction: Portcove retains originals deliberately copied under originals, this entry’s default configuration, saves under saves, known default save locations, numbered screenshots and declared recording files. Put custom recordings under demos or use a demo-prefixed .lmp filename. Upstream may read and write its music-pack profile on Play. Music packs and custom paths outside this installation remain external and outside Portcove backups. Extra files written inside the installation outside its declared folders are outside this offered scope and can block maintenance. Keep the creating runtime, original files and actual data before changing a source variant or using an older runtime.

steps.title: Keep updates in one place
steps.instruction: Portcove manages this new official game installation and the data listed for it. It does not import an existing project profile or convert a separately registered game. Existing registered copies keep their external files and update tools. Back up those external profiles and original files separately. Automated fixture checks and reaching a setup menu do not establish original-file or gameplay compatibility.

warnings: Play opens the project’s setup and launch controls. Supply your own matching original game files that you are permitted to use.
Portcove backups exclude external music packs, custom paths and data belonging to separately registered games.

references.title: Install the native package on Linux or Mac
references.instruction: On Debian, install the crispy-doom package through the package manager. On Mac, use the upstream-documented MacPorts port or a supported Homebrew formula. Start crispy-doom with -iwad followed by the quoted path to your own DOOM2.WAD from Doom II or DOOM2F.WAD from the French edition. Use the external package manager for replacement.

references.title: Keep the existing Crispy profile
references.instruction: Preserve the actual Crispy config, saves, demos and original IWADs. Linux normally uses ~/.local/share/crispy-doom or XDG_DATA_HOME/crispy-doom. Mac normally uses ~/Library/Application Support/crispy-doom. Keep any custom locations and the creating runtime before switching package versions. The external profile can be shared across games.

steps.title: Prepare a separate Cave Story folder
steps.instruction: Keep your current game and store installation. For the original freeware edition, put the official Windows or Linux player beside a copy of your Doukutsu.exe and data folder. Flathub provides io.github.doukutsu_rs.doukutsu-rs for x86-64 and ARM64. Place your permitted prepared data folder under ~/.var/app/io.github.doukutsu_rs.doukutsu-rs/data/doukutsu-rs for the Flatpak. Open and update that copy through Flatpak.

steps.title: Use the Intel or Apple Silicon Mac app
steps.instruction: Choose the official archive for your Mac’s processor and keep the full doukutsu-rs.app. Follow the upstream Mac guide to put your prepared data folder in Contents/Resources before opening the app. Back up the old app, data and profile before replacing it.

steps.title: Set up the upstream Android app
steps.instruction: Install the official universal Android APK. Use Android Files to open the doukutsu-rs game-data location, then copy your permitted prepared Cave Story data folder there. Keep a separate copy of your game data and the app’s saved progress. Install newer releases through the same upstream channel.

warnings: The 2026 Steam remaster is not established by this guide, and remastered saves are incompatible with original-version saves.

Its Advanced menu can open the user-data folder; keep a separate backup of it, including settings.json and saves, before changing versions or editions. Portcove does not back up, roll back or delete this external game/data tree.

listings.name: Dragon's Crown Pro (PS4) (Dragon's Crown Pro PC)
listings.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared Dragon’s Crown Pro Windows installation in its same-process mode. This title-specific PS4 x86-64 compatibility layer owns upstream PKG preparation; overlay handoff, online services and updates retain separate boundaries.

steps.title: Prepare an exact permitted PS4 build upstream
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. Version 0.9.1 supports your own decrypted Dragon’s Crown Pro PS4 package: USA CUSA10454 base 1.00 or base plus 1.01; Japan CUSA07001 base 1.00 or base plus 1.02/1.03; Asia/Hong Kong CUSA10209 base 1.00 or base plus 1.02. Updates require the matching base. Follow the pinned upstream table for title, content, version and each build’s eboot.bin SHA256; a title match alone is insufficient. Encrypted console packages and other code versions are refused. Finish upstream import and preparation before adding the game to Portcove. Keep your originals and check the testing limits for your build. Portcove does not obtain or run packages, keys or setup helpers for you.

steps.title: Keep the complete title-specific Windows runtime
steps.instruction: Keep the complete DragonsCrownProPC-v0.9.1-windows-x64.zip contents together, including dragons_crown_pro.exe, trg-updater.exe, matching DLLs, resources, licences and prepared game/image data. This Windows player runs the game’s x86-64 code using a title-specific PS4 compatibility layer and Vulkan translation. It does not provide general PS4 support. Select dragons_crown_pro.exe; the updater, internal boot image, DLLs and original eboot.bin are not game players.

steps.title: Select the same-process prepared play mode
steps.instruction: In the game’s settings, turn Allow overlay programs Off and finish preparation. Select dragons_crown_pro.exe, use the complete extracted package folder as the working directory and enter --dcp-skip-launcher as the single argument. Review those launch details and consent, then choose Play separately. With overlays Off, the game continues in the selected process. Enabling overlays starts another process and closes the selected one, which Portcove does not track. Portcove does not lock this setting; confirm it remains Off before playing. This process behavior has not been tested through Portcove.

steps.title: Preserve all builds and the actual user tree
steps.instruction: Keep the complete game/prepared/<build> and game/image/<build> trees, original PKGs, user/dcp.ini, user/savedata, trophy data, caches and numbered logs. Retain user/keys.json if you previously configured a Trophy Key; this guide neither reads nor obtains it. Existing explicit app0/image, --user, --logs or --log selections can point elsewhere; preserve every effective root without creating overrides here. Selecting another build does not prove save compatibility or migrate data. No import, backup, rollback, credential or deletion operation is performed by this attachment.

steps.title: Complete online, overlay and update work upstream
steps.instruction: Keep online account/Friend Code, service/usage-data choices and overlay/injection tools under explicit upstream/user control; this guide does not create an account, request credentials or qualify network play. Complete updater/helper, install/reinstall, build switching, overlay handoff and runtime replacement outside an attached session. Close actual players/helpers/successors, preserve independent recovery copies and review/relink changed bytes. Upstream’s reinstall/recovery behavior is not a Portcove rollback promise. Quit normally; forced termination is not a save-flush or successor-quiescence guarantee.

steps.title: Keep licences and platform limits in view
steps.instruction: Keep the GPL2-or-later licence for original project code, TRG Launcher MIT licence and all component, NVIDIA and font notices. They do not grant original-game, console or package rights. Check the documented untested features for non-USA builds. Linux, AppImage, Steam Deck and upstream online results do not establish Windows compatibility. Portcove has not confirmed gameplay, online play, save/reload or installed behavior. Removing the registration leaves all external files in place; Portcove does not install, update, roll back, back up or delete this external copy.

warnings: Keep Allow overlay programs Off for the same-process route; enabling it starts a successor outside the tracked player. Preserve all prepared builds, saves and existing key files.

steps.title: Use the complete Windows desktop distribution
steps.instruction: Keep the full rotp-windows-directory.zip v0.21.2 layout. The ordinary entry is the root Relic of the Past.exe alongside Update.exe and current/. The current directory contains replaceable application files; do not select Update.exe as the game or move a single executable away from its companions. Project MIT, zelda3 and other component/font/MSU terms remain separate from original-game rights.

steps.title: Import your own supported game data upstream
steps.instruction: In the application use the title-bar Data → ROMs → Import ROM route with your own US NTSC A Link to the Past SNES .sfc/.smc, then create a profile and select its ROM/language. EU and Japanese originals are separate language-import sources, not the gameplay base. Upstream copies imported originals and extracts zelda3_assets.dat into its data directory. The selected base-ROM specification accepts unknown hashes, so import acceptance alone is not proof of an exact original-file fingerprint. Portcove supplies no ROM, external ROM URL, asset extraction or source validation.

steps.title: Add the ordinary application entry
steps.instruction: Select the root Relic of the Past.exe, set the complete extracted distribution root as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready and use the existing upstream profile. Keep the root launcher and current application together. It can hand off to another process: Portcove observes the selected program only, so a finished activity does not prove the game or Electron helpers have closed.

steps.title: Preserve the actual data root and every profile
steps.instruction: The normal Windows data folder is %APPDATA%/relic-of-the-past. Existing portable mode uses data/ beside Update.exe, outside current/; preserve that existing choice and all its contents. Keep profiles/<profile>/saves with all save kinds, settings/controls, imported ROMs, extracted assets, languages, MSU packs and related user files. Do not create an empty data folder just to register the player: that changes the active data root and can hide existing profiles. Do not place user data in current/, which upstream replaces during updates, or assume switching portable mode migrates anything.

steps.title: Leave updates, profile changes and recovery upstream
steps.instruction: Quit the actual game and all helpers before upstream update, replacement or recovery, even after Portcove’s activity ends. Use upstream’s own profile and data tools deliberately; profile deletion is destructive and is not part of adding or removing the library reference. Keep prior complete application/data copies and review the selected entry after changes. Portcove removes only its reference and offers no managed installation/update, ROM or save conversion, backup, rollback, full-session tracking or Supported qualification. No personal gameplay, controller or real-save acceptance is claimed.

listings.name: Forza Horizon (Forza Horizon 1: ReImagined)
listings.summary: An independent Forza Horizon 1: ReImagined implementation with project-reported racing, free roam and co-op. The Windows installer or Linux Flatpak/tar.gz launcher downloads tools and builds locally from your own 2012 Xbox 360 disc, GOD or extracted game. TU4 is optional for Rally and 1000 Club. The launcher manages setup and updates. macOS is a source experiment without a launcher download: opening drives render, but full races, save/reload and physical controllers remain unconfirmed. Exact PC package architecture, original revision/hashes and further BIOS/firmware requirements are unconfirmed. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

steps.title: Prepare your own Xbox 360 original upstream
steps.instruction: Use the official v0.2.4 Windows setup and complete its supported original-file selection, game-code build and graphics/settings preparation. Inputs are your own Forza Horizon Xbox 360 disc image, Games on Demand package or complete extracted folder, title ID 4D5309C9. The selected base manifest identifies XEX module hash D48ABF1704CE5C4A; optional Title Update 4 uses version 0.0.4.12/module hash 336A44DC03EC8782. These module identifiers are not whole-disc cryptographic hashes. Retain owned update/DLC inputs separately.

steps.title: Select the installed waiting launcher
steps.instruction: After setup succeeds, select the actual installed forza-launcher.exe, use its complete installed directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Keep its bundled files intact. Review the selected program, working folder and arguments and choose Play when ready, then use its ordinary Play. The selected GUI creates a game Session, polls its child until exit and waits for that child when closing. Keep the launcher open while the game runs, then close both normally. Do not select ForzaHorizon1-ReImagined-Setup-0.2.4.exe, an update helper, bare forza.exe, server or command-line build/extract mode.

steps.title: Keep the exact launch context
steps.instruction: The launcher passes the actual game-data root and selected user/cache/profile paths, writes the game configuration and supplies graphics/session environment. It also handles save preparation and post-session processing. Directly starting forza.exe with default paths would instead risk selecting Documents/forza and omit that context. Keep the already selected local or Xenia-derived profile, original/base or TU4 build, DLC and graphics configuration; do not switch them merely to attach the player. Optional online, public sharing, haptics, VR, account or token operations remain upstream/user choices and are not performed here.

steps.title: Preserve both settings and game-data roots
steps.instruction: Keep %APPDATA%/ForzaReImagined with launcher.json, settings/logs and private profile information, plus the actual game-data root. New Windows data normally uses %LOCALAPPDATA%/ForzaReImagined; an existing Documents/forza install can remain active, and configured data roots or a failed legacy carry can retain another actual root. Preserve originals, saves, profile/Xenia copies, DLC, photos, backups, cache and both historical/active roots. Upstream carry operations copy without deleting the source and do not justify merging or deleting existing profiles. No data relocation, save editing, migration, restore or deletion is performed here.

steps.title: Keep upstream ownership and qualification limits
steps.instruction: The upstream launcher owns compiler/source staging, preparation, self-update and failed-build recovery. Retain project GPLv3-or-later, ReIGlue/ReXGlue, compiler, bundled libraries and component notices; they do not license the original game, DLC, mods or shared content. Finish updates outside a game session, preserve recovery and review/relink changed bytes. The observed setup EXE header is the installer, not proof of the compiled game’s architecture or behavior. No native/installed, online/multiplayer, full campaign, real-save restore, Supported or managed lifecycle acceptance is asserted.

warnings: Select the installed forza-launcher.exe after upstream preparation. Its waiting session preserves the actual data/profile context; keep both launcher settings and all active/historical game roots.

listings.name: DoDonPachi SaiDaiOuJou / SDOJ-Recomp (eandis)
listings.summary: Play the DoDonPachi SaiDaiOuJou recompilation with your own Xbox 360 disc or Games-on-Demand copy and its Title Update 1 data.

steps.title: Add your own disc or Games-on-Demand files
steps.instruction: Before the first start, put exactly one supported ISO of your own Xbox 360 disc or converted Games-on-Demand copy beside the game program, with its matching Title Update 1 data. Disc default.xex SHA-256 is 709EB9FD2E4446E5754461616693B3BBB8B78FEF5AA613FFCDE6D643DA0133F5 and its TU1 file is 598,016 bytes with SHA-256 0A893048C761BA6CF8ED14637F326726BC616B5183CA1EE52DE02FC12B46B215. The Games-on-Demand default.xex is 41AB091576813248712A387B273398E5D700454505E83F6F1FEB7DE2C1027707 and needs CA022100.binp, CA022110.binp and default.xexp instead. On first start the game checks them, extracts game_data and applies the update; keep your originals separately and delete the copies afterwards.

steps.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
steps.instruction: Keep the complete package for your system together, including its runtime libraries, extractor and notices; the standard and Vulkan ZIPs are separate packages. Start DoDonPachi SaiDaiOuJou.exe (DoDonPachi SaiDaiOuJou on Linux) from its own folder with no arguments. Settings marked as needing a restart apply the next time you start the game.

warnings: Disc and Games-on-Demand copies use different checks and are not interchangeable; do not mix their files. The game refuses incomplete or unsupported game_data rather than merging it. No gameplay, performance or save compatibility across versions is promised.

The package includes statically recompiled game code, icon art and an unlicensed project layer that the project license does not cover. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.

references.title: Keep the game folder's data
references.instruction: By default the game keeps saidaioujou_recomp_tu1.toml, game_data, user_data (saves, the shader cache and update-check notes) and logs beside the program. A game_data_root or other path setting in the toml moves that data elsewhere. In a copy you manage yourself, back these up before replacing the program. The game checks GitHub for new releases and can open the release page; it never downloads or installs them.
