listings.name: Wolfenstein 3D (ECWolf)
listings.summary: Play Wolfenstein 3D with ECWolf using your original game files or the public shareware. Set up an installation you maintain, then add it to Portcove.

steps.title: Prepare the Windows player and Wolfenstein game files
steps.instruction: Download the official Windows x64 ECWolf ZIP and extract the complete package. Keep ecwolf.exe, ecwolf.pk3 and the accompanying files together. For the public Wolfenstein 3D 1.4 shareware, extract wolf3d14.zip and copy its eight .WL1 files beside ecwolf.exe. Keep your original download separately. WOLF3D.EXE and CATALOG.EXE from the old DOS distribution are not the ECWolf player. The ecwolf.exe selection step below applies to Windows.

steps.title: Set up the Linux package
steps.instruction: Install the official matching Ubuntu amd64 package with your system package manager so its dependencies and system data are present. Put the complete matching .WL1 data set in ~/.config/ecwolf, or the ecwolf folder below your XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Preserve the filenames and their case. Select /usr/games/ecwolf and its containing folder in Portcove; enter --data and WL1 as two separate arguments. Review the details, add the game, then choose Play. Use the system package manager or upstream to update this installation.

steps.title: Add the Intel or Apple Silicon Mac player
steps.instruction: Copy the complete official ECWolf.app from the DMG into Applications and open it normally once. Copy all eight matching .WL1 shareware data files into ~/Library/Application Support/ECWolf, preserving their names and case. In Portcove, select /Applications/ECWolf.app/Contents/MacOS/ecwolf and its containing folder; enter --data and WL1 as separate arguments, review the details, then add the game and choose Play. Keep ecwolf.pk3 and the complete app together. The later ecwolf.exe choice applies to Windows; Mac uses the native file inside ECWolf.app.

steps.title: Select the prepared player
steps.instruction: Select ecwolf.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Enter these literal argument values in order, one array item per argument: ["--data","WL1"]. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

warnings: Keep your actual saves, settings, original game files, mods and their creating ECWolf version backed up with the game closed before changing versions. Save compatibility with another version or engine is not established.

references.title: Android and other processor builds
references.instruction: The official download page also offers Android APKs, Windows ARM64 and Linux ARM packages. Choose the matching upstream build and follow its setup notes. Upstream warns that Android support is buggy; check its system-version notes before installing. Android installation, updates and saved data stay with the app and the player. Portcove desktop registration does not manage these other host routes.

references.title: Registration ownership and removal
references.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

references.title: Player-data ownership
references.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: Windows Roaming AppData/ECWolf settings and Windows Saved Games/ECWolf progress, including upstream fallback locations; Linux XDG configuration/ecwolf and data/ecwolf/savegames folders; Mac ~/Library/Preferences/ecwolf.cfg, ~/Documents/ECWolf/Savegames, ~/Library/Application Support/ECWolf and upstream fallback locations; original game files, mods and any explicit --config or --savedir locations. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

listings.name: Chrono Trigger (Nintendo DS) — Egg of Time
listings.summary: Build a native Chrono Trigger player from your own Nintendo DS cartridge dump using Egg of Time.
listings.download_block_reason: Portcove downloads are paused while the first-start build tools and recovery are being reviewed. The guide covers a copy you already trust and are permitted to use.

steps.title: Choose your original Nintendo DS game
steps.instruction: Use an unmodified .nds dump from your own cartridge. The accepted SHA-1 values are USA (YQUE) 11f9e8204e484eab42181b210c9f214584be75bf, Europe (YQUP) a6c69d789a6f2e31b27fba950423bea3c2f30a37, and Japan (YQUJ) afc91a3f1f6c1bd02845b76416239e4dabfae19f.

steps.title: Start the Windows x64 package
steps.instruction: Use a trusted EggOfTime Windows x64 ZIP ending in -windows-x64.zip. Extract it into a writable folder and open Egg of Time.exe. The package includes the tools for the local first-start build.

steps.title: Start the Linux x64 package
steps.instruction: The current Linux x64 packages need glibc 2.35 or newer, Python 3 and libcurl. They include Zig for the first-start build. The file picker uses xdg-desktop-portal or zenity. Extract the -linux-x64.tar.gz package and start Egg of Time from its folder, or make the separate x86-64 AppImage executable and open it.

steps.title: Let Egg of Time build your game
steps.instruction: Choose the .nds file when asked and wait for the local build to finish. The launcher copies the original to rom/CT.nds. If the build fails, open game/build.log in the same data location.

warnings: Use these steps with a copy you already trust and are permitted to use. Follow your operating system’s security prompts.
Keep your ROM, extracted assets, generated game code and saves private. Close Egg of Time and wait for any build to finish before replacing the package or copying its data.
The upstream macOS runtime compiles from source. Upstream lists a full Mac game build as untested.

references.title: Find the data for your package
references.instruction: For the Windows ZIP and Linux tarball, data stays beside the player. For the AppImage, keep EggOfTime under XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share/EggOfTime by default. Back up rom/CT.sav, rom/CT.state, eggoftime.ini, controls.ini and your mods before an update or a ROM region change.

references.instruction: Use Building from source in the upstream guide. It lists CMake 3.25+, Ninja, a C11 compiler, Python with Capstone, SDL3, FFmpeg, system libcurl and ds-decomp 0.12.1. Follow the region-specific extraction and build instructions with your own original.

steps.instruction: After successful upstream preparation, select build-release/Einhander_Recompiled.exe, the completed executable’s parent directory as working directory and the supported --launcher literal argument. Keep its staged game.toml and matching resources in place. The root setup executable starts a replacement product and exits on Windows, so select the completed product instead. Keep Generate/Rebuild and SDK/toolchain changes as deliberate upstream maintenance outside the active attached session; an intentional rebuild can end or replace the process.

steps.title: Prepare the official Linux or Mac kit
steps.instruction: Extract the complete Linux x86-64, Intel Mac or Apple Silicon Mac ZIP for your host. The observed Linux setup player needs glibc 2.38 and libstdc++ providing GLIBCXX_3.4.29, plus the host OpenGL and zlib libraries libOpenGL.so.0 and libz.so.1. The Mac setup player has a macOS 11 minimum. Select the Apple Command Line Tools or Xcode toolchain for its Clang and SDK. Install upstream’s required Python 3 and use its Generate & rebuild wizard and supported toolchain. Supply your own USA SCUS-94243 CUE and all referenced BIN files. Use the title’s default generated OpenBIOS or a separately owned SCPH-1001 as upstream allows. Start the completed build-release/Einhander_Recompiled in its own folder after upstream setup. Keep it with its matching config, assets and the complete creating project.

steps.title: Review launch details, then choose Play
steps.instruction: Select the completed game executable, its working folder and supported launch arguments. Review those details and agree to use them, then choose Play separately. You manage setup, game replacement and recovery using the project’s tools. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, conversion, data migration or deletion for this external copy. Removing its registration leaves external files in place. Before changing versions, close the game and its companion programs and keep the working copy and its data. Review and select the changed executable before playing again.

warnings: Use only a copy and components you are permitted to use. Before changing versions, keep the complete working game, original files and every profile, mod, generated-code cache and custom data location. Another executable may use the same saved data.
This title enables its GCC overlay backend. Keep the creating toolchain, actual generated overlay data and compiler settings with the original project before updating.
The Linux and Mac kits perform local generation and use upstream setup and replacement. Package inspection does not qualify a generated native game, multiplayer or a save migration.

references.title: Preserve the whole creating project and effective player data
references.instruction: Keep both the complete source/setup kit and build-release product, every original and BIOS, generated code, toolchain resources, mods and all custom roots. settings.toml and input.ini are anchored beside the executable; game.toml/game_options.toml and their effective project root affect source and relative data paths. The packaged memcard_dir=saves can be overridden by settings or explicit card paths. Preserve actual memory cards, save states/options, keybinds, diagnostics, overlay code caches, backups and temporary files with their creating runtime. Do not relocate or rewrite paths from a developer example, copy another title’s source hashes, or assume cross-version state/save compatibility.

listings.name: FreeOrion
listings.summary: Explore the galaxy, develop colonies and lead a space empire in FreeOrion. Prepare the upstream client, then add it to Portcove.

steps.title: Install the stable client
steps.instruction: On 64-bit Windows, run the official setup program and follow its installer prompts. The 0.5.1.2 installer filename says Win32 and contains a 64-bit client. On Mac, choose the Intel or Apple Silicon disk image and copy the complete FreeOrion app into Applications. The current package needs macOS 10.15 or newer on Intel and macOS 11 or newer on Apple Silicon. For Intel or Apple Silicon Mac registration, keep its name FreeOrion.app and select /Applications/FreeOrion.app/Contents/MacOS/FreeOrion with its containing folder. Keep the whole bundle and leave ordinary launch arguments empty. Review the details, add the client and choose Play. The later FreeOrion.exe selection and executable-containing folder instructions apply only to Windows. On Mac or Ubuntu, use the program and working folder specified for that platform.

steps.title: Use your Linux package manager
steps.instruction: On Ubuntu x64, install matching freeorion and freeorion-data packages with all dependencies. In the reviewed 0.5.1.2-1 package, select the native /usr/lib/freeorion/freeorion and set /usr/share/games/freeorion as the working folder, with no arguments. Keep the sibling server/AI programs and package data/libraries installed. /usr/games/freeorion is a shell wrapper, not the native selection. Review the details, add the client and choose Play. Other distributions can use different paths; verify their complete native installation first. Flathub remains a separate option: install and run org.freeorion.FreeOrion through Flatpak, which owns its runtime and updates. Do not select Flatpak’s internal /app/bin path as a host-native program. Update through the same package manager.

steps.title: Keep your saves and settings
steps.instruction: Close FreeOrion and any separately hosted local servers before backing up. A local server and its AI can finish shutdown after the client closes; wait for their exit before copying or changing the installation or data. Copy the FreeOrion folder under %APPDATA% on Windows or ~/Library/Application Support on Mac. On Linux, keep the freeorion folders under ~/.config and ~/.local/share, using your configured XDG folders if they differ. For Flathub, keep ~/.var/app/org.freeorion.FreeOrion. Also keep any separate save directory you chose in the game.

steps.title: Select the prepared player
steps.instruction: Select FreeOrion.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

references.title: Client and server ownership
references.instruction: Portcove tracks the graphical client you select. FreeOrion starts its own server and AI processes for games; a local server you host can stay separate after the client closes. Portcove does not take ownership of those servers or certify that every companion has stopped. You and upstream own installation, updates, saves, settings, mods, backups and removal. Removing the registration preserves all external files. The current official release has no Android package or native Windows ARM64 build.

references.title: Registration ownership and removal
references.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

references.title: Player-data ownership
references.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: Windows %APPDATA%/FreeOrion saves, settings and mods; Linux XDG configuration and data/freeorion folders, or ~/.config/freeorion and ~/.local/share/freeorion; Mac ~/Library/Application Support/FreeOrion settings, saves and mods; every custom save or user-data location; separately running upstream servers and AI retain their own writes. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

steps.title: Use a completed Windows copy
steps.instruction: Use an independently permitted completed Windows copy. The inspected 1.7 ZIP (SHA-256 21e13616bbc0d62dcf1341be10d392694b1f6033965dc4c9ab15f13a8f028ac6) contains bigodao_1.7_win/bigodao_1.7_win.exe and tools/wl_sm3_dx_v12_patch.json beneath that folder. Keep both together in a writable folder. A separately completed source build instead uses wario_land_port.exe; this route does not supply missing generated game code or establish source-to-binary reproducibility.

steps.title: Keep exact original and patch inputs
steps.instruction: For upstream first-run preparation, supply your legally obtained Wario Land - Super Mario Land 3 (World) ROM (SHA-256 ac1682f17abcf590311a233289ee325214c2d71ab3a5aa175004002d85075e56) and independently permitted korxo DX v1.2 IPS patch (SHA-256 599d9f59090df3e1e77c1678e069290a2cd9ce59c71cf58d66c4dc3db8b7facd). Owning the game or the project code license does not grant acquisition or redistribution of the patch or optional music/art packs.

steps.title: Back up old and new storage before startup
steps.instruction: Before first startup or an update, close Bigodão and separately back up the complete old and new folders, saves/, legacy loose .sav/.rtc/.state files, wario.o2r and any .tmp recovery file, mods/, and the SDL preference directory for gbrecompiled/runtime (normally %APPDATA%/gbrecompiled/runtime/runtime_prefs.ini; local runtime_prefs.ini is a fallback). Startup copies eligible legacy loose saves into missing saves/ destinations and retains the old files; failure to create saves/ falls back to beside-executable storage.

steps.title: Let upstream prepare its private data package
steps.instruction: Complete the upstream ROM/IPS picker before registration. It patches a copy in memory and creates wario.o2r beside the executable, with a current-directory fallback for an existing package. An older texture recipe can request re-preparation; creation verifies a temporary package, then removes the prior package before renaming the replacement. Keep the separate pre-start backup and original inputs; cancelling that update can continue with the previously loaded old ROM.

steps.title: Link the ordinary native executable
steps.instruction: For the inspected 1.7 Windows package, add bigodao_1.7_win.exe through the existing-copy route, use the bigodao_1.7_win folder containing it as the working directory, and leave arguments empty. For a separately completed source build, select its wario_land_port.exe with that executable's parent folder and no arguments. The source runs its picker and normal game loop in one process; Portcove has not tested launch with this package. Do not select Android files, packaging tools, or a compiler helper.

steps.title: Keep replacement ownership upstream
steps.instruction: Quit the game completely before maintenance, relinking or removal. Upstream and the user own preparation, runtime replacement and updates; Portcove only links the selected executable and does not install, update, roll back, move or delete this external copy or its player data.

warnings: The selected runtime uses wario_land_sm3_dx_v12 for saves; upstream owns save-slot replacement/deletion and all compatibility decisions. Save or mod compatibility across other ports, builds or editions is not established.

references.title: Preserve saves, preferences and mods
references.instruction: Preserve the complete saves/ folder, legacy save copies, preferences, mods/ including 3d_marcas.txt, captures and custom packs. The selected runtime uses wario_land_sm3_dx_v12 for saves; upstream owns save-slot replacement/deletion and all compatibility decisions. Save or mod compatibility across other ports, builds or editions is not established.

references.title: Use the Android Bigodao package
references.instruction: The project’s 1.8.0 release publishes Bigodao-1.8-release.apk for ARM64. Use Android’s file picker to give the app your own unmodified Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3 (World) ROM. The APK includes the patch manifest. On Android, Back opens the project menu so you can reach controls and settings again.

listings.name: Crash Team Racing: Nitro-Fueled (CTR-NitroFueled-PC)
listings.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared GetLostIn CTR Nitro-Fueled Windows installation. Its native settings launcher waits for the game runner; upstream owns PS4-data preparation, runtime replacement and the external save/cache roots.

steps.title: Prepare the correct PS4 game and update upstream
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. The 0.4 Windows route documents your own CTR Nitro-Fueled PS4 CUSA13795 or CUSA14876 base game and matching 1.21 update; both documented 1.21 firmware builds are accepted by upstream. Follow its first setup outside Portcove and keep independent originals before creating its merged game folder. Its preparation uses hard links where possible: a merged tree is not an independent backup of original file contents. No original, DLC, extractor, Python helper or game is obtained or executed here.

steps.title: Keep the complete selected Windows implementation
steps.instruction: The inspected CTR-NitroFueled-PC-portable-windows.zip contains CTR-NitroFueled-PC-portable/CTR-NitroFueled-PC.exe, bin/sacredfire.exe, bundled python, scripts, DLLs and resources. The ordinary frontend is an AMD64 native Windows launcher, not the older Python launcher or a standalone game exe. Keep the whole matching package. This is the existing GetLostIn Windows adaptation of SacredFire with its own maintained Windows layer/launcher and credited upstream fixes; a common game title does not merge it with the separate online fork or qualify the parent’s Linux route.

steps.title: Select and retain the normal launcher session
steps.instruction: After upstream setup, select CTR-NitroFueled-PC.exe, use its complete extracted portable package directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately. This opens the upstream launcher; request its Play only when ready. The native frontend waits for its Python runner, which waits for sacredfire.exe. The runner loops over its own Apply and restart exit code, retaining the ordinary waiting chain. Quit the actual game before closing the frontend; its Stop game and quit action forcibly terminates the job and is not a save-flush guarantee. Portcove has not tested this launch-and-quit sequence.

steps.title: Preserve the actual data and hard-link sources
steps.instruction: Keep the whole package user tree with savedata, cache and trophies, the separate backups and DLC directories, launcher.ini, bbport.ini, patches.json, logs and the full prepared game view. Keep the original base/update/DLC sources independently too. The runner normally uses user for saves/cache, while an established BB_USER_DIR or other data/mod/config override can select additional external roots; preserve every effective location. Do not edit a hard-linked merged source as though it were an isolated disposable copy. This guide performs no save import, migration, backup or deletion.

steps.title: Leave replacement and recovery with upstream
steps.instruction: Complete upstream updates, first preparation, repairs and source-root changes outside an attached session. Close all actual players/helpers before replacing files, keep independent recovery copies, then review/relink changed executable bytes. Normal waiting/restart source paths do not establish observed forced-stop cleanup or save consistency. Portcove does not own the mutable upstream runtime, merged originals, backups or external player data. Removing registration preserves all external files.

steps.title: Retain permission and platform limits
steps.instruction: Preserve GPL 2-or-later and all packaged third-party/NVIDIA/font notices; these grants do not grant original-game or DLC rights. Upstream playable race/audio/controller/save reports remain upstream claims; shader stalls and experimental upscaling/frame-generation/ultrawide limits remain. This guide does not establish Portcove gameplay, multiplayer, save/reload, installed-app or Supported acceptance. No managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal is offered.

warnings: Keep independent original base/update copies: upstream’s merged game view can use hard links. Quit the game normally before closing its native launcher.

listings.summary: Windows x64 GT4Recomp official launcher for an upstream-prepared Gran Turismo 4 USA v2.00 installation. steps.title: Use the complete installation and your own disc
steps.instruction: Use the complete GT4Recomp v1.2.5 Windows installation and your own Gran Turismo 4 USA v2.00 SCUS-97328 plain ISO. steps.title: Finish official upstream setup
steps.instruction: Complete the official installer and launcher disc setup outside Portcove. The launcher copies the ISO, verifies preparation, installs the renderer and checks CPU/Vulkan requirements. Use supported Windows x64, SSE4.1 CPU, Vulkan 1.2 and WebView2; retain the complete matching installation and DLLs. This route uses the official launcher, not the internal gt4vulkan.exe with a guessed environment or another version's renderer.

steps.title: Back up all current and legacy roots before first startup
steps.instruction: Close the game and launcher; keep a separate complete prior installation and current <install>/data, %APPDATA%/GT4Recomp, %LOCALAPPDATA%/GT4Recomp and Documents/Gran Turismo 4, including any moved-name sibling or recorded previous installation data. Include settings, controls, Saves, Replays, card backups, runtime/card.ps2, original/prepared disc data, custom textures and configured read/fallback roots. Keep the backups outside old installation cleanup targets. Startup can move user and large data, flatten textures and remove the old per-user program/game folder, fixed shortcuts and registry entries. The running installation and its data-folder layout are excluded from that legacy cleanup; do not rely on an old executable folder as your recovery copy.

steps.title: Register the official outer launcher
steps.instruction: Select GT4Recomp.exe from its complete creating installation, use its installation directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Start only when a separate GT4Recomp instance is not already running; a second launcher can merely bring the first forward and return. Portcove tracks the selected launcher session, not game-only play time. Save launch details and consent to Play separately; then use the upstream launcher's Play operation.

steps.title: Let the upstream launcher own the game session
steps.instruction: The launcher stays alive, hides to the tray during Play and watches its child game; when the game exits it harvests the card and returns Home. The launcher supplies required renderer environment, config, per-session files and card locks. Quit/save through the game, wait for the upstream launcher to finish card handling, then close the launcher to end the selected session. Closing it while playing asks first and can end the game through its kill-on-close job. Do not register an internal payload, bypass the owner or assume closing Portcove provides a save checkpoint.

steps.title: Keep update and restart transitions upstream-owned
steps.instruction: Upstream owns setup, renderer downloads/updates, runtime replacement, data movement and recovery. A launcher update starts its installer and exits; WebView recovery can restart the launcher in safe mode. Complete these transitions outside the registered normal session and revalidate the resulting launcher. Portcove does not reproduce renderer environment, follow replacement processes, acquire originals or delete/restore external data.

steps.title: Retain component terms and known limits
steps.instruction: Keep MIT code notices, the separately GPL-licensed GSdx/PCSX2 renderer notices and source, and all other component notices. Check upstream’s limits for licence demos, menu backgrounds, wheels, long sessions and hardware. Portcove has not confirmed game execution or save compatibility with this launcher route.

warnings: The package includes Gran Turismo 4 cover art and derived brand artwork that the project license does not cover. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.
Track the official launcher session and let it own preparation, renderer environment, card handling and ordinary game launch. Optional installer/WebView restarts are not followed.

Keep the backups outside old installation cleanup targets. Startup can move user and large data, flatten textures and remove the old per-user program/game folder, fixed shortcuts and registry entries. The running installation and its data-folder layout are excluded from that legacy cleanup; do not rely on an old executable folder as your recovery copy.

Before Play the launcher builds the runtime card from its library, then harvests after exit; do not edit card/library files concurrently. It prunes older session folders to 20 and may rewrite corrupt update metadata to .json.bad. Preserve all current/fallback/legacy roots before maintenance; do not assume cross-version save compatibility.

references.title: Preserve effective saves and recovery paths
references.instruction: Large data normally stays in <install>/data; a nonwritable install may read that folder while writing to %LOCALAPPDATA%/GT4Recomp. Per-user settings, controls, save/replay libraries and card backups normally use %APPDATA%/GT4Recomp, with upstream fallback/read layers retained during migration. The Windows ZIP instructions require upstream resource extraction or the documented manual ANIM/DATA/MAPS/MUSIC copy before normal play. The Linux Flatpak first-start resource picker is a different route. Portcove does not run the extraction BAT, acquire demo/original assets or install Windows redistributables for this prepared-copy route. Select native fheroes2.exe after setup. Keep the creating working directory, complete runtime/resources and all original/custom maps and music. Windows profile selection checks an existing HOME environment first, using HOME/.fheroes2, then APPDATA/fheroes2, with an SDL preference fallback. Preserve the actual creating account/environment and selected config/data directories rather than assuming AppData is always used; Portcove does not inject environment variables. Keep fheroes2.cfg, the full data/profile tree including files/save, saves, custom files and unknowns. Do not force a new portable profile or treat the missing-resource error window as an original-data picker. Finish setup with upstream’s tools and start and quit the intended copy before registering it. Keep the creating version and actual data locations recoverable when replacing an external copy.

steps.title: Choose an independent Linux or Mac package
steps.instruction: For a separate Linux x86-64 or ARM64 ZIP, keep the complete archive contents in a permanent folder and use upstream’s extraction script or manually copy your own ANIM, DATA, MAPS and MUSIC when present. Start fheroes2 from its folder. The Linux ZIPs need SDL2, SDL2_image, SDL2_mixer, zlib, glibc 2.35 and libstdc++ providing GLIBCXX_3.4.30. Flathub’s io.github.ihhub.Fheroes2 uses its own first-start import and sandbox profile. On Apple Silicon, use the native Homebrew or MacPorts route and upstream’s fheroes2-extract-resources tool. For the Intel Mac ZIP, follow upstream’s SDL library setup. The Intel binary needs macOS 10.15 or later and matching Intel SDL2 compatibility, SDL2_image, SDL2_mixer and libpng at its /usr/local/opt paths. Standalone Mac builds use ~/.fheroes2 with an ordinary HOME; source-built Mac app bundles use separate Library/Preferences and Library/Application Support profiles. Keep the actual profile and the package that created it.

steps.title: Import your originals with the Android Toolset
steps.instruction: Extract the official fheroes2_android.zip and install fheroes2.apk. The package documents Android 5.1 or newer. Put your own original ANIM, DATA, MAPS and MUSIC directories that are present in one ZIP, copy it to the device, and choose Extract HoMM2 assets in fh2 Toolset. Open fheroes2 after the import. Keep the original ZIP and an accessible backup of the actual Android profile before clearing app data or replacing the package.

steps.title: Select the prepared Windows player
steps.instruction: Select fheroes2.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

warnings: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant rights to original game assets, music, mods or bundled components.
Before updating the game, keep a copy of its working files and every location containing saved data. Choosing a different executable does not give it a separate profile.

Back up the actual upstream profile before replacing the runtime. The Linux ZIP normally uses ~/.config/fheroes2 for settings and ~/.local/share/fheroes2 for data, including files/save and custom maps. If you set XDG_CONFIG_HOME or XDG_DATA_HOME, preserve those actual locations and use absolute paths outside the runtime folder. Flatpak, Mac and Android keep their own profiles.
The Windows x64 ZIP may need the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 Redistributable linked by upstream. Portcove runs no bundled resource, demo or prerequisite installer.

The Linux x86-64 ZIP needs SDL2, SDL2_image, SDL2_mixer, zlib, glibc 2.35 and libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.30. Intel Mac requires macOS 10.15 or later and matching Intel SDL2 compatibility, SDL2_image, SDL2_mixer and libpng at the upstream /usr/local/opt paths.

Keep a separate backup of the actual external fheroes2 profile, including files/save, settings and custom maps. Use a separately prepared copy for custom profile or resource locations. Real save compatibility across versions remains unverified.

references.title: Registration ownership and removal
references.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

references.title: Player-data ownership
references.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: the actual external fheroes2 profile and the original and custom resources of your prepared copy. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

references.title: Managed runtime ownership
references.instruction: Portcove installs and replaces its separate official runtime using the declared release rules. Existing external registrations retain their files and user/upstream ownership. Runtime rollback carries current declared data; it does not rewind saves or establish older-runtime compatibility. Gameplay and populated-save compatibility remain separate qualification. The managed copy has no declared local player data to back up. Back up the external profile separately.

steps.title: Prepare the complete owned-disc installation upstream

No original, compiler, helper or build is obtained or run by this registration. The official 0.2.2 Windows ZIP unpacks to Breakdown-Recompilation-0.2.2/ with Breakdown.exe and tools/. steps.title: Select the completed normal native launcher
steps.instruction: Select Breakdown.exe in its complete creating Windows package directory, use that directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Keep the matching prepared installation and companions. The selected launcher loads work/build/breakdown_game.dll and runs the game in its own process/window; it is not an instruction to select a generated DLL, internal standalone executable, build helper or Linux launcher. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately.

steps.title: Preserve the actual installation and all data roots
steps.instruction: The launcher normally uses %LOCALAPPDATA%/BreakdownRecomp for settings.ini, work/ with extracted game/generated build/ready markers, and logs/. Preserve that complete tree plus the selected original ISO and package. An established BREAKDOWN_DATA or BREAKDOWN_TOOLS override selects different roots; retain them too without creating a new override here. Logs include build/game/launcher records. Keep complete recovery copies outside generated work and staging trees before rebuilding.

steps.title: Keep the effective save folder separate from rebuild data
steps.instruction: The upstream default save folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%/xboxrecomp. Its Options saved-games setting can select another location and is passed through XBOXRECOMP_SAVE_DIR. Preserve the actual save tree, settings and every established custom/external root; that default name does not establish per-title isolation or save compatibility. Choosing another saved-games folder does not move existing saves. This guide performs no save migration, import, backup or destructive management.

steps.title: Complete rebuild and restart paths outside attachment
steps.instruction: Ordinary prepared play runs inside the selected process. Upstream repair/rebuild can invalidate ready/build stamps, replace generated work/toolkit/project/build material and request a fresh launcher process; Restart starts a successor and the current process exits. Complete setup, rebuilds and such restarts outside the attached-session scope, close all actual players/helpers/successors, then review/relink changed bytes. Portcove does not adopt or terminate a successor or own runtime replacement; preserve originals and independent recovery copies first.

steps.title: Retain release and ownership limits
steps.instruction: Upstream 0.2.2 is explicitly early/incomplete: some background music loops, Retry/loading can take a long time and some textures appear late. These remain attributable upstream limitations, not Portcove passes or repaired failures. Keep component notices; project/toolkit/component terms grant no Namco original-game rights. The release assembler takes an external toolkit working checkout, so exact packaged toolkit/source correspondence is not established here. Removing registration preserves every external file. No managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal or Supported/protected acceptance is offered.

warnings: Version 0.2.2 is early and incomplete. Upstream reports looping background music, slow Retry/loading and late textures.

The offered Crispy 7.2 runtime rejects retail v1.0; use the upstream-recommended official upgrade to v1.1 while preserving your original copy. The unsafe -v10override bypass is not offered, and demo/shareware data is not qualified by this managed base-game route. An expansion alone does not supply the base game, and Heretic is a different original. Keep your originals and edition identity; renaming another game’s WAD does not convert it. Originals are not included or authenticated by Portcove. Use a recognized upstream installation, or deliberately copy matching files into the originals subfolder (named exactly originals) of this entry’s fresh private data folder; keep your original copies.

steps.title: Use the upstream setup and launch controls
steps.instruction: Play opens crispy-hexen-setup.exe. Configure controls and use F2 Warp for single-player launch; choose the matching detected IWAD there. The main-menu launch command forwards its existing arguments. The PWAD/mod browser is not an original-IWAD browser. Keep different title entries separate. Do not switch this entry’s original edition in place: its retained runtime versions share data. Use a separate Portcove library or independently owned upstream copy for another source variant. No automatic switching or cross-variant save compatibility is established. An upstream setup exit does not establish that the game loaded or ran successfully.

steps.title: Keep the declared private data scope
steps.instruction: Portcove retains originals deliberately copied under originals, this entry’s default configuration, saves under saves, known default save locations, numbered screenshots and declared recording files. Put custom recordings under demos or use a demo-prefixed .lmp filename. Upstream may read and write its music-pack profile on Play. Music packs and custom paths outside this installation remain external and outside Portcove backups. Extra files written inside the installation outside its declared folders are outside this offered scope and can block maintenance. Keep the creating runtime, original files and actual data before changing a source variant or using an older runtime.

steps.title: Keep updates in one place
steps.instruction: Portcove manages this new official game installation and the data listed for it. It does not import an existing project profile or convert a separately registered game. Existing registered copies keep their external files and update tools. Back up those external profiles and original files separately. Automated fixture checks and reaching a setup menu do not establish original-file or gameplay compatibility.

warnings: Play opens the project’s setup and launch controls. Supply your own matching original game files that you are permitted to use.
Portcove backups exclude external music packs, custom paths and data belonging to separately registered games.

references.title: Install the native package on Linux or Mac
references.instruction: On Debian, install the crispy-doom package through the package manager. On Mac, use the upstream-documented MacPorts port or a supported Homebrew formula. Start crispy-hexen with -iwad followed by the quoted path to your own HEXEN.WAD from retail Hexen updated to v1.1. Use the external package manager for replacement.

references.title: Keep the existing Crispy profile

Mac normally uses ~/Library/Application Support/crispy-doom. Keep any custom locations and the creating runtime before switching package versions. The external profile can be shared across games.

steps.instruction: Use your independently permitted noncommercial copy and own Frontschweine German PAL disc (SLES-02767), with its CUE and all three BIN tracks. Keep the complete original set separate. Upstream identifies data Track 01 by 391706784 bytes, MD5 a833706e9f28020cc665b9f1d5148f74 and SHA-1 ba85ec068293da37cdc261c2b77143dfb2057774; these do not identify the CUE or whole set and do not grant game-data rights.

steps.title: Complete upstream setup
steps.instruction: Use the matching v0.1.0 Windows setup kit or documented source recipe. Supply your own disc, Generate and rebuild outside Portcove; Windows uses Git and Python 3.11 and the upstream toolchain setup. Its rebuild includes PGO training runs. Finish all preparation before registration. Bundled OpenBIOS replaces a retail BIOS. Preserve the exact title/framework/UI combination, staged mods, BIOS and runtime dependencies.

steps.title: Select the completed game
steps.instruction: Select build/Frontschweine_Recompiled.exe, use its complete creating build directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Do not register the root setup host, unfinished output, toolchain or rebuild process. The completed player runs its normal launcher and game in the selected process; optional Generate/rebuild successors are outside this route. Saving launch details and requesting Play are separate actions requiring consent.

steps.title: Back up effective data before startup
steps.instruction: With the game closed, retain a separate complete prior runtime and copies of exe-local settings.toml, disc.cfg, bios.cfg, mods, saves/, game.toml and game_options.toml, every configured external card/save/disc path and overlay-capture root. Default cards and states use the title saves directory; explicit card paths and --memcard-dir can change effective roots. Include loose legacy state_*.pst, openbios/scph1001 state folders and the .pst_bios_isolated marker: upstream can move legacy states on first startup and write its marker even after skipped moves. Do not assume retries or cross-BIOS/build state compatibility. Card initialization can attempt a blank-card write after an existing image cannot be opened. Include current settings.toml.bad outside the active installation: malformed settings cause startup to delete the older .bad file, then rename current settings.toml to .bad before future settings writes.

steps.title: Preserve extracted files, mods and caches
steps.instruction: The game-owned Instant Loading mod reads or rewrites exe-local extracted/ files from the mounted disc and removes a failed partial extraction. Runtime-loaded overlays can be translated and cached; preserve build/cache, custom capture roots, extracted data and all custom mods separately before rebuilding. Build staging owns bundled mod content. Missing overlay tools can leave upstream interpreter fallback; this guide does not promise every code path is already compiled.

steps.title: Preserve both mod layouts before migration
steps.instruction: Before startup, separately back up the complete exe-local mods/ tree, including packages/, bundled/, installed/ and state.toml. The pinned runtime migrates legacy mods/packages/<id>/<version> into mods/installed/<id>/<version>, preferring a rename then recursive copy fallback. It deletes legacy versions already present in bundled/ or installed/, and removes the remaining legacy packages tree when its migration reports no stranded version/error. Do not rely on duplicate legacy folders or unrecognized loose files as recovery copies; preserve them outside that tree before starting. Build-staged bundled mods and user-installed mods remain upstream-owned.

steps.title: Keep one replacement owner
steps.instruction: Upstream and the player own tools, generation, rebuilds, updates, game settings, cards and recovery. Portcove only registers your selected completed native copy; it does not acquire originals, build or replace the runtime or delete its external files. Finish upstream maintenance outside a tracked session, retain a complete recovery copy, then revalidate the selected executable. Recover runtime and current player data deliberately rather than rewinding saves with an old build.

steps.title: Keep title and permission limits
steps.instruction: This is the German PAL title, not a promise for another Hogs of War region or build. The upstream playthrough statement is its report, not a new qualification of your prepared copy. Preserve the project and pinned framework PolyForm Noncommercial notices, the UI notice and supplied OpenBIOS licence; their component terms do not grant the original disc contents.

warnings: Use an independently permitted completed native copy for the noncommercial purposes allowed by its components.
Setup, PGO, optional netplay and rebuilding remain upstream operations; save compatibility is not promised.

listings.name: Icewind Dale II (GemRB)
listings.summary: Set up Icewind Dale II through its upstream gemrb player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use a complete installed original Icewind Dale II working copy. Icewind Dale I, Enhanced Edition and the included trivial demo are different inputs. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=iwd2. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
steps.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/icewind-dale-2, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate icewind-dale-2.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. Back up the sandbox config and actual saves separately. To register the standalone x86-64 AppImage, allow the downloaded file to run and select the AppImage itself in Portcove. Choose your private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines, then review and save the selection. If the official AppImage reports that it cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run as the first separate argument. Keep -c and the config path on their own lines. Play starts the upstream player. For Flatpak, use the command above.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Mac build
steps.instruction: Use the Mac Source Ports Universal 2 DMG at https://github.com/MacSourcePorts/MSPBuildSystem/releases/tag/GemRB_0.9.5. Its v0.9.5 build uses macOS 10.15 or later on Intel and macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon. GemRB’s SourceForge release directory also offers separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Keep the bundle complete. Use this game’s own configuration and point GamePath to the prepared original game folder. Keep this title’s saves, config and working data together when replacing the bundle. To register the Mac Source Ports bundle, copy the complete gemrb.app from the DMG and open it normally once. Select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb in Portcove. Choose your private working folder, then enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines. Review the selection and choose Play.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

warnings: GemRB clears its cache directory. Use a dedicated private CachePath, separate from original files, saves and profile roots.

GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.
These sibling routes use upstream setup, launch and replacement. Keep the creating runtime and actual player files recoverable before changing versions.

listings.name: Icewind Dale (original) (GemRB)
listings.summary: Set up Icewind Dale (original) through its upstream gemrb player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use a complete installed original Icewind Dale working copy. Keep Heart of Winter/Trials of the Luremaster only with their matching installed data; do not invent those expansions from the base game or substitute Enhanced Edition data. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=auto. For original Icewind Dale, let this build recognize the installed iwd/how expansion combination; do not force an absent expansion. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
steps.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/icewind-dale, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate icewind-dale.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. Back up the sandbox config and actual saves separately. To register the standalone x86-64 AppImage, allow the downloaded file to run and select the AppImage itself in Portcove. Choose your private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines, then review and save the selection. If the official AppImage reports that it cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run as the first separate argument. Keep -c and the config path on their own lines. Play starts the upstream player. For Flatpak, use the command above.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Mac build
steps.instruction: Use the Mac Source Ports Universal 2 DMG at https://github.com/MacSourcePorts/MSPBuildSystem/releases/tag/GemRB_0.9.5. Its v0.9.5 build uses macOS 10.15 or later on Intel and macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon. GemRB’s SourceForge release directory also offers separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Keep the bundle complete. Use this game’s own configuration and point GamePath to the prepared original game folder. Keep this title’s saves, config and working data together when replacing the bundle. To register the Mac Source Ports bundle, copy the complete gemrb.app from the DMG and open it normally once. Select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb in Portcove. Choose your private working folder, then enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines. Review the selection and choose Play.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

warnings: GemRB clears its cache directory. Use a dedicated private CachePath, separate from original files, saves and profile roots.

GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.
These sibling routes use upstream setup, launch and replacement. Keep the creating runtime and actual player files recoverable before changing versions.

references.title: Preserve working data across updates
references.instruction: GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.

listings.name: ICO (ico-pc / nathanialf)
listings.summary: Explore ICO (ico-pc / nathanialf) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Select your ICO disc on first Play
steps.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own ICO European SCES-50760, Japanese SCPS-11003 or Korean SCPS-56001 disc image when asked. Use ISO, CHD, or BIN with its matching CUE; the US disc is not supported. Keep the image outside the runtime folder. The game verifies and extracts its data on first launch (about 1 GB); later launches use that extracted copy. Keep your original image available if a future data-format change requires extraction again.

steps.title: Keep saves with this portable copy
steps.instruction: The official portable download enables portable=1 and keeps saves, settings and extracted disc data in userdata beside the player. Windows puts the player in x64; Linux puts it at the archive root. Back up userdata/memcard for saves, and use userdata/memcard2 for an optional second card. With portable=0 or an unwritable portable folder, data instead uses the upstream user-profile folder. Preserve that folder separately. Texture/model packs go in the documented textures/models folders. Close the game and preserve your current data before replacing a runtime; older versions may not read newer saves.

steps.title: Other upstream platforms
steps.instruction: The upstream project also publishes Apple-silicon macOS bundles, ARM Linux and mobile packages. Follow its platform guide for those copies; their setup and data locations differ from these Windows x64 and Linux x64 portable archives.

listings.name: ICO (ICO & Shadow of the Colossus Collection) — ICO PC Port (feanor-noldorin)

steps.instruction: Use your own PlayStation 3 collection disc dump. The exact serial and revision are not confirmed here; check pipeline/ico_profile.json before setup.

steps.title: Follow upstream setup
steps.instruction: Follow alpha 0.2.3 Setup.exe with your own disc and RPCS3 decryption. It recompiles the game locally.

warnings: Upstream reports the title, opening and gameplay controls at 30 FPS. Long sessions have not been tried.
Portcove has not confirmed setup, gameplay, saves or updates for this experimental port.

listings.name: Hollow Knight / HK: Dual Souls (igawa6)
listings.summary: Explore Hollow Knight / HK: Dual Souls (igawa6) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.
listings.download_block_reason: The selected upstream README states that the APK contains Hollow Knight compiled game code; its redistribution audit also identifies the patch as carrying game content. No publisher permission for that distribution is established here. Fresh Portcove downloads remain unavailable until an attributable grant or a package that creates those materials from the player’s own inputs resolves this boundary. Existing permitted copies keep their files and upstream ownership.

steps.title: Keep a permitted prepared copy
steps.instruction: For an already obtained permitted copy, follow this fork’s on-device Import Game flow with your own complete Hollow Knight GOG/Steam v1.5.12620 Voidheart folder and its matching release patch. The folder contains Hollow Knight_Data or hollow_knight_Data. Choose the game folder and patch, then Build game data and START GAME. Do not substitute another game version or describe the published patch as containing no game content.

steps.title: Keep your data when changing versions
steps.instruction: The upstream Save Files page exports/imports slots; saves use Android/data/igawa6.dualsouls/files and imports retain the previous slot as .bak. Preserve an export before changing the app. Upstream says to update over the same signed app and never uninstall first: uninstall or Clear storage deletes saves and built data. A required data rebuild uses the matching new patch; PC save wrapping is not directly compatible.

listings.name: Mario Party 6 (Starlit Party)
listings.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared Starlit Party Windows player for your own Mario Party 6 USA disc. Preserve its actual working-directory saves and content root; limited minigame coverage and title-specific launcher/font permission scope remain explicit.

steps.title: Prepare your own USA disc upstream
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. Finish upstream preparation outside Portcove, keep independent originals and recovery copies. No original, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed by this guide. Use your own Mario Party 6 USA GameCube disc image or matching extracted disc tree. Complete the supported upstream content import and configuration first, retaining the independent original and any selected external content root. Another region or Mario Party game is not admitted by the shared engine. The Windows native player, Android APK and browser/iPhone experience are different artifacts, not a shared native-platform qualification.

steps.title: Keep the complete Windows package
steps.instruction: The inspected official 0.5.0 Windows ZIP contains AMD64 mp6native.exe, renderer libraries, res/ and notices. Keep the complete extracted package. The selected native entry launches the UI and calls GameMain within the same process; do not select a GameCube executable, disc image, browser bundle, Android package or build script. Package presence and source review do not establish complete imports, dependencies or Windows gameplay.

steps.title: Attach the prepared player
steps.instruction: Select mp6native.exe, use its complete extracted package folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately, then use the upstream player UI with its already prepared content. Working directory matters: Windows saves are deliberately relative to it. Complete any missing import/preparation outside the attached attempt. Quit the actual game normally; forced termination is not a save-flush guarantee.

steps.title: Preserve actual saves and content configuration
steps.instruction: Keep mp6_config.json beside the executable, the saves/ directory relative to the established working directory, memory-card GCIs, states, logs, renderer caches and the selected external content tree. Preserve old working-directory save roots if they differ from the package directory; do not change CWD without reviewing that effect. Upstream states require the same linked build, while GCIs are durable game saves; neither establishes observed restore compatibility. This guide performs no move, migration, backup or deletion.

steps.title: Retain title-specific permission and font evidence
steps.instruction: Keep docs/PARTYBOARD_PROVENANCE.md, all author credits, res/fonts/LICENSES.txt and runtime/component notices. The selected upstream publicly records its maintainer’s 2026-09-12 confirmation of permission to redistribute the adapted Partyboard launcher and N64 Party font with this MP6 release. It explicitly does not claim a public general license for those foreign materials; this guide does not reuse that confirmation for another project or artifact. Other fonts have separate OFL/Apache terms. Original game code/assets still require a copy you are independently permitted to use.

steps.title: Maintain the external copy and limited scope
steps.instruction: Quit the game normally before changing files; forced termination may not finish saving. After an upstream update, relink and review the changed executable. Removing the registration leaves all external files in place; Portcove does not install, update, roll back, back up or delete this copy. Upstream reports only 49 of 81 minigames playable, with unsupported board minigames skipped after a notice. Portcove has not confirmed minigames, boards, microphone support, saving or gameplay on Windows or other platforms.

warnings: Preserve working-directory saves and exact USA content. Partial minigame coverage and this release’s limited launcher/font permission record do not grant broader support or reuse rights.

steps.title: Follow upstream setup
steps.instruction: Follow the developer source-build instructions and launcher setup with your own disc. Machine-translated English preview content is optional.

listings.name: inFamous (2009 PS3) (inFAMOUSreborn)
listings.summary: An early inFamous PS3 recompilation with setup 1.1. The Windows 10/11 x86-64 Direct3D 12 setup EXE checks or installs build tools, imports your own European BCES00220 ISO or game folder, then generates and compiles locally. Encrypted ISOs need their matching .dkey. A launch announcement does not establish playable progress; Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

steps.title: Finish the supported European game setup
steps.instruction: Use your own inFamous European PS3 BCES00220 files and complete the upstream Windows setup, translation and build before adding the player. An already decrypted supported folder avoids a key-input route; encrypted images have their separate owner-supplied requirements. This guide provides no keys, decryption or game data. The selected 1.1 Windows setup is a preparation program, not an already compiled game. Windows 10/11 x64, Direct3D 12 and the upstream build/runtime prerequisites remain required.

steps.title: Keep the complete prepared installation
steps.instruction: Retain the full completed port directory, its native inFamous.exe launcher, installer/launch.txt, build-install/inFamousRecomp.exe, the prepared game/ELF, libraries, settings and notices. The producer writes executable, working-directory, argument and environment values into launch.txt. The normal launcher reads those values; selecting the bare game without its published context is not an equivalent shortcut. Keep project/runtime/compiler/component terms separate from original game rights and do not share private translated outputs.

steps.title: Add the native upstream launcher
steps.instruction: Select the completed inFamous.exe in its existing port directory, use that directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready. Its native launcher supplies the producer-written launch configuration and environment. Portcove observes that launcher only; it can report the launch finished after handoff while inFamousRecomp.exe and helpers still run. Use the game’s own controls to quit and do not interpret the launcher’s exit as full-game completion.

steps.title: Preserve the current saves and launch configuration
steps.instruction: Keep the whole existing port, installer/launch.txt, settings.ini, all original/generated content and gamedata/. Default saves are under gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata relative to the configured port working directory; retain all profiles, trophies and related data as present. Existing SAVEDATA_ROOT and other producer/user path overrides must remain intact. Do not transplant launch.txt into a different layout, reset populated settings or merge saves merely to add the launcher. No save conversion, migration, backup or restore is performed.

steps.title: Leave updates and recovery upstream
steps.instruction: Close the actual game and helpers before upstream replacement, rebuild, repair or recovery, even if Portcove’s activity has finished. Upstream owns imports, build tools, runtime replacement and launch configuration; review/select the current launcher again after changes. Early-release PPU/SPU, rendering and campaign claims do not establish gameplay/controller/real-save acceptance here. Removing the library reference preserves all external files. No managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking or Supported qualification is supplied.

warnings: Select the completed inFamous.exe launcher and preserve installer/launch.txt plus its full port/data directory. Its handoff can outlive Portcove’s activity; close the actual game/helpers before upstream changes. The setup EXE and a context-free bare runtime are separate routes.

listings.name: inFAMOUS Second Son — inFAMOUS-Second-Son-PC-Edition (kam0n4ik)
listings.summary: Upstream reports city gameplay, saves and 46–51 FPS on one PC. Frame-time measurements and experimental presets are separate results; a full playthrough and broader hardware compatibility remain unconfirmed. Follow the setup instructions below. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

steps.title: Check the required game files
steps.instruction: Use your own decrypted CUSA00004 update 01.07 folder containing eboot.bin, sce_module, sce_sys and art, about 30 GB. Upstream explicitly requires no PS4 firmware files.

steps.title: Follow upstream setup
steps.instruction: README offers SecondSonPC-win64.zip. Extract beside owned eboot.bin and run play.cmd; first launch compiles shaders, not the game CPU executable. Alternative build.ps1 uses LLVM 20+, CMake/Ninja and Visual Studio headers/SDK, with pinned shadPS4 source patches. Saves stay in userdata and are backed up by play.cmd.

warnings: Upstream reports city gameplay, saves and 46–51 FPS on one PC. Frame-time measurements and experimental presets are separate results; a full playthrough and broader hardware compatibility remain unconfirmed.
Portcove has not confirmed setup, gameplay, saves or updates for this experimental port.

listings.name: inFAMOUS 2 — infamous2-pc (ThiagoFraga761)

Its 54–130 FPS result covers one Ryzen 9800X3D/RX 9070 XT Linux PC. First-use shader spikes remain, and the backend is Linux-only. Portcove has not run the game. Follow the setup instructions below. steps.instruction: Use your own inFAMOUS 2 PlayStation 3 BCUS98125 version 01.00 disc tree with decrypted PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.elf and your own PS3 dev_flash firmware. Keep generated game code local.

warnings: Upstream reports startup, videos, menus, cutscenes and gameplay from Empire City to New Marais, with controls, audio and saves. Its 54–130 FPS result covers one Ryzen 9800X3D/RX 9070 XT Linux PC. First-use shader spikes remain, and the backend is Linux-only. Portcove has not run the game.
Portcove has not confirmed setup, gameplay, saves or updates for this experimental port.

listings.summary: Upstream reports startup, menus, cutscenes and the first New Marais missions. This alpha has never been tested from start to finish. Follow the setup instructions below. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

steps.title: Check the required game files
steps.instruction: Use your own digital NPUA80638 package, license and game files. This guide does not specify the required update; check the project’s requirements before setup.

steps.title: Follow upstream setup
