listings.name: Infinite Undiscovery Recomp (doc-haz)
listings.summary: Explore Infinite Undiscovery Recomp (doc-haz) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Import your own game on first Play
steps.instruction: The official Windows x64 ZIP is portable and has no installer. Choose InfiniteUndiscoveryRecomp.exe and keep its DLLs and notices together. On first Play, the game’s integrated wizard validates and imports your own Disc 1 from a supported XDVDFS ISO or extracted folder; Disc 2 and A/B Voucher DLC are optional. It identifies supported USA, USA-UNDUB, Europe, Japan and Asia editions from the media. Do not mix editions. Portcove does not run an extraction helper or developer compiler. Windows 10/11 x64 and Direct3D 12 are required; use Microsoft’s Visual C++ 2015–2022 x64 Redistributable if the documented runtime DLLs are missing.

warnings: Close the game before updates or copying data. Keep interrupted import/staging folders recoverable and consult upstream; do not merge different editions. Backups can include large original-game files and DLC, so keep them private.
Do not copy old runtime DLLs or shader caches over the replacement. Runtime rollback does not rewind saves or guarantee that older software can read them.

The selected release-tag documentation had not tested the Disc 1 to Disc 2 transition. Later upstream documentation at 614a0a0ebd72103fce8aaa52c715d847b703a53e reports repeated successful transitions, while complete Disc 2 progression and a full playthrough remain unverified and a Vesplume Tower / Orb of Patience softlock remains under investigation. These are upstream reports; Portcove has not run the game.
Keep cache/runtime.toml too: it contains runtime settings despite the cache folder name.

references.title: Keep each content profile together
references.instruction: The complete portable folder holds setup.json and separate USA, USA-UNDUB, EUROPE, JAPAN and ASIA profiles. Each configured profile owns its imported assets/DLC, saves and configuration. Keep cache/runtime.toml too: it contains runtime settings despite the cache folder name. Close the game before updates or copying data. Keep interrupted import/staging folders recoverable and consult upstream; do not merge different editions. Backups can include large original-game files and DLC, so keep them private. The separate IU Save Bridge companion is optional and is not run by Portcove.

references.title: Update an existing copy safely
references.instruction: For a copy you register yourself, you or upstream provide updates. Extract a new official player into a separate folder, keep the working copy, and follow the selected release’s instructions for carrying its complete compatible content profiles and setup.json. Do not copy old runtime DLLs or shader caches over the replacement. Runtime rollback does not rewind saves or guarantee that older software can read them. The selected release-tag documentation had not tested the Disc 1 to Disc 2 transition. Later upstream documentation at 614a0a0ebd72103fce8aaa52c715d847b703a53e reports repeated successful transitions, while complete Disc 2 progression and a full playthrough remain unverified and a Vesplume Tower / Orb of Patience softlock remains under investigation. These are upstream reports; Portcove has not run the game.

listings.name: Initial D Arcade Stage 3 / Native SH-4 recompilation WIP
listings.summary: Explore Initial D Arcade Stage 3 / Native SH-4 recompilation WIP and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Use the public Windows early-demo route
steps.instruction: Use the complete Initial.D.Arcade.Stage.3.Recompiled.v2489.zip folder, keeping Initial D Arcade Stage 3 Recompiled.exe, Initial D Arcade Stage 3 Recompiled Runtime.exe, tools, libraries, settings and notices together. This is an unfinished Windows x64 public playtest for NAOMI 2 Initial D Arcade Stage 3 GDS-0033, not the Dreamcast game or a finished release. Its native SH-4/static-AOT and Vulkan claims remain upstream observations; Portcove does not infer complete instruction coverage, hardware or gameplay acceptance from them.

steps.title: Complete upstream owned-data preparation
steps.instruction: Supply your own legally obtained matching gds-0033.chd and 317-0384-com.pic in the included game files directory. The ordinary upstream launcher validates and extracts the required files locally; allow about 1.3 GB of temporary space. A NAOMI 2 BIOS is neither required nor accepted by this route. Do not substitute a different CHD/PIC, bypass integrity failures, use a BIOS as the executable or share extracted private game files. Original arcade, project/runtime and component rights remain separate; this guide grants no acquisition, firmware or decryption authority.

steps.title: Add the ordinary native launcher
steps.instruction: Select Initial D Arcade Stage 3 Recompiled.exe, set its complete containing product folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready and use the upstream launcher. It owns preparation/update prompts and supplies the runtime’s game, card, music, settings and presentation context. Keep its supplied PowerShell/tools and runtime with it; do not select powershell.exe, a PS1 script, the integrity/setup helper or a context-free Runtime.exe as the game. Preserve the upstream 60 FPS starting/default choice and any existing F1 choices rather than forcing experimental presentation.

steps.title: Preserve the whole portable player-data layout
steps.instruction: Keep game files, card data, custom music and logs, idas3_user_settings.ini, update preferences and all other existing user files in the product folder. Preserve card data/InitialD_player_card.card or the existing selected CardImage path and every other card. A card image and a game-state snapshot are separate; do not reset a populated card, merge files, discard pending recovery data or assume that another arcade/Dreamcast build can use it. Portcove performs no card import/conversion, backup, restore or source extraction.

steps.title: Keep maintenance and completion evidence upstream
steps.instruction: The selected native launcher can hand off through helpers. Portcove follows that program only; a finished activity does not prove the runtime/helpers have stopped or make files safe to replace. Quit them before upstream updater, repair or recovery, preserve the previous complete application/data, and review/select the launcher again after changes. Upstream’s update preservation, rollback, card and physical-controller reports are not Portcove observations. Removing the reference preserves external files. Managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking and Supported qualification are unavailable; this title’s unfinished acceptance remains explicit.

warnings: Select Initial D Arcade Stage 3 Recompiled.exe with the complete v2489 product folder and your own matching CHD/PIC preparation. Preserve game files, every card, custom music, settings and logs; the runtime and setup scripts require their upstream context.

listings.name: Bugs Bunny: Lost in Time / BBLIT Remaster
listings.summary: Use the upstream renderer and control enhancement with your existing Bugs Bunny: Lost in Time PC game.

steps.title: Keep your original PC game recoverable
steps.instruction: Use your permitted original PC installation and an executable edition listed by upstream. Preserve the working game folder, saves, settings and any existing renderer wrapper before changing it. The download is an enhancement, not a standalone game.

steps.title: Place the enhancement beside the player
steps.instruction: Copy the archive’s BIN/ddraw.dll and BIN/remaster.ini into the game’s BIN folder beside bugs.exe. Review any existing file before replacing it. Do not register the DLL or the BugsBunny.exe launcher.

steps.title: Set the required launch details
steps.instruction: Select BIN/bugs.exe, set the working directory to BIN, and add five separate launch arguments: /opengl, /win, /b0, /x800, /y600. Then choose Play explicitly. Keep saves, settings and remaster.log in BIN backed up; updates remain with you and upstream.

warnings: The enhancement checks specific original bugs.exe editions. Modified or other editions are outside this claim; use upstream’s exact requirements. Linux Proton observations do not establish a native Linux player or Portcove-managed compatibility layer.

listings.name: Descent 3 / Piccu Engine (InsanityBringer)
listings.summary: Explore Descent 3 / Piccu Engine (InsanityBringer) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Add your own Descent 3 data before Play
steps.instruction: Before Play, open the new runtime folder and copy only the original data from your own patched Descent 3 1.4 installation: d3.hog, extra.hog, extra13.hog, and missions/d3.mn3, d3_2.mn3, d3voice1.hog, d3voice2.hog and training.mn3. Keep the old installation intact. Add merc.hog and missions/merc.mn3 only if you own Mercenary; the upstream also recognizes the Steam extra1.hog expansion layout. For multiplayer, follow the packaged README for your own netgames directory and missions/Fury.mn3 and bedlam.mn3; movies are optional. Do not copy old top-level executables or DLLs over this runtime. Then choose Play. This ZIP has no installer; Portcove does not verify a retail-edition checksum for this upstream setup route.

steps.title: Keep a separate backup of your Saved Games profile
steps.instruction: Normal saves, pilots, demos, screenshots and temporary scripts use Windows Saved Games/Piccu Engine. The SDL configuration is Saved Games/Piccu Engine/PiccuEngine.registry, including when portable mode is used. Back up that external profile separately before changing runtime versions; older versions may not read newer data. Keep your original HOG files, missions, netgames and movies available separately too.

steps.title: Keep customized copies separate
steps.instruction: Adding piccu_portable, custom -setdir/-tempdir arguments or failure to resolve Saved Games can place player data and generated DLL caches in the runtime folder. An early startup crash can also leave a dump beside the player. Close the game and preserve your actual player-data locations before changing a customized copy. Do not copy generated script caches into another engine version; follow upstream instructions when changing storage modes.

steps.title: Choose this Preview deliberately
steps.instruction: This optional Windows Preview is the upstream SDL prototype, with fixes for pilot-control loading and input issues. Some settings do not import from older Piccu versions, and switching fullscreen/windowed can show a stray cursor. The stable v1.2.2 upstream copy remains available through the release list or an existing installation; it has separate known control issues. The player is Win32 and can run on 64-bit Windows through Windows compatibility support. Other platforms, gameplay, minimum Windows versions and populated-save restoration are not qualified here.

listings.name: Daggerfall Unity
listings.summary: Play The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall with Daggerfall Unity and your own compatible game folder. Choose your original files in the game’s first-run setup wizard; keep external saves and originals recoverable.

steps.title: Start the game
steps.instruction: On first Play, use Daggerfall Unity’s setup wizard to select your compatible original Daggerfall game folder. It validates the game data. The package is a native Unity player and needs no separate game compilation. Keep external originals where they are.

steps.title: Use the security-updated Intel Mac app
steps.instruction: Download the Mac ZIP from the Daggerfall Unity v1.1.1-cve-2025 release. Unpack DaggerfallUnity.app into a permanent folder separate from your DOS Daggerfall game. The current app executable is Intel x64. In the setup wizard choose the compatible game folder containing ARENA2.

steps.title: Add the prepared native player

If you intentionally use --game_data_root, --user_data_root or --cache_root overrides, retain those exact working paths. Saving launch details and Play remain separate actions. steps.title: Preserve portable data and upstream ownership
steps.instruction: Upstream/player owns installation and runtime replacement. Preserve game/, configuration, and userdata/ beside pacman.exe, including achievements, save-backups/ and cache/. If userdata/ cannot be created, the selected source falls back to Documents/pacman; explicit user/cache roots remain in effect. Upstream creates changed-save snapshots in save-backups/ and retains ten; that is upstream behavior, not Portcove backup coverage or a guarantee of save compatibility. Keep every active root and your own backup before updates; Portcove does not delete or roll back these external files.

warnings: This guide follows the selected upstream source and release descriptions. Portcove has not checked the archive’s contents or checksum, installed prerequisites, or tested launch, graphics, gameplay or restoring real saves.

listings.summary: Use your own DOS JetStrike CD-ROM data with the Windows package or a source build on Linux or Mac.

steps.title: Prepare a writable copy of your original game
steps.instruction: Use your own DOS CD-ROM installation. Keep JS_CDROM.EXE and the INTRO, DATA, GFX, MAP, MISC and PLANE directories together in a writable Game copy.

steps.title: Use the upstream Windows setup
steps.instruction: Extract the complete Windows x64 ZIP into its own folder and keep both executables and every DLL together. Open JetStrike.exe to choose your data and options. The optional Rip CD music action uses your owned CUE image and writes the 14 audio tracks under Game/MUSIC.

steps.title: Build the direct player on Linux
steps.instruction: The reviewed release has no Linux package. Use the upstream source with a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and SDL3 development files. From the repository root, run cmake -S jsport -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DJS_LAUNCHER=OFF -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD_LIBRARIES=-lm, then cmake --build build --target jsport. Keep the built jsport and its SDL3 runtime available. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used on Linux. This build has not been tested with original CD-ROM data on Linux.

steps.title: Build the direct player on Mac
steps.instruction: Use a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and the macOS SDL3 framework from SDL’s official development package. Keep SDL3.framework in a stable folder. From the repository root, run cmake -S jsport -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DJS_LAUNCHER=OFF -DSDL3_DIR="/full/path/SDL3.framework/Resources/CMake" -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH="/full/path/framework-folder", then cmake --build build --target jsport. Replace both paths with your actual framework locations. Build on the Mac you will use, so the player matches Intel or Apple Silicon. Keep the framework folder in place after building. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used. Native Mac game startup and saving have not been tested.

steps.title: Register the actual player in Portcove
steps.instruction: On Windows, choose jsport.exe as the existing installation; on Linux or Mac, choose the built jsport. Choose the player’s containing directory as the working directory. Add --game-dir and your writable Game copy as two separate arguments. Review the selected player, folder and arguments, then choose Play. The separate upstream launcher can stay open or close while its game continues.

warnings: Use your own original game files. The native port includes reconstructed original program behavior and its own separately licensed port code.

references.title: Keep your settings and progress before replacing files
references.instruction: Back up JS.CFG, js_save.000 through js_save.009 and any MUSIC folder with your working game data. Copy %APPDATA%/JetStrike/settings.ini as well. Close both the player and launcher before replacing files. Portcove keeps a launch registration. You and upstream own runtime replacement and backups. Removing the registration leaves the working files and profile in place.

references.title: SDL3 development framework for Mac
references.instruction: Get the official SDL3 development download from https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/latest. Use SDL3.framework from the macos-arm64_x86_64 folder in SDL3.xcframework. The iOS and simulator frameworks are different targets.

references.title: Other platforms
references.instruction: Windows x64 has the reviewed official package. Linux x64 uses the upstream source build described above, with no reviewed Linux package or title-run evidence. Intel Mac and Apple Silicon use the upstream source build described above. Both native architectures were built; Mac game execution remains untested, and there is no reviewed Mac package. Android has no reviewed package or mobile host integration. Those platforms do not inherit Windows or Linux observations.

steps.title: Windows installer setup

steps.title: Prepare the exact supported original upstream
steps.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own GameCube USA GLME01 or Europe GLMP01 revision 0 disc. steps.instruction: The inspected official 1.1.5 Windows x64 ZIP contains AMD64 LuigisMansionRecomp.exe, matching Aurora/Dawn/SDL3/nod and other libraries plus llvm/bin/clang.exe and lld-link.exe. The runtime builds game/<id>/module.dll locally from the original’s main.dol; the release does not supply that original. Keep the whole package and actual generated data. The port’s decompilation and adapted code use their CC0 scope, Aurora MIT and LLVM Apache-with-exception; these do not relicense the original game.

steps.title: Attach the already prepared normal player
steps.instruction: Select LuigisMansionRecomp.exe, use the complete extracted LuigisMansionRecompiled-1.1.5-windows-x64 directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately. When configured discs/modules/overlays are current, the integrated setup is skipped and the module is loaded into this same native player. Missing/stale inputs can trigger local rebuilding; complete it upstream before retrying. Do not select a module DLL or compiler as the executable, and do not enable setup-auto, recovery-reset, finite-frame or test overrides.

steps.title: Preserve regional cards and destructive move recovery
steps.instruction: Normally keep the actual %APPDATA%/Luigi's Mansion Recompiled root, including install.ini, settings.ini, game/GLME01 or GLMP01 modules/keys, hidden_mansion/ overlays, USA/Card A and other regional card folders, caches, logs and recovery state. Older Luigi's Mansion PC folders can be renamed on first 1.1+ start; failed rename can copy while retaining the old folder. Existing portable.txt or portable/ instead selects the package-local portable tree. An upstream requested data move copies/checks and switches, then can delete the previous system root; interrupted portable.lm-tmp/portable.lm-old leftovers can be deleted on next startup. Keep independent copies of both old/new roots and any pending move evidence before starting or changing layout. This guide creates no marker and performs no move, recovery, backup or deletion.

steps.title: Maintain the external player and its rights explicitly
steps.instruction: Keep all own-code, decompilation, adapted Dusklight, Aurora and bundled component notices. Original Nintendo assets, other-region content and optional mods require independent permission. Existing external card/cache/source overrides remain authoritative; keep both disc originals and actual relative/absolute install.ini selections. Quit normally before upstream updates or card/data operations, retain independent recovery and review/relink changed executable bytes. The unfinished original two-player content and upstream campaign claims are not native/installed, co-op, gameplay, save/reload or Supported acceptance here. Removing registration preserves external files; managed lifecycle operations remain unavailable.

warnings: Preserve the actual regional cards and both sides of any system/portable data move before startup. First-use builds, automatic stale-module rebuilding and recovery remain upstream-owned.

listings.name: Monster Hunter Portable 3rd HD Ver. Yakumo
listings.summary: Play your own MHP3rd HD disc image with Yakumo. Portcove can manage a separate Windows x86-64 copy or launch one you prepared.

steps.title: Prepare the game on first Play
steps.instruction: On first Play, choose the uncompressed PSP UMD ISO from your own Monster Hunter Portable 3rd HD Ver. PS3 release (NPJB-40001) and let Yakumo prepare the game. If Yakumo copies the image, the copy is kept and backed up with the managed data. If you use the image where it is, keep it at a stable location outside the managed runtime and back it up yourself.

steps.title: Complete the exact owned-input preparation upstream
steps.instruction: Yakumo needs the PSP UMD image from your own Monster Hunter Portable 3rd HD Ver. PS3 release (NPJB-40001) as an uncompressed ISO. The ordinary PSP edition, a whole PS3 disc image and compressed CSO files are different inputs. For a Windows copy you prepared yourself, let Yakumo prepare the game there and keep Yakumo.exe in its complete creating folder with its overlay libraries, FFmpeg DLLs and other files. If that working copy already starts with supported literal --data-dir or game-folder arguments, enter the same arguments when you select it instead of leaving them empty; do not silently change the creating data or save roots.

steps.title: Set up Yakumo on Linux, Steam Deck, Mac or Android
steps.instruction: On x64 Linux or Steam Deck, open the Flatpak through your desktop or Steam; it uses the Freedesktop Platform 25.08 runtime. If you unpack the x64 tarball instead, start it with ./yakumo from the unpacked folder so the launcher sets the stack size; it needs glibc 2.29 or later, a Vulkan driver and the Vulkan loader. On an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 13 or later, open the ARM64 disk image and copy the whole Yakumo.app to Applications, then open it directly. The publisher uses ad hoc signing; follow its macOS guide for the first-open prompt. On Android 10 or later with Vulkan 1.1, install the ARM64 APK and choose your ISO in the Android file picker. The app copies it into its own storage, so allow about 1.3 GB for the image in addition to the app, and use Yakumo to back up your saves before replacing or removing the app. Use Yakumo for setup and play on these systems.

steps.title: Select the prepared Windows player
steps.instruction: Select Yakumo.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

warnings: MIT covers the project’s own original code; third-party IP remains independently owned. Preserve the applicable packaged FFmpeg LGPL and font/dependency notices; this is not a whole-game rights certificate.

Upstream documents untranslated/blank save-dialog screens, curved-surface issues and unsupported code mods; reported rendering, multiplayer, controller and save compatibility are publisher claims, not Portcove observations. No game, original, helper, installer or native session was run.

For a copy you prepared yourself, the Windows installed profile normally uses %APPDATA%/Yakumo/MHP3rd and the upstream ZIP with portable.txt uses data/ beside the executable. Existing portable.txt, a data/ folder, --portable, --data-dir and MHP3RD_DATA_DIR/MHP3RD_PORTABLE choices affect selection; retain the actual established mode and do not add/remove markers or trigger profile-copy prompts as registration work. A non-writable data directory fails instead of silently falling back.

In a copy you prepared yourself, upstream Set Up Game Data Again and Restart Now after save import can end the selected process and start a successor. Perform those actions outside the attached session; Core does not adopt that successor or offer upstream save import/export, texture installation, backup or network configuration. Retain the old working runtime and all data before replacement.

Yakumo keeps the managed copy's settings, saves, save backups and prepared game in its data folder. Leave MHP3RD_DATA_DIR, MHP3RD_GAME_DIR, MHP3RD_MODS_DIR and MHP3RD_PORTABLE unset, and add no --data-dir or game-folder argument. Otherwise Yakumo can play from or save to a folder Portcove does not keep.
Restart Now after a save import and Set Up Game Data Again restart Yakumo. On Windows, Portcove keeps the session open until the restarted Yakumo closes.
If you already use Yakumo, the first Play of the managed copy can offer to copy your data from %APPDATA%\Yakumo\MHP3rd. The original files stay where they are.

references.title: Find and back up the data you actually use
references.instruction: Keep settings.ini, prepared EBOOT.ELF, copied disc.iso or its external in-place original, ms0/PSP/SAVEDATA (including ULJM05800, ULJM05800QST and ULJM05800DAT), mods, texture packs, pipeline caches/keys, logs, controller mappings, translations/fonts, save-backups, temporary files and all custom roots. A source-build game directory may retain its own ms0 and older saves; do not migrate it automatically. The Flatpak keeps data in ~/.var/app/io.github.teamgdb.Yakumo/data/Yakumo/MHP3rd and can export saves to Downloads. The Linux tarball uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/Yakumo/MHP3rd or ~/.local/share/Yakumo/MHP3rd by default. The Mac app uses ~/Library/Application Support/Yakumo/MHP3rd. Keep your actual profile and any ISO used in place before replacing the app. Yakumo checks NPJB-40001 and encrypted EBOOT.BIN SHA-256 79e25f3512d56e0f7bf5c48351d7d0d255269675ffc8811ac5599322bb66945e, then verifies prepared EBOOT.ELF SHA-256 55c0598436c0753b04331f8e95d406f832d9217806e3a896fed0e88b33637d8c. The check covers those files and the disc ID.

references.title: Registration ownership and removal
references.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

references.title: Player-data ownership
references.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: the data folder the copy actually uses, chosen in this order: a --data-dir folder, the MHP3RD_DATA_DIR folder, data beside Yakumo.exe when portable.txt or a data folder is there (unless MHP3RD_PORTABLE=0), then %APPDATA%\Yakumo\MHP3rd; plus any game folder it starts with and any disc image used in place. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

references.title: Managed runtime ownership
references.instruction: Portcove installs and replaces its separate official runtime using the declared release rules. Existing external registrations retain their files and user/upstream ownership. Runtime rollback carries current declared data; it does not rewind saves or establish older-runtime compatibility. Gameplay and populated-save compatibility remain separate qualification. Portcove preserves only these declared local inputs during replacement and backup: data. Its backup does not include external profiles.

steps.title: Keep an independently permitted complete installation
steps.instruction: Use the completed Windows installation and components you are independently permitted to use. The released setup installs a statically recompiled player; code/component licences and ownership of a disc do not themselves establish permission for every translated game-code package component. steps.title: Supply the exact own disc and title update through upstream
steps.instruction: Finish upstream setup outside Portcove with your own extracted Xbox360 original disc folder, not an ISO: Default.xex, GAME.DAT/GAME.HDR and all required archives. steps.title: Select the actual installed native entry
steps.instruction: Select legodimensions.exe, use its complete containing installation directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Keep matching game/, update/, content/, mods/, tools and any update-mods/ companions produced by the installer. Do not select DimensionsRecompiled-Setup.exe, rexupdate.exe, modcli.exe or a tool script. The native window/game stays in the selected process. Saving launch details and Play are separate actions; driver changes and external Toy Pad setup remain upstream/user tasks.

steps.title: Keep updates, companions and replacement with upstream
steps.instruction: Upstream owns installer updates, DLC import, mod application, config merging and recovery. Installer/updater can enforce compatibility settings and replace runtime/mod files; preserve old complete output and custom data outside all replacement paths first. The game may check for updates and, on your choice, start an external updater and exit; that updater/relaunched game is outside this entry’s tracked session. Optional Toy Pad autostart is upstream-owned; externally started companions remain your responsibility. Close every actual game, updater, restart successor and companion before backup/relink/removal. Review/relink changed selected bytes afterward. Removing registration preserves external files; no Portcove-managed update/rollback/backup/migration/deletion or successor adoption is offered.

warnings: Use only the exact supported Xbox 360 disc and TU23; a title-update filename alone does not identify a compatible copy. Follow upstream setup for physical USB-pad drivers and optional companions. This guide does not guarantee complete campaign play, save/mod compatibility or continuation into a successor process.

Back up the complete installation, legodimensions.toml, content/ (the configured user-data/save/profile/DLC root), game.log/logs, mods/ and update-mods/, plus custom user_data_root, metadata_root, cache_root, game_data_root, update_data_root and log paths recorded by your setup. Preserve external Toy Pad app settings and original sources separately.

The startup relocation helper rewrites paths under an old missing install root to the new executable folder when its game/ exists; it changes configured path references rather than proving save migration. Preserve both locations before moving/starting. Before startup, separately back up both actual vanilla update_data_root and mods_update_root, including PATCH3.DAT/PATCH3.HDR and their .off variants, plus the old/new configuration and recovery copies outside both roots. Upstream applies the fern setting to both roots at startup, renames those files to/from .off and can remove an older .off when a live file exists. Its startup also forces present_effect fsr2/fsr3 to fsr and readback_memexport_batched to false; preserve prior settings without treating those compatibility changes as Portcove migration or feature control.

listings.name: NHL '94 (Genesis) (ninety-four)
listings.summary: Play NHL ’94 on Windows with the Ninety Four native engine and your own supported Genesis ROM. Modified rosters and online sessions have separate compatibility requirements.

steps.title: Choose your own NHL ’94 cartridge dump
steps.instruction: On first Play, select your own supported 1 MiB NHL ’94 Genesis US/Europe ROM in the upstream picker. Keep it at a stable location outside the managed runtime.

steps.title: Prepare the exact original upstream
steps.instruction: Use a complete player and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own 1 MiB retail NHL ’94 Genesis US/Europe ROM. Finish the upstream first-launch ROM picker and saved settings before attachment; retain the independent original. Optional larger ROM hacks and roster imports are separate upstream operations, not another accepted retail revision by title alone. This guide obtains or executes no ROM, converter, helper or game. The inspected official 0.3.6 ZIP contains ninety-four-windows-x86_64/nhl94.exe as an AMD64 native player with matching library and notices. Keep that complete directory. This is the native rewrite using the linked pulseman hardware/audio/frontend facilities; it is not an original Genesis executable or a generic emulator admission. A source build and another platform’s application are separate artifacts. Upstream documents the remembered ROM picker for normal windowed starts; the native entry runs the game in the selected process. Complete a missing-ROM prompt outside the attached attempt. Do not add headless, finite-frame, trace, ROM-extraction or network-server arguments as normal Play.

steps.title: Preserve the actual Linux and Mac data locations
steps.instruction: Preserve any older working-directory data before choosing a different folder. SRAM and whole-machine states are different objects; the source checks a session state against its roster set, which does not prove observed restore or cross-version compatibility. This guide performs no import, migration, backup or deletion. Quit the actual game normally before upstream replacement, restoring SRAM/states or changing roster sets. Keep independent recovery copies and review/relink changed executable bytes; forced termination is not a save-flush guarantee. Upstream whole-game, 60 FPS, rewind and online reports remain upstream claims. No native/installed-app, gameplay, save/reload or Supported acceptance is asserted. On Linux x86-64, the upstream archive needs glibc 2.34 or newer, SDL2 and the GNU C++ and GCC support runtimes. For an existing copy, keep nhl94 and its full archive together and run it from that folder. On macOS 11 or newer, use the upstream universal application for Intel or Apple Silicon. Finder launches keep settings and saves under ~/Library/Application Support/ninety-four. A shell launch can use the working directory instead. Keep the complete application bundle and back up the data location your copy actually uses. Portcove manages the separate Linux runtime, while the Mac application stays with upstream setup.

steps.title: Keep original, roster and component terms separate
steps.instruction: Retain the project MIT notice and pulseman/component notices, including Nuked-OPN2 LGPL-2.1, ymfm BSD-3 and the separately credited upscalers. They grant nothing over the original NHL ’94 name or game data. Use only originals, roster art and modified content you are independently permitted to use. Online peers need matching releases and applicable roster/state data; no account, relay/server, real multiplayer or full user-content corpus qualification is provided.

steps.title: Select the prepared Windows player
steps.instruction: Select nhl94.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

warnings: Keep the original retail ROM and actual working-directory data. Cartridge SRAM, states, modified rosters and online session compatibility are separate.

Use the default data paths with the managed runtime. Keep an independent copy of your ROM, and use a separately prepared copy for custom data paths. Runtime rollback does not establish save-state compatibility.
On Linux x86-64, use glibc 2.34 or newer with SDL2, libstdc++.so.6 and libgcc_s.so.1.

references.title: Registration ownership and removal
references.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

references.title: Player-data ownership
references.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: settings.ini; out/nhl94.srm cartridge SRAM; states/ including Autosave; rosters, recordings, screenshots, videos and configured external ROM/save paths. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

references.title: Managed runtime ownership
references.instruction: Portcove installs and replaces its separate official runtime using the declared release rules. Existing external registrations retain their files and user/upstream ownership. Runtime rollback carries current declared data; it does not rewind saves or establish older-runtime compatibility. Gameplay and populated-save compatibility remain separate qualification. Portcove preserves only these declared local inputs during replacement and backup: out, rosters, screenshots, settings.ini, states, videos. Its backup does not include external profiles.

steps.instruction: Install the stable x86-64 AppImage in Portcove and choose Play. Your Linux system needs AppImage support. The package includes the freeware resources and SDL2. steps.instruction: For an already permitted 1.2 or 1.3 copy, use Android 10 or newer and OpenGL ES 3.0. On Android 10 grant the storage permission. steps.instruction: With an already permitted 1.2 source checkout, use Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake and a Mac with OpenGL 4.1. Follow scripts/build-macos.sh. steps.instruction: Close the game and launcher before copying their data. On Android retain the actual chosen data folder and use the upstream export for memory cards. The card ZIP covers the cards only. After Pikmin setup completes on a supported desktop, choose Use an existing installation. steps.title: Choose your original Xbox disc image on first Play
steps.instruction: On first Play, select your own Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox .iso or .xiso; every edition works. OpenCE extracts its maps into the maps folder beside the player. Keep the disc image outside the game folder, because the game offers any image it finds there. Halo PC or Custom Edition maps do not replace these Xbox maps.

steps.title: Run a Windows copy you manage yourself
steps.instruction: Extract halo-windows-release.zip into its own folder and start halo.exe with no arguments. Use the release package for playing. Debug builds stop at failed assertions, and symbol archives contain debug information. OpenCE asks before installing its own updates and can replace its program files when you accept.

steps.title: Run the external Linux player
steps.instruction: Extract halo-linux-release.zip and keep libSDL3.so.0 beside halo. Make halo executable if needed with chmod u+x halo and run ./halo from that folder. Use a Linux host that can run 32-bit x86 programs. It needs 32-bit glibc 2.29 or newer, OpenGL and display libraries, and PipeWire or PulseAudio client libraries. Choose your own Xbox ISO or XISO on first launch. The file picker needs a desktop portal or zenity. If neither is available, start with a copy of the image beside halo. OpenCE handles updates for this external copy.

warnings: OpenCE is a port of a Halo: Combat Evolved decompilation; the project’s AGPL licence does not cover the original game code. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.
Optional Halo Custom Edition maps and their matching resources belong in custom_maps. OpenSauce maps are incompatible.

Clicking a Halo or Discord invite starts OpenCE directly, outside Portcove, using the version that last registered the link. Close any game started that way before updating or rolling back in Portcove, and start OpenCE from Portcove once after an update before using an invite.

references.title: Keep all actual data locations
references.instruction: Beside the program OpenCE keeps config.toml, the extracted maps, custom_maps, mods, load_order.toml, screenshots, crash reports and debug logs. The default profile, save and shader cache location is AppData/Roaming/halo on Windows and $XDG_DATA_HOME/halo-linux on Linux, usually ~/.local/share/halo-linux. If paths.saves or HALO_SAVE_ROOT overrides it, copy the configured location before an update.

references.title: Use the publisher’s Android release
references.instruction: On a 64-bit ARM device with Android 9 or newer, extract app-release.apk from halo-android-release.zip and install it with Android’s package installer. Start OpenCE and choose your own Halo Xbox ISO or XISO with the system picker. Allow about 2 GB for the extracted maps. The app handles its own updates. Before uninstalling, copy your maps and the save/u profiles from Android/data/com.halo.decomp/files. That app folder also contains config.toml and mods.

steps.instruction: The managed route retains its accepted v0.1.4 setup and data contract. For the current upstream Windows release, download the complete player from the official OpenPete page and prepare it in a separate writable folder. Compare the download with the checksum published there. Keep your existing working copy intact.

steps.title: Supply your own Spyro disc through upstream setup
steps.instruction: Use your own original Spyro the Dragon NTSC-U disc, SCUS-94228. Follow the current player’s first-run import instructions: it copies the disc into library and compiles game code alongside it. Keep the bundled compiler and runtime companions together. Save the completed Windows player’s launch details with that folder as its working directory, then choose Play separately. Portcove discovery does not run the compiler or import a disc automatically.

steps.title: Prepare the upstream Linux x86-64 AppImage
steps.instruction: Get the complete AppImage from the official OpenPete page and compare its SHA-256 there. Make it executable and run it on a system with glibc 2.31 or newer and Vulkan 1.2. If FUSE is unavailable, pass --appimage-extract-and-run. Supply your own NTSC-U Spyro disc as a BIN/CUE pair. OpenPete copies it into its private library before building the game, so a failed build can leave a copied disc entry. Keep your original and your existing working library separately.

warnings: Preserve your ordinary .mcr memory cards, settings, states, mods and the library folder before changing it. Keep the creating runtime with its generated code and states, and confirm your ordinary game saves in the new copy before retiring the old one.
This external copy has no Portcove-managed Update, Backup or Rollback; removing its registration preserves every file.

references.title: Keep progress and generated files with their working version
references.instruction: You or upstream update the separate current copy. Preserve your ordinary .mcr memory cards, settings, states, mods and the library folder before changing it. Keep the creating runtime with its generated code and states, and confirm your ordinary game saves in the new copy before retiring the old one. Use the corresponding paths if you have set XDG overrides.

listings.summary: Choose Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn or Dune 2000, then let OpenRA prepare the game content on first Play.

steps.title: Choose the game you want to play
steps.instruction: The Windows portable ZIP contains three different players: RedAlert.exe, TiberianDawn.exe and Dune2000.exe. The installer is an alternative; run it deliberately and select the installed player afterward. Server and utility tools are not game players.

steps.title: Finish content setup on first Play
steps.instruction: Choose Play explicitly to open that game’s own content screen. OpenRA can import your original media or offer its minimal content download; review that choice in OpenRA. No content installer or helper is started by discovery or by saving launch details.

steps.instruction: Choose the stable x86-64 AppImage named for Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn or Dune 2000. Keep server and utility commands for their separate tasks.

steps.instruction: Choose the official ARM64 Windows portable ZIP from a playtest release. Extract the whole ZIP and open RedAlert.exe, TiberianDawn.exe or Dune2000.exe from its own folder. The ARM64 package is a preview. Use the same OpenRA release as the other players if you play online.

steps.title: Use the OpenRA Flatpak on Linux
steps.instruction: Install net.openra.OpenRA from Flathub on Linux x64 or ARM64. Use the desktop launcher for Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn or Dune 2000 and finish content setup in that player. Back up the game’s Flatpak app data separately and update it through Flatpak. Use the official x64 AppImage if you need to switch between official and community mods outside the Flatpak sandbox.

steps.title: Choose the matching OpenRA application on Mac
steps.instruction: The stable upstream DMG contains a separate Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn and Dune 2000 application. The reviewed launchers include Intel and Apple Silicon. warnings: Keep settings, saves, maps, mods and content together, and retain a working copy when changing versions. These external files are outside Portcove backup and rollback.

references.instruction: OpenRA or you provide updates. Preserve the actual profile: normally %APPDATA%\OpenRA on Windows, ~/.config/openra on Linux, or ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRA on macOS. steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own legally obtained decrypted PS5 PPSA15552, content UP4016-PPSA15552_00-DEADCELLS0000000, version 01.000.000 / master 01.01 data: eboot.elf, sce_sys, sce_module, res.pak and the complete remaining game files. steps.instruction: Select deadcells.exe, set its complete prepared package folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact selected intent and request Play separately; use the upstream settings window/Play if shown. The selected launcher starts the prepared game child and waits for its normal exit. It can reprepare when originals, tools or preparation stamps change: finish such work outside the attached attempt first. Do not select a generated internal executable or relinker to bypass the supported entry. Normal waiting does not establish forced-stop quiescence or save flushing.

steps.title: Keep your prepared game and player data
steps.instruction: Keep the complete _sd save folder beside deadcells.exe, original game files, dc_runtime.exe and its matching generated metadata, shader caches, logs, configuration and any existing external paths. The original executable must remain available even after preparation. This guide performs no save conversion, migration, cleanup or backup; keep independent recovery copies.

steps.title: Separate component terms from the original game
steps.instruction: Retain the project GPLv2 notice, AnyPS5 and all library/component notices. These do not grant rights to the original Dead Cells: Return to Castlevania Edition executable, shaders or assets; use only a complete copy you are independently permitted to use. No other PS5 game or original PC edition is admitted by this title-specific route.

steps.title: Close the game before maintenance
steps.instruction: Quit the actual game normally and wait for the launcher to return before upstream replacement or data operations. Preserve independent recovery copies and review/relink changed executable bytes. Requirements and limits include Vulkan 1.1 with the documented depth-clip, BC texture and buffer-device-address features; upstream RTX 5070 Ti reports do not qualify other hardware. steps.title: Prepare the exact PSP title
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. Finish upstream preparation outside Portcove, keep independent originals and recovery copies. No original, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed by this guide. Use your own Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories PSP ULUS-10160 input targeted by the selected profile. No decryption, firmware, key or credential operation is authorized by this guide.

steps.title: Keep the complete Windows player
steps.instruction: The inspected official Windows ZIP contains AMD64 VCSNative/VCSNative.exe, VCSLauncher.exe and matching runtime libraries. Keep the complete VCSNative directory. The native program uses the generated Allegrex profile, linked PSP services and Vulkan graphics; native CPU output does not remove those system/graphics compatibility layers. Do not select a PSP executable, build helper, macOS application or settings launcher as the attached game.

steps.title: Add the player with its supported local files
steps.instruction: After upstream preparation, keep PSP_DATA beside VCSNative.exe with PSP_GAME/SYSDIR/EBOOT_DECRYPTED.ELF and complete PSP_GAME/USRDIR. Select VCSNative.exe, use the full VCSNative directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. Source discovers that package-local layout and runs the game on its native worker while the main thread services events until the worker finishes. A launcher-only remembered external path is not silently substituted for this direct route.

steps.title: Preserve all data roots and originals
steps.instruction: Keep VCSNative.ini, ProperShaders.ini, the full active save/profile/memory-stick data, textures, logs and PSP_DATA, plus any established external paths. Preserve complete package and separately configured save roots before replacement; the macOS Application Support path is not a Windows save-path claim. This guide does not migrate PSP saves or verify mission/save compatibility. Keep independent original data and do not treat a linked working tree as its backup.

steps.title: Keep optional packs and component grants separate
steps.instruction: Retain the PSPRecomp MIT notice and each profile/component notice, including separately credited graphics/mod components. Those do not license original game code/assets or third-party textures. The optional VCSTexturePack is a separate download and is not part of this guide; keep only existing components you are independently permitted to use. No pack is fetched, generated or executed here.

steps.title: Maintain upstream explicitly
steps.instruction: Quit the actual game normally before upstream replacement or data operations; forced termination is not a save-flush guarantee. Review/relink changed executable bytes. Source, package and upstream playability reports do not establish native gameplay, complete-game, save/reload, installed-app or Supported acceptance. Removing registration preserves external files; managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal remain unavailable. Upstream reports playable 60 FPS but less testing of missions/saves than opening areas. Windows Vulkan and macOS platform claims remain distinct; no full campaign or physical-client qualification is asserted.

listings.summary: Prepare Perimeter: Emperor's Testament through its upstream player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use the matching original game

steps.title: Prepare the Windows player
steps.instruction: The inspected 3.0.10 GitHub release inventory has no binary assets. Follow upstream INSTALL.eng.md to build the Windows player and its required DLLs, or use an already prepared working upstream player. Keep a private working game copy. Register perimeter.exe and retain its working directory. The upstream content override is one literal argument, content= followed by the absolute folder containing Resource and Scripts. Do not infer that the linked Legate Edition retail distribution includes both classic campaigns.

steps.title: Prepare the Linux player
steps.instruction: On a 64-bit Linux system with glibc 2.28 or later, use Perimeter Release x86_64 from a successful main-branch push on the official Linux Build workflow at https://github.com/KD-lab-Open-Source/Perimeter/actions/workflows/linux_build.yml. Unzip the download and unpack Perimeter.tar. Keep the perimeter executable beside libdxvk_d3d9.so and libsteam_api.so. steps.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=pst. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

steps.title: Keep your originals and game data
steps.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
steps.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/planescape-torment, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate planescape-torment.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. Back up the sandbox config and actual saves separately. To register the standalone x86-64 AppImage, allow the downloaded file to run and select the AppImage itself in Portcove. Choose your private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines, then review and save the selection. If the official AppImage reports that it cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run as the first separate argument. Keep -c and the config path on their own lines. Play starts the upstream player. For Flatpak, use the command above.

steps.instruction: Use the Mac Source Ports Universal 2 DMG at https://github.com/MacSourcePorts/MSPBuildSystem/releases/tag/GemRB_0.9.5. Its v0.9.5 build uses macOS 10.15 or later on Intel and macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon. GemRB’s SourceForge release directory also offers separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Keep the bundle complete. Use this game’s own configuration and point GamePath to the prepared original game folder. Keep this title’s saves, config and working data together when replacing the bundle. To register the Mac Source Ports bundle, copy the complete gemrb.app from the DMG and open it normally once. Select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb in Portcove. Choose your private working folder, then enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines. Review the selection and choose Play.

steps.title: Preserve the exact game original and separate BIOS
steps.instruction: Use your own unchanged Pokémon Emerald USA GBA original, SHA-1 f3ae088181bf583e55daf962a92bb46f4f1d07b7, and your own retail GBA system BIOS, 16384 bytes, SHA-1 300c20df6731a33952ded8c436f7f186d25d3492. Keep originals unchanged outside the new player folder and use matching private copies in a separate writable folder before upstream preparation; do not select the original archive as a writable save location. Other revisions, patched games, other regions or another Pokémon game are different inputs. Do not override an upstream mismatch warning or infer that a warning authenticates a file.

steps.title: Finish upstream setup and select this game player
steps.instruction: Open the linked official v0.1.3 release and extract its complete EmeraldRecomp-windows-x64-v0.1.3.zip package into a separate writable folder for this exact game. Keep EmeraldRecomp.exe, DLLs, assets, mods and overlay_toolchain companions together. Finish normal upstream BIOS/ROM selection using the matching private copies, then register the already working EmeraldRecomp.exe with its containing folder as working directory and preserve its already working literal arguments. The packaged tcc.exe and i386-win32-tcc.exe are compiler helpers, not game players. Keep the upstream PolyForm Noncommercial and dependency/attribution notices. These are in-development previews despite the release metadata flag; a package version is not gameplay qualification.

steps.title: Keep the data and compiler paths
steps.instruction: Before explicit Play, preserve the complete creating runtime and its actual data locations. The launcher writes config.ini/keybinds.ini and BIOS/ROM path caches; the runtime also has bios.cfg/rom.cfg sidecars. Default battery data sits beside the selected ROM as .sav, with .sav.tmp and .sav.prev-size.bak witnesses; save states use .state<N>, .suspend.state and .suspend.pending beside that ROM. Existing --save or --state-dir arguments change those coordinates: preserve their actual destinations and do not rewrite them through this guide. Generated reports and recomp_cache/JIT executable output belong to upstream; keep the full working player folder and actual ROM/data folder, not just the EXE or one save file. Close every game/compiler process before copying or replacing files. Do not share these folders between titles, transplant emulator/PokePort/another engine saves or states, or infer compatibility between builds.

steps.title: Use the upstream Linux AppImage
steps.instruction: Choose EmeraldRecomp-linux-x86_64 from the upstream releases page. The observed v0.1.5 player needs glibc 2.34 and libstdc++ providing GLIBCXX_3.4.30. Open it with the host’s AppImage support and use its own ROM and BIOS picker. Its launcher uses ~/.local/share/EmeraldRecomp by default, or EmeraldRecomp under XDG_DATA_HOME when set. EMERALDRECOMP_HOME overrides the complete path. Different AppImages can share that writable home. Back up that whole profile, the original files, and actual save and state locations before replacing the app.

steps.title: Import the separate ROM and BIOS in the Android app
steps.instruction: Use the official Android ARM64 APK. The observed v0.1.5 package requires Android 9 or later. In its setup screen choose your own USA Pokémon Emerald ROM and 16 KiB retail GBA BIOS separately. The app validates and copies them into its private roms and bios folders. Keep your original files separately. The app keeps its battery save under its private saves folder, and clearing app data or uninstalling can remove that save. Use a same-signed in-place update if you need to retain the app’s data and keep the creating version until you have verified actual recovery.

steps.title: Register the prepared player and use explicit Play
steps.instruction: You manage this external game, original files, compiler outputs and saved data. It saves the executable, working folder and launch arguments you select; choose Play explicitly when you are ready. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion for this copy. Finish first-time setup with the project’s tools. These instructions do not confirm successful original-game setup, gameplay, multiplayer, saving and loading or physical controls.

steps.title: Complete upstream preparation from your own P.T. copy
steps.instruction: Use your own P.T. PS4 US CUSA01127 dump folder or an already decrypted fake PKG made from that dump. An encrypted store PKG is not supported, and other regional data are not established as equivalent. Complete the upstream Windows setup into your chosen destination before adding the player. It copies chunk1.psarc, texture.qar and pathid_list_ps4.bin next to the port; eboot, modules and system files are not used. steps.title: Keep the complete installed or prepared Windows port
steps.instruction: The selected portable artifact is P.T.PC.Port-portable-windows.zip v1.0.8; its pt-port-20261022-484d2c1d folder contains pt.exe and companions, but still needs your prepared game data. Retain the full existing folder, libraries, resources, fonts, notices and game archives. Windows 10/11 x64 and the documented Vulkan/DirectX 12 graphics requirements apply. Original-game, project and each component/upscaling/font permission remain separate; no permission to redistribute private game data is inferred.

steps.title: Add the ordinary native game
steps.instruction: Select the prepared installation’s pt.exe, use its complete containing application folder as working directory and leave arguments empty when upstream setup has placed the three archives there. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready. An existing external-game route instead needs the same explicit --game "<existing extracted folder>" argument it already used. Preserve that route rather than moving original files. Do not select pt-updater.exe, the extractor, setup or a crash-dump helper as gameplay.

steps.title: Preserve the Windows data directory and overrides
steps.instruction: Keep the whole data/ beside pt.exe, including pt.ini, saves, logs, caches, mods and existing recovery/migration files as present, plus the complete application, prepared game archives and original dump. Preserve any existing --settings, --save-dir or --mods choices and their populated locations. Existing upstream user-data migration behavior is not a Portcove conversion or cross-build compatibility guarantee. Do not reset settings, replace newer state, move roots or turn on diagnostic/VR/rendering features merely to register the player.

steps.title: Keep maintenance and acceptance upstream
steps.instruction: The application can check for updates and use its own updater/restart path; upstream owns replacement, prerequisites and recovery. Quit the actual game and all helpers before maintenance, retain the previous complete runtime/data and review/select pt.exe after changes. Portcove observes the selected program only and removing the reference preserves all external files. Managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking and Supported qualification are unavailable. Upstream whole-teaser, controller and save reports are not Portcove native/gameplay or real-save observations.

steps.instruction: The inspected official v.0.1.1 Windows ZIP contains AMD64 PuyoPuyoBox_Recomp.exe as the preparation host with SDK/project resources and OpenBIOS. Do not attach the first-run setup host or RetComM hub and assume it represents the finished player. If the named native product is absent or generation/rebuild is still needed, finish upstream preparation before attachment; do not substitute a guessed executable.

steps.title: Keep your setup, game and memory-card paths
steps.instruction: Retain the complete upstream setup/project tree and build-release product, generated source/build metadata, staged game.toml/game_options.toml, settings.toml, bios/, disc files, mods/ and actual saves/memory-card paths. Source/runtime defaults use saves/, but existing per-slot/external card settings remain authoritative. Keep every previous product root and original CUE/BIN; rebuilds can replace the native program and restage support data. Cards, save states, netplay track/TOC identity and four-player settings have separate compatibility scope. This guide performs no import, conversion, backup, restore, migration or deletion.

steps.title: Check component licences and known limits
steps.instruction: The authoritative gitlinks are psxrecomp 17f49ad3b20dc30917a881a02baaa25374c13d18 (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0) and recomp-ui 655d77d5858aa677f88e7b19cd70460773a17476 (MIT), with OpenBIOS and other component notices retained. listings.name: Quake II / Q2rePRO
listings.summary: Set up the Q2rePRO engine with your own Quake II rerelease installation.
listings.download_block_reason: Use the publisher’s Windows nightly and the matching SDL dependency. For Linux, build from the pinned source.

steps.title: Prepare the Windows nightly
steps.instruction: On Windows x64, choose q2repro-rerelease-client_win64_x64.zip from the publisher. Use a separate writable engine folder and install the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. For the November 12, 2026 build, extract SDL3.dll from the official SDL 3.4.14 Windows x64 runtime ZIP at https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/tag/release-3.4.14 and place it beside q2repro.exe. Check a newer build’s requirements before replacing either file.

steps.title: Use your installed Quake II rerelease
steps.instruction: Run q2repro.exe from the extracted engine folder. It can discover an installed Quake II rerelease. Keep the complete original installation, with its rerelease PAK files and game DLL, in place. To add the Windows player to your Library, select q2repro.exe and use its own folder as the working directory.

steps.title: Build the Linux player
steps.instruction: Check out commit 9619f8e20a74dec67dff0b20eb8f34a3adf926da with its submodules. Follow BUILDING.md for Meson, a C and C++ toolchain, and the Linux dependencies. Install the build with Meson so it places the native game library in baseq2 under the configured library directory. For an uninstalled build, pass the absolute Meson build directory containing baseq2/game_x86_64.so with +set libdir. Use +set basedir with the folder containing the rerelease baseq2 directory and +set homedir with a separate writable profile. Keep the source installation intact.

warnings: On Windows in rerelease mode the engine uses the Windows Saved Games folder under NightDive Studios/Quake II. Back up that shared profile before switching engines. A separate executable folder does not isolate the profile.
The publisher marks native rerelease game-DLL multiplayer as unfinished. The nightly release can replace its ZIP in place.

steps.instruction: The Reckoning/xatrix and Ground Zero/rogue each need their own original pak/video and matching addon code; do not infer those from base-game setup. Keep complete original and prepared sets plus each compatible addon/runtime tuple recoverable. Engine/component terms do not grant rights to originals, music, mods or sibling renderer packages.

steps.title: Keep your working folder, data and profile choices
steps.instruction: Use the actual prepared runtime directory as working directory and retain established supported literal arguments, including actual -datadir, -cfgdir and -portable choices. The default Windows user root is actual Documents/YamagiQ2; -cfgdir changes its selected subdirectory and -portable omits that home-profile search. Do not force portable mode or rewrite a host root during registration. Preserve complete runtime/DLLs, baseq2 and other selected game directories, actual config/saves/screenshots/demos/music/mods/custom/legacy roots and unknowns. Finish upstream normal start/quit, review intent/consent and choose Play separately. No actual backward-save or addon compatibility is certified.

steps.instruction: Close every running copy before changing external files. You manage setup, game replacement, profile changes, data migration and recovery. Keep the working game version and every data folder, update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable before choosing Play. Portcove monitors only the process you selected and agreed to launch. It does not prevent other copies from running, restrict file access or take over unrelated helpers or replacement processes. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or deletion.

listings.name: Shadow Warrior (Raze)
listings.summary: Play Shadow Warrior in Raze using your own original PC game files.

steps.title: Use your recognized original game files
steps.instruction: Use your own 1997 PC Shadow Warrior data folder, anchored by SW.GRP. Keep its accompanying files and any separately owned expansion data. The 2013 reboot is a different game. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini, or in raze_portable.ini for the Portcove-managed Windows player; do not copy game files into the managed player folder, because Portcove verifies that folder. Elsewhere, you may instead place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

steps.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
steps.instruction: On Windows, choose Install, then Play explicitly. Portcove downloads and verifies the official Windows ZIP, keeps the player folder together, and creates Raze’s portable configuration marker so its configuration, saves, screenshots and demos stay beside the managed player, where Portcove preserves them across updates. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your SW.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
steps.instruction: On Windows, Portcove replaces the managed runtime and preserves its declared data. A separate existing Windows copy stays yours: registering it preserves every external file and Portcove does not manage its Update, Backup or Rollback, and the normal-profile settings described below are not imported into a managed install. Elsewhere, you and upstream replace this external player. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. A native Linux build outside Flatpak uses its own profile, usually ~/.config/raze. Preserve that profile and any older ~/.raze directory before launching a replacement.

steps.title: Use Raze from Flathub on Linux
steps.instruction: Install org.zdoom.Raze from Flathub for Linux x64 or ARM64. Make sure ~/.config exists in your home directory. Keep your original files and place a complete working copy of this game's data in its own subfolder under ~/.var/app/org.zdoom.Raze/.config/raze. Open Raze and choose this game if a picker appears. Close Raze and back up its actual configuration, saves and mods before updating through Flatpak.

steps.title: Keep the correct player and profile
steps.instruction: The managed player follows the Rolling latest build; this channel does not establish gameplay qualification. On Windows, the managed copy selects openjk_sp.x86_64.exe for single player. Multiplayer remains available by registering your separately prepared openjk.x86_64.exe copy with its actual GameData working folder; openjkded.x86_64.exe is a server. This selected Windows package contains the non-portable home-directory branch: normal saves, configuration and logs use the actual Documents/My Games/OpenJK profile. Back it up separately with your originals and creating runtime before changing versions. Portable builds, unavailable Documents folders and explicit home-path overrides can change the write location; those configurations need their own preserved external registration. A runtime rollback does not rewind external saves or establish older-runtime, mod or recorded-demo compatibility.

steps.title: Keep an existing prepared copy
steps.instruction: Extract the complete official OpenJK-windows-x86_64.zip into the prepared GameData folder. Select openjk_sp.x86_64.exe for single player or openjk.x86_64.exe for multiplayer, with GameData as working directory. A registration selects one player/mode; openjkded.x86_64.exe is a dedicated server, not the player. Retain all package libraries/resources. Existing registrations keep their selected player/mode, arguments, files and user/upstream runtime owner. Removing their registration preserves those files; this catalog change does not adopt or migrate them.

steps.title: Prepare the multiplayer player
steps.instruction: Use a separately prepared external GameData copy with the complete official Windows x64 package and your own matching assets0.pk3 through assets3.pk3 in base. Keep the package's base and OpenJK libraries intact; do not copy old game DLLs over them. Select openjk.x86_64.exe with that GameData folder as working directory, not the single-player executable or dedicated server. This player also needs a compatible Microsoft Visual C++ v14 x64 runtime; the x86 runtime alone is insufficient. For the documented software-audio route, enter +set, s_UseOpenAL and 0 on three separate argument lines. Each line is one literal argument. The bundled legacy OpenAL/EAX DLLs are 32-bit and are not x64 dependencies for this route.

steps.title: Choose one installation route
steps.instruction: A library can have only one installation or registration for this title at a time. Choose managed single player or a separately prepared external player; do not register files inside a Portcove-managed installation or output folder. Preserve your originals, complete external profile and creating runtime before changing routes, then use the existing removal choice first. Registration-only removal preserves all external files. The external multiplayer route offers reviewed registration, separate Play and preserving registration removal, not managed installation, updates, backup, rollback, migration or deletion of that copy. Existing managed single-player installations and retained registrations keep their own contracts.

steps.title: Prepare the upstream Mac player
steps.instruction: Unpack the official OpenJK Mac tarball for your Mac with the system archive tools. Keep the app and its required game data in the matching Jedi Academy GameData layout. Open openjk_sp.arm64.app or openjk_sp.x86_64.app for the campaign. Use openjk.arm64.app or openjk.x86_64.app for multiplayer. Keep the complete app, including libSDL2-2.0.0.dylib in Contents/Frameworks and follow the project’s data setup instructions. The inspected packages require macOS 14 or later on Intel and macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon.

steps.title: Prepare the Linux OpenJK campaign profile
steps.instruction: Put the original archives in $XDG_DATA_HOME/openjk/base when XDG_DATA_HOME is set to an absolute path. Otherwise, with XDG_DATA_HOME unset, use ~/.local/share/openjk/base. Use only assets0.pk3 through assets3.pk3 from your own patched PC GameData/base. The inspected official build requires glibc 2.34, libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.29, SDL2, zlib, libjpeg.so.8, libpng16.so.16 and libOpenGL.so.0.

warnings: Keep the external working GameData copy and its originals too. Upstream or you replace this multiplayer runtime. Server downloads and mods are not Portcove-managed runtime updates, and existing demos, mods, saves or server compatibility are not guaranteed after replacement.

Keep the Unix profile and original archives outside the Portcove library and back them up separately. Use a separately prepared copy for profiles with alternate native modules. Managed runtime replacement and rollback leave this external data in place.

references.title: Keep multiplayer profiles and downloads
references.instruction: Preserve the complete actual OpenJK profile, including base and each mod's directory, openjk.cfg, logs, screenshots, recorded demos and server-downloaded packages or unfinished downloads. The selected non-portable Windows build normally uses Documents/My Games/OpenJK; fs_homepath overrides, portable builds or an unavailable Documents folder can change the location. Keep the external working GameData copy and its originals too. Upstream or you replace this multiplayer runtime. Server downloads and mods are not Portcove-managed runtime updates, and existing demos, mods, saves or server compatibility are not guaranteed after replacement. Preserve the actual Linux OpenJK profile at $XDG_DATA_HOME/openjk or ~/.local/share/openjk, or ~/Library/Application Support/OpenJK on Mac. Keep any explicit fs_homepath, original data, mods and the creating runtime. The upstream apps can share a profile location.
