listings.name: Starship
listings.summary: Native Star Fox 64 port from HarbourMasters.

steps.title: Download from the official Starship project
steps.instruction: Use HarbourMasters/Starship on GitHub, open its v2.0.0 release and download Starship-Barnard-Alfa-Windows.zip. Extract every file into a new folder outside your Portcove library. Keep existing originals, installations and saves in place.

steps.title: Prepare the supported Star Fox 64 original
steps.instruction: Supply your own Star Fox 64 US 1.0 or US 1.1 Rev A original in .z64 format. JP and EU originals can supply optional voices with a US base; they cannot create the base game. Follow upstream’s conversion instructions if your dump is .n64 or .v64, keeping the original unchanged. Portcove registration does not validate or authenticate these original files.

steps.title: Complete upstream setup before adding the game
steps.instruction: Open Starship.exe from the extracted folder and select the supported US .z64 original in the upstream file picker. Let it generate sf64.o2r. Keep that generated file, the separate shipped starship.o2r and all other package files in the game folder. A ROM launch argument or the shipped starship.o2r alone does not finish preparation. Close the game normally before registration.

steps.title: Select the prepared game in Portcove
steps.instruction: Open this game’s Files tab, expand Use an existing installation · Installation options, then choose Use an existing installation. Choose game executable and select Starship.exe from the prepared folder. Set Start in folder to that folder and leave launch arguments empty. Review launch details and confirm the registration, then choose Play. Selecting this executable records your intent to run it; it does not authenticate it as an official publisher package.

warnings: Portcove cannot automatically install the v2.0.0 Windows package because the expected download check is missing. Choosing Starship.exe yourself does not confirm who published it.

If the game crashes with DirectX 11, upstream documents switching to OpenGL through Settings or starship.cfg.json, then restarting. Preserve the configuration before editing it. This guide covers Windows; it does not qualify other platforms.

references.title: Download check
references.instruction: The inspected v2.0.0 release metadata did not publish a SHA-256 for Starship-Barnard-Alfa-Windows.zip. A locally calculated hash identifies the file but does not confirm who published it.

references.title: Updates and backups
references.instruction: Use the project’s tools to update this copy. Close the game and helpers, preserve the whole working folder including sf64.o2r, mods, saves, starship.cfg.json and any legacy config.json, then prepare an update separately before changing launch details. Portcove offers launch and registration removal; it does not offer managed updates, backups, rollback, migration or deletion for these external files. Removing the registration preserves them. steps.title: Supply the matching original game files
steps.instruction: Supply STRIFE1.WAD from your original PC commercial Strife updated to at least v1.2; the Veteran Edition includes that data. The original demo is unsupported and v1.1 has known issues. Keep VOICES.WAD beside STRIFE1.WAD for speech; do not add it with -file. Keep your originals and edition identity; renaming another game’s WAD does not convert it. Originals are not included or authenticated by Portcove. Use a recognized upstream installation, or deliberately copy matching files into the originals subfolder (named exactly originals) of this entry’s fresh private data folder; keep your original copies.

steps.title: Use the upstream setup and launch controls
steps.instruction: Play opens crispy-strife-setup.exe. Configure controls and use F2 Warp for single-player launch; choose the matching detected IWAD there. The main-menu launch command forwards its existing arguments. The PWAD/mod browser is not an original-IWAD browser. Keep different title entries separate. Do not switch this entry’s original edition in place: its retained runtime versions share data. Use a separate Portcove library or independently owned upstream copy for another source variant. No automatic switching or cross-variant save compatibility is established. An upstream setup exit does not establish that the game loaded or ran successfully.

steps.title: Keep the game’s listed local data
steps.instruction: Portcove retains originals deliberately copied under originals, this entry’s default configuration, saves under saves, known default save locations, numbered screenshots and declared recording files. Put custom recordings under demos or use a demo-prefixed .lmp filename. Upstream may read and write its music-pack profile on Play. Music packs and custom paths outside this installation remain external and outside Portcove backups. Extra files written inside the installation outside its declared folders are outside this offered scope and can block maintenance. Keep the creating runtime, original files and actual data before changing a source variant or using an older runtime.

steps.title: Keep updates in one place
steps.instruction: Portcove manages this new official game installation and the data listed for it. It does not import an existing project profile or convert a separately registered game. Existing registered copies keep their external files and update tools. Back up those external profiles and original files separately. Automated fixture checks and reaching a setup menu do not establish original-file or gameplay compatibility.

warnings: Play opens the project’s setup and launch controls. Supply your own matching original game files that you are permitted to use.
Core backups exclude external music packs, custom paths and registered external-player data.

references.title: Install the native package on Linux or Mac
references.instruction: On Debian 13, install the crispy-doom package through the package manager. On other Linux versions, check that the package includes crispy-strife or use the upstream build instructions. On Mac, use the upstream-documented MacPorts port or a supported Homebrew formula. Start crispy-strife with -iwad followed by the quoted path to your own STRIFE1.WAD from retail Strife v1.2 or newer. Keep VOICES.WAD beside STRIFE1.WAD for speech. Use the external package manager for replacement.

references.title: Keep the existing Crispy profile

warnings: Use your permitted upstream copy under its applicable conditions. Keep both the older working folder and current user profile backed up before first Play.

references.title: Keep your runtime and data recoverable

steps.title: Choose a fresh managed runtime or keep your external player
steps.instruction: For a fresh Portcove-managed runtime, use Install and then explicit Play. Keep the ordinary upstream launcher: choose this entry’s exact game/version and its complete matching original-data folder there. No automatic title dispatch or original authentication by Core is promised. The managed definition passes four separate literal arguments, -datadir, ., -cfgdir, ., with the actual player's parent folder as working directory (reflectionhle.exe on Windows, reflectionhle on Linux). On Mac, the official universal app runs with the same arguments from the folder containing reflectionhle.app. Upstream creates its version-specific writable directories after accepting the originals; no setup marker or helper is fabricated. For your separate existing external player, keep the original upstream route: Extract the official Windows 64-bit ZIP and keep reflectionhle.exe, SDL3.dll and libspeexdsp-1.dll together. Select reflectionhle.exe inside its wrapper folder and use that same folder as the working directory. Leave launch arguments empty to use the game/version picker. steps.title: Preserve the shared profile and each game version
steps.instruction: Windows normally stores ReflectionHLE settings and per-version writable data beneath %APPDATA%/reflectionhle. Preserve that whole profile, your original game folders and any custom data/config/mod locations with all copies closed before changing runtimes. Several game entries share settings; version-specific writable folders remain distinct. Changing a data/config argument redirects storage and does not migrate it. Retain the working runtime for existing saves; no cross-version or cross-engine save compatibility is established.

steps.title: Keep new private progress separate from old profiles
steps.instruction: The fresh managed runtime stores ReflectionHLE configuration, controller mappings, original-location references and per-version progress in the declared paths beside the player on Windows and Linux, or beside the app bundle on Mac. It imports no AppData, DOS or existing-player saves/configuration and adopts no populated external folder. Core manages that separate runtime and its declared data through the existing install/update, retained-runtime, backup/recovery and reviewed removal contracts. Keep originals and every external profile outside it unchanged. Existing user-selected registrations retain their creating runtime and old external ownership; they are not converted by this offer. Runtime rollback does not certify save compatibility. Preserve the creating runtime and actual progress before older-version use. Customized original/data/config argument overrides require separate upstream/external handling.

warnings: The ordinary upstream launcher still requires explicit matching game/version/original-folder selection. Fixed -gamever skips that picker and is not used.

This new installation does not import existing saves from external copies or the original DOS game. Save compatibility has not been confirmed. Keep those saves and the game versions that created them separately.
Matching original game files are required to play and are not included. Existing saves are not imported, and compatibility with saves from other versions has not been confirmed.

steps.title: Keep the matching original

steps.title: Play or replace your working game
steps.instruction: After adding your Windows or Linux game, choose Play. Use upstream tools to replace the game or manage its saves. Removing the Portcove registration leaves the game and data in place. Close the game and its updater before replacing files.

steps.title: Open the Linux or Steam Deck game
steps.instruction: Unpack the complete x64 Linux ZIP and run sm64coopdx from that folder so it can find its bundled libraries. references.title: Keep the game version and data you use

On Windows the upstream default checks %APPDATA%/sm64coopdx and can instead reuse a populated %APPDATA%/sm64ex-coop folder; an existing --savepath override changes that selection. Preserve both relevant roots and the actual selected path, copied ROM, saves, configuration, mods and caches. A new executable folder does not isolate these profiles. Do not change the path, adopt populated legacy data, add mods or migrate profiles through this guide. Upstream can start its own updater and successor process; close all game/updater windows and confirm they stopped before copying or replacing files.

references.title: Find your Linux or Mac profile

The game can reuse a populated sm64ex-coop folder when sm64coopdx is empty. Preserve the actual folder with your original copy, saves, mods and settings. listings.name: Surge the Rabbit
listings.summary: Play a retro platformer and build your own levels with the Open Surge engine.

steps.title: Install through Portcove on Windows
steps.instruction: Install the publisher’s portable game and choose Play on a 64-bit Windows PC. Portcove backs up the bundled game’s preferences, captures and levels stored in its managed data folder. Keep separate backups for custom projects you open from other folders.

steps.title: Install an upstream copy
steps.instruction: On Windows, extract the entire publisher ZIP into a folder you can write to and open opensurge.exe. The package includes the game and uses a 32-bit Windows executable. On Linux, install Open Surge from your distribution or install Surge Engine from Flathub for x86-64 or ARM64.

steps.title: Start the bundled adventure
steps.instruction: Choose Start Game from the Surge the Rabbit title screen. The package already includes the levels and other game files. No separate game data is needed.

steps.title: Keep your settings and creations
steps.instruction: Close the game before copying your files. For a manually extracted Windows copy, back up the extracted game folder. On Linux, copy the Surge the Rabbit folder under ~/.local/share/opensurge, or use the matching path under XDG_DATA_HOME if you set it. For Flatpak, look under ~/.var/app/org.opensurge2d.OpenSurge/data/opensurge. If you set OPENSURGE_USER_PATH, copy the folder it points to for your player data. Also keep any separate folders you use for your own games or levels.

warnings: For a Windows installation managed by Portcove, choose a library folder using basic Latin characters. Open Surge 0.6.1.3 can write preferences and saves in a different folder when the library path contains other characters.

references.title: Get the publisher’s Android build
references.instruction: The publisher offers an Android APK for ARM64 and 32-bit ARM in the release downloads. Keep your own copies of any projects you import. The Android app stores its active data in its own app storage.

listings.name: Hexen II / uHexen2 Tweaked
listings.summary: Play Hexen II with the upstream Tweaked OpenGL player and your prepared original game files.

steps.title: Copy your original game data before Play
steps.instruction: Copy pak0.pak and pak1.pak from your own retail Hexen II installation, patched to version 1.11, into the data1 folder of the game folder you will play from, and keep your original installation separately. The engine refuses older or mixed pak versions; nothing patches them for you, and the package contains no game data or patching tools.

steps.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
steps.instruction: Extract the complete Windows test ZIP into a separate working Hexen II folder that already holds data1. Select glh2.exe with that folder, then choose Play. This is a Win32 OpenGL Hexen II preview, not HexenWorld.

warnings: The test package bundles ten third-party codec and runtime DLLs without their licence notices. Portcove downloads the package only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.

references.instruction: On Linux x86-64, build the test-1 tag from engine/hexen2 with make DEMO=1 h2 and the SDL 1.2, ALSA, libmad and Vorbis development libraries. listings.name: Teeworlds
listings.summary: Swing through 2D arenas, play local and online matches, and create your own maps.
listings.download_block_reason: Choose a download from the Teeworlds project or install the game through your package manager.

steps.title: Add the Windows client to Portcove
steps.instruction: After extracting the complete official Windows x64 ZIP, select teeworlds.exe and its containing folder. Keep the data folder and the accompanying files together. Leave launch options empty, review the details, and add the game. Choose Play separately. teeworlds_srv.exe is the dedicated server, not the client.

steps.title: Add the Linux client to Portcove
steps.instruction: Select the teeworlds client from your complete Linux x64 package and use its containing folder as the start folder. A distribution package normally installs it at /usr/games/teeworlds; install its data package and dependencies through the same package manager. Leave launch options empty. Update the installation through upstream or your package manager. The separate community Flathub client is available on Linux x64 and ARM64; install and update that copy through Flatpak rather than selecting a Flatpak launcher as a native executable.

steps.title: Add the Intel Mac client to Portcove
steps.instruction: Copy the complete Teeworlds.app from the publisher disk image into Applications and open it normally once. In Portcove, select /Applications/Teeworlds.app/Contents/MacOS/teeworlds, use its containing folder as the start folder, and leave launch options empty. Keep the complete app bundle together. Teeworlds Server.app is a separate dedicated server. The later teeworlds.exe choice applies to Windows; Mac uses the native file inside Teeworlds.app. The bundled 0.7.5 Intel runtime requires macOS 10.13 or later; Portcove has its own system requirements.

steps.title: Play and record a match
steps.instruction: The Teeworlds 0.7 client connects to Teeworlds 0.7 servers. In a match, press F1 and enter record followed by a demo name. Enter stoprecord to finish, then open the recording from Demos.

steps.title: Select the prepared player
steps.instruction: Select teeworlds.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

warnings: Before moving your setup, close the game and copy the data folder with settings07.cfg, demos, custom maps, and any skins you want to keep.

references.title: Find your data folder
references.instruction: The defaults are %APPDATA%/Teeworlds on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Teeworlds on Mac, and ~/.local/share/teeworlds on Linux. On Linux, the game prefers an existing ~/.teeworlds folder or uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/teeworlds if XDG_DATA_HOME is set. For the Flathub installation, check ~/.var/app/com.teeworlds.Teeworlds/.teeworlds. If you changed storage.cfg, use its save location.

references.title: Registration ownership and removal
references.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

references.title: Player-data ownership
references.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: Windows %APPDATA%/Teeworlds settings07.cfg, demos, maps and skins; Linux ~/.local/share/teeworlds, existing ~/.teeworlds or $XDG_DATA_HOME/teeworlds; Intel Mac ~/Library/Application Support/Teeworlds and any storage.cfg save path; the save location selected by storage.cfg, and any custom maps or skins kept with the installation. listings.original_game_title: Ultima VII Part Two: Serpent Isle

source_editions.title: Ultima VII Part Two: Serpent Isle (PC)

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use your installed original Serpent Isle data, especially its complete STATIC folder. Silver Seed is optional and remains a separately owned add-on. Black Gate data does not supply Serpent Isle. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: Choose the official Windows installer from Exult’s download page, or keep a complete upstream-prepared player with its runtime data. Configure this installed game’s path in Exult, keeping Black Gate and Serpent Isle entries distinct. On Windows, register exult.exe with its installation folder as working directory, using the upstream game picker or the documented single argument --si. Do not register Exult Studio or a usecode/compiler helper as the player.

steps.title: Set up the upstream Linux package
steps.instruction: Install info.exult.exult from Flathub and open it once to create its sandbox folders. Put this game’s own STATIC directory in ~/.var/app/info.exult.exult/data/serpentisle or configure the actual working path. Preserve the sandbox config, serpentisle data, saves and gamedat. A native non-Flatpak Exult uses a separate profile, normally ~/.exult.cfg and ~/.exult/serpentisle. On Linux x86-64, install the Ubuntu 26.04 exult package; version 1.12.1 was checked. Prepare this game’s configuration with that package first. Select /usr/lib/games/exult/exult and a private working folder. Do not select the packaged exult launcher script, because it can split arguments that contain spaces. Enter -c, the absolute path to your prepared configuration, and --si on separate argument lines. Start Flatpak copies through their upstream route.

steps.title: Prepare the official Mac app
steps.instruction: Use Exult’s official Intel/Apple Silicon DMG. Keep the complete app and point it to your own Serpent Isle installation. The documented default original folder is /Library/Application Support/Exult/serpentisle. Back up ~/Library/Preferences/exult.cfg, ~/Library/Application Support/exult/serpentisle, and every custom savegame, gamedat and mod location before replacing the app. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac, keep the official Exult.app intact and select Contents/MacOS/exult and its containing folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to your prepared Exult configuration as separate arguments, followed by --si. Use the configuration for the matching original and preserve its actual save and gamedat locations before changing players.

steps.title: Import this edition in the Android launcher
steps.instruction: Choose the official Android APK under the stable release on Exult’s download page and check its Android version requirement. Zip your own Serpent Isle STATIC folder and its contents, then choose the matching game in the upstream launcher and select that ZIP. Exult installs the files in its app-private serpentisle/static directory. Keep your original ZIP separately. It does not contain Exult’s settings or saves. Use an in-place update from the same signer and keep the app data intact unless you have a verified backup of the actual profile.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

warnings: Preserve the complete Exult profile and each game/mod’s configured savegame and gamedat locations, including any path overrides and original STATIC data.
Close all copies before upstream updates; preserve the creating runtime until its game/mod saves work in a replacement.
These sibling routes use upstream setup, launch and replacement. Keep the creating runtime and actual player files recoverable before changing versions.

references.title: Keep your originals and game data
references.instruction: On current Windows, exult.cfg normally lives under the actual Local AppData/Exult folder. Preserve the complete Exult profile and each game/mod’s configured savegame and gamedat locations, including any path overrides and original STATIC data. Keep optional add-ons separate from base-game choices. Close all copies before upstream updates; preserve the creating runtime until its game/mod saves work in a replacement.

references.title: Set up this edition on iPhone or iPad
references.instruction: Use Exult’s TestFlight build if you receive an invitation, or build the pinned 1.12.1 source yourself in Xcode for iOS or iPadOS 13 or later. Prepare a game folder with your own Serpent Isle files under game/serpentisle/static. Use lowercase for every file and folder name, then copy the complete game folder into the app with Finder or iTunes file sharing. Keep the app’s Documents folder, including its settings, saves and autosaves, before changing the app. The iOS guide is at https://exult.info/docs.html#iOS-Guide.

listings.name: Doom / UZDoom (UZDoom)
listings.summary: Choose your own Doom-family game data and mods in UZDoom; the upstream launcher provides runtime updates.

steps.title: Use the upstream-owned player
steps.instruction: On Windows, extract the complete official x64 archive into a separate folder. Choose uzdoom.exe with that folder as its working directory and save launch details, then choose Play deliberately. updater.exe is the upstream runtime replacement helper, not the player to register.

steps.title: Choose your game data
steps.instruction: Use the launcher to select your own supported IWAD or compatible free game data. Keep mods and game data under the upstream documented setup. Adding launch details does not start a game; choose Play separately.

steps.title: Register your prepared Windows player
steps.instruction: Complete the upstream setup in your permitted working copy first. Select the actual uzdoom.exe and its containing folder as the working directory; keep all companions. Normally leave arguments empty. Enter separate literal arguments only when deliberately following documented options. Confirm the selected player, folder and arguments; registration does not start a game. Choose Play separately when ready.

steps.title: Register your Linux x86-64 AppImage
steps.instruction: Keep the full official AppImage in a folder outside your Portcove library. Make it executable and open it with AppImage support to finish upstream setup. The player needs glibc 2.34 or newer. Select the AppImage itself and its containing folder. Leave arguments empty for the IWAD chooser, or supply documented options as separate arguments. Confirm the selection and choose Play separately.

warnings: Portcove tracks the player you selected. On Windows, if UZDoom’s error window restarts it, the new player can keep running after Portcove reports the original process finished. Close any remaining UZDoom players before choosing Play again or updating files. Removing the registration does not confirm that restarted players have stopped and leaves every external file untouched.

Keep that runtime ownership with upstream. Portcove leaves these external files untouched and offers no managed Update, Backup or Rollback promise for them. Before changing versions, close the game and back up your actual IWADs, mods and configured save paths.
Custom config/save overrides and relocated Windows user folders need their own backup. Keep the working copy recoverable; upstream update_backup is not a Portcove-verified player-data backup.
Close all actual players and preserve the working copy and every actual data location before upstream changes.
Managed Install, Update, Backup, Rollback, migration, original authentication and external deletion are unavailable for this route.

references.title: Update through upstream
references.instruction: UZDoom’s launcher checks for updates and can use updater.exe to replace package files. Keep that runtime ownership with upstream. Portcove leaves these external files untouched and offers no managed Update, Backup or Rollback promise for them. Before changing versions, close the game and back up your actual IWADs, mods and configured save paths. Windows normally stores uzdoom.ini under Documents/My Games/UZDoom and saves under the Windows Saved Games/UZDoom folder. Portable mode uses uzdoom_portable.ini and the local Save and Screenshots folders. Custom config/save overrides and relocated Windows user folders need their own backup. Keep the working copy recoverable; upstream update_backup is not a Portcove-verified player-data backup.

references.title: Keep your Linux or Mac files
references.instruction: On Linux, keep configuration in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/uzdoom (default ~/.config/uzdoom) and saves under $XDG_DATA_HOME/games/uzdoom/savegames (default ~/.local/share/games/uzdoom/savegames). Screenshots have a separate Pictures location. On Apple Silicon with macOS 12 or newer, copy the complete UZDoom.app from the official ARM64 DMG to Applications and open it through macOS. Preserve ~/Library/Preferences/uzdoom.ini and ~/Documents/UZDoom.

listings.name: Vagrant Story (PlayStation) (rood-boi)
listings.summary: A playable but unfinished Vagrant Story implementation according to the project. Unimplemented paths stop explicitly, and a complete playthrough is unconfirmed. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

listings.name: VCMI
listings.summary: Open-source Heroes III engine. Portcove can manage the official Windows x64 engine while you import your own game data with the upstream launcher. The shared profile remains yours.
listings.original_game_title: Heroes of Might and Magic III

steps.title: Install VCMI on Windows or Mac
steps.instruction: On Windows x64, extract the portable ZIP or run the x64 installer, then open VCMI_launcher.exe. On Windows ARM64, run the official VCMI-Windows-arm64.exe installer and open VCMI Launcher from the Start menu. Update that copy through the upstream installer. On Mac, choose the Intel or Apple Silicon DMG, copy VCMI.app to Applications and use its launcher.

steps.title: Run the VCMI AppImage on Linux
steps.instruction: Choose VCMI-Linux-x64.AppImage for x86-64 or VCMI-Linux-arm64.AppImage for ARM64 from the official release. Make the full AppImage executable and open it on a system with glibc 2.38 or newer and AppImage support. Use its built-in launcher to import your Heroes III data. If you use a distribution package or Flatpak instead, follow the upstream Linux guide and update through that package manager.

steps.title: Import your Heroes III data
steps.instruction: In VCMI Launcher, import your GOG offline installer with its matching BIN file, or use a supported Heroes III Complete or Shadow of Death installation. Keep the launcher for data import and optional mods.

steps.title: Choose the client after upstream setup
steps.instruction: To register an upstream copy on Windows x64, select VCMI_client.exe and its containing folder. On Linux x64, use the native vcmiclient executable and its containing folder for a distribution package. Play through the upstream launcher on Windows ARM64 or when using an AppImage, Flatpak or Mac app.

warnings: Heroes III Restoration of Erathia and the HD Edition are not supported; use Complete or Shadow of Death game data.
VCMI saves from different major versions are usually incompatible. Finish ongoing games or keep your current runtime and a profile backup before changing major versions.
Windows game data, saves and settings normally live in Documents/My Games/vcmi; keep that profile when updating the upstream runtime.

references.title: Preserve the profile for your installation
references.instruction: Windows normally uses Documents/My Games/vcmi. Mac uses ~/Library/Application Support/vcmi. Linux normally uses ~/.local/share/vcmi, or ~/.var/app/eu.vcmi.VCMI/data/vcmi for Flatpak. Keep the actual data and settings folders, including any custom profile paths, when changing versions.

references.title: Linux setup guide
references.instruction: https://vcmi.eu/players/Installation_Linux/

references.title: Upstream Android setup
references.instruction: Use the official Android setup guide for Google Play, F-Droid or the matching upstream APK (ARM64, ARMv7 or x86-64). Import your own Heroes III data in the app and keep your originals separately. Install and update through the same channel because Android checks package identity and signing. Preserve the app profile before removing it. Android guide at https://vcmi.eu/players/Installation_Android/.

references.title: Upstream iPhone and iPad setup
references.instruction: Check the upstream iOS guide for the current system requirements. Use VCMI’s upstream TestFlight route when available, or provision the official IPA yourself through the upstream sideloading guide. In VCMI Launcher, select your owned Heroes III Complete GOG installer EXE and its matching BIN. Alternatively, copy owned Complete or Shadow of Death Data and Maps, plus optional Mp3, into the VCMI folder in Files. Keep the app’s Documents folder, including Saves and config, before changing its channel or identity. iOS guide at https://vcmi.eu/players/Installation_iOS/.

listings.name: Shantae / shantaerecomp (vibecodekun)
listings.summary: Play the Shantae recompilation with your own exact USA Game Boy Color ROM.

steps.title: Choose your original ROM on first start
steps.instruction: Start the game and pick your own exact Shantae USA Game Boy Color ROM in its chooser: SHA-256 1b92e22d5510c51bab97d23074e4aad7464d93eb15f7596ef7da0a5efa27a19d, CRC32 E994B59B. World, Switch and Limited Run Games releases are different ROMs. The chooser enables Play only for the accepted original and remembers its path in rom.cfg, so keep the ROM where it is.

steps.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
steps.instruction: Keep the complete package for your system together with its libraries, assets, shaders and notices, and start shantae.exe on Windows or shantae on Linux from its own folder with no arguments. Return to Launcher closes the game and starts the same program again.

warnings: The project uses the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0; observe its noncommercial terms. The package includes recompiled game code without a licence grant, an unlicensed gbrecompiled engine fork, shaders under their own licences, and the Lato, Noto Sans Symbols 2 and OpenMoji fonts under the OFL and CC BY-SA licences. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.
Save and save-state compatibility is specific to this build; do not assume another gbrecompiled game or version can read them. Portcove has not observed native setup, gameplay or saves.

references.title: Keep the game folder's data
references.instruction: By default the game keeps rom.cfg, keybinds.ini, runtime_prefs.ini, imgui.ini, shantae.ini, the shantae.sav battery save, shantae.state1 to shantae.state10, shader_presets and shader_cache beside the program; GBRECOMP_STATE_DIR moves them elsewhere. In a copy you manage yourself, back these up before replacing the program.

listings.name: Banjo-Tooie / Banjo-Tooie: Recompiled (Vidanox)
listings.summary: Use the Banjo-Tooie player package and select your own USA cartridge dump.

steps.title: Choose your original cartridge dump on first Play
steps.instruction: Choose Play, then Select ROM and supply your own Banjo-Tooie USA 32 MiB cartridge dump. The project recommends an unmodified big-endian .z64; the player also converts byteswapped dumps of the same cartridge. Another region or a modified image is not accepted. The player checks the file and keeps its own copy in its profile, so keep your original separately.

steps.title: Keep the complete player package
steps.instruction: For a copy you manage yourself, extract the whole package. On Windows, run BanjoTooieRecompiled.exe with assets and the supplied SDL2 and DXC libraries beside it. On Linux, run run.sh, or start BanjoTooieRecompiled with its extracted folder as the working folder.

warnings: Upstream calls Linux less exercised than Windows. Portcove has not observed native setup, gameplay or saves. On Linux the player needs Vulkan, SDL2, FreeType, D-Bus and a running xdg-desktop-portal service for Select ROM.

The package includes the Suplexmentary Comic NC font, which the project license does not cover, and menu art based on Rare's promotional artwork. Portcove downloads the package only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.

references.title: Keep your actual profile when updating
references.instruction: Preserve the player's profile before replacing a copy you manage yourself: normally %LOCALAPPDATA%\BanjoTooieRecompiled on Windows or ~/.config/BanjoTooieRecompiled on Linux. It holds the copied original bt.n64.us.1.0.z64, saves, settings and mods. For Flatpak, keep the complete ~/.var/app/io.github.Vidanox.BanjoTooieRecompiled folder, and keep any APP_FOLDER_PATH or portable.txt folder you actually used. Keep a working copy before replacing the player.

listings.name: Vyruz: Destruction of the Untel Empire (OpenVyruz)
listings.summary: A native engine for Vyruz using the original game data from your own copy.
listings.original_game_title: Vyruz: Destruction of the Untel Empire

steps.title: Select the original Vyruz data
steps.instruction: Keep your own vz-data.rsc in a writable original-game folder outside the engine. Intro.avi in the same folder is optional. The original and this player can both write vzconf.txt, session and vz.sco there. Back up that whole folder before starting.

steps.title: Start the Linux player
steps.instruction: The v1.1.0 Linux x86-64 tar.gz contains Vyruz. Use a Vulkan driver and loader, glibc 2.38 or later, and libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.31. The picker uses zenity or kdialog. You can pass the original archive or folder to the upstream executable if the picker is unavailable.

warnings: Keep your original folder and effective user profile. A runtime backup cannot restore files stored in those external folders.

references.title: Find the remembered setup
references.instruction: On Linux the normal profile is $XDG_DATA_HOME/OpenVyruz or ~/.local/share/OpenVyruz. On Windows it is %APPDATA%/OpenVyruz. The game remembers the data path in game-folder.txt. If it cannot locate a user home it can write OpenVyruz relative to its working directory.

listings.name: Vyruz: Destruction of the Untel Empire / Vurus
listings.summary: Run Vyruz in Vurus using your own original disc image or extracted game resources.
listings.original_game_title: Vyruz: Destruction of the Untel Empire

steps.title: Prepare your original game files
steps.instruction: Copy your owned Vyruz ISO, or a single-BIN CUE with its BIN, beside the Vurus player, then start it. Keep the CUE and BIN together to import CD music, and keep your original separately. On first start Vurus imports the disc into data/ beside the player and reuses that import later, so you can then delete the copied image. To import a different image after a previous import, use --data with its path.

steps.title: Use the Mac release
steps.instruction: On macOS 15 or later, pick desktop release v202610242327-beta, extract the Intel or Apple Silicon archive matching your Mac into a writable folder, and run vurus from a terminal. The Mac builds are unsigned.

steps.title: Keep imports and progress
steps.instruction: Keep data/, saves/, slot1.vzs, options.cfg, vz.sco and benchmark-results/ with the player. Portcove keeps them across managed updates. If you keep a copy you manage yourself, back them up before replacing the player. Keep any resource folder, save file or options file you chose with --data, VURUS_DATA_DIR, --save-file or --options-file.

warnings: The managed routes use the desktop beta packages. The separate PortMaster package needs compatible handheld firmware. There is no Android APK or general-purpose Linux ARM64 desktop package in this release.

references.title: Set up the upstream PortMaster build on an ARM64 handheld
references.instruction: Use compatible ARM64 firmware with PortMaster installed, SDL 2.0.18 or newer and native OpenGL ES 3.0. Get vurus-portmaster.zip from https://github.com/rzrbld/vurus/releases/tag/portmaster-v202611031626-beta. Extract Vurus.sh, Vurus Benchmark.sh and vurus/ together into the firmware’s Ports folder.

references.title: Import and preserve your handheld data
references.instruction: Place your own ISO or single-BIN CUE and its BIN beside vurus.aarch64, or copy an existing data/ import there. Start Vurus from the firmware’s Ports menu. Back up data/, saves/, slot1.vzs, options.cfg and vz.sco before applying an upstream update. Keep these files when updating the engine in place. You manage this copy.

listings.name: Wario Land 4 (BioRhythmic Studios)
listings.summary: An unofficial native PC port of Wario Land 4. The upstream launcher needs your own unmodified US Game Boy Advance ROM.

steps.title: Open the upstream Windows launcher
steps.instruction: On Windows, select the Windows x64 release, extract the entire ZIP into a folder you own, and open wl4-launcher.exe. Keep both EXEs, SDL3.dll, and the notices together.

steps.title: Select the Linux AppImage
steps.instruction: Use the official Linux x64 AppImage on a host with glibc 2.38 or later. Make the file executable. In Portcove, select the AppImage and use its containing folder as the working directory. If FUSE is unavailable, enter --appimage-extract-and-run as one argument.

steps.title: Choose your original game
steps.instruction: In the launcher, choose Browse and select your own unmodified US Game Boy Advance ROM. The launcher checks for an 8 MiB file with game code AWAE and MD5 5fe47355a33e3fabec2a1607af88a404. Choose Launch Game.

steps.title: Select the prepared Windows player
steps.instruction: Select wl4-launcher.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

warnings: The packages contain recompiled game program code. Upstream's MIT notice covers its identified sources, and upstream documents inherited code with no recorded license. The launcher reads game data from your own original ROM.

The Windows v0.3.2-beta runtime could not start on the Windows 11 build 26300 host tested by Portcove. This release could not reserve the memory range it needs for the game. See upstream for newer beta releases.

The Windows launcher saves the selected ROM path in your user registry. Windows v0.3.2-beta can read earlier settings, but beta 1 and beta 2 cannot read the newer settings it saves. Back up settings before downgrading.

references.title: Registration ownership and removal
references.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

references.title: Player-data ownership
references.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: Windows %APPDATA%\wl4\wl4.sav and settings.cfg; the Windows user registry entry for the original ROM path; Linux ~/.local/share/biorhythmicstudios/warioland4/ and ~/.config/biorhythmicstudios/warioland4/ (or your XDG overrides). Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

listings.name: RaceWave46
listings.summary: Native Wave Race 64 recompilation. Gameplay remains untested.

listings.name: Wave Race 64: Recompiled
listings.summary: Native Wave Race 64 recompilation. Portcove installs the official packages on Windows and Linux.

steps.title: Windows: use a copy you already prepared
steps.instruction: On Windows, choose Install for the copy Portcove manages. To keep playing a copy you extracted yourself, select WaveRace64Recomp.exe with its folder as the working directory and leave arguments empty. You and upstream maintain that copy.

steps.title: Linux: prepare the host and choose Install
steps.instruction: Use an x64 host with glibc 2.43, libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.32, SDL2, GTK 3, FreeType and a working Vulkan driver. Choose Install and select your own Wave Race 64 (USA) (Rev A) original. Use Start Game after opening the managed copy.

steps.title: Keep a separate upstream Linux copy
steps.instruction: A copy you already extracted stays yours to maintain. Start it with WaveRace64Recomp.sh and use Load ROM to select your original if it has no source yet. Keep its creating runtime and profile before replacing it.

warnings: The package contains recompiled game code; some bundled components have their own notices. Use only your own original game.

references.title: Find your saves and settings
references.instruction: A copy with an empty portable.txt beside the program keeps saves and settings in its own folder: the saves folder and the .json settings files. Without it, Windows uses %LOCALAPPDATA%\WaveRace64Recomp and Linux uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/WaveRace64Recomp, usually ~/.local/share/WaveRace64Recomp. Back these up before replacing a copy you maintain.

references.title: Move from a Windows copy you added earlier
references.instruction: A v1.0.2 folder you added to Portcove keeps working where it is. Portcove doesn't copy its saves or settings into a managed copy. To switch, close the game and back up that folder's saves folder and .json settings files. Remove the registration (your files stay in place) and choose Install, but don't start the game yet. Open its saved data folder from the game's details and copy the saves folder and .json files into it. Portcove adds them to the game the first time you start it. If you've already started the managed copy, its own saves replace files copied this way.

listings.name: Wing Commander (Kilrathi Saga) (Wing Commander Reloaded / wc1-re)
listings.summary: Native SDL2 Wing Commander player for your own Kilrathi Saga installation. Portcove can manage a separate Windows x64 engine while the supported in-process launcher selects your existing writable game-data directory. Original files, SAVEGAME.WLD and shared SDL settings remain externally owned and outside Core backups. The older MSVC reconstruction and partial DOS route do not inherit this offer or gameplay qualification.

steps.title: Use the modern SDL2 player and your own Kilrathi Saga data
steps.instruction: Use the official modern SDL2 package for Windows x64, Linux x86-64 or an Apple silicon Mac with all companion libraries, or an already permitted working copy of that same route. Select normal wc1-modern.exe (wc1-modern on Linux or a Mac) for an attached copy. On an Intel Mac, the official Intel ZIP needs macOS 15 and a compatible Intel SDL3 library supplied separately for its SDL2 compatibility library. The separate win32-msvc420 reconstruction package is not this player. Use your own full Wing Commander Kilrathi Saga installation: GAMEDAT plus STREAMS/PREFLITE.STR, POSFLITE.STR and MISSION.STR. DOS support is partial and does not inherit this offer.

steps.title: Choose the actual writable original directory in upstream setup
steps.instruction: A new managed engine starts its supported graphical launcher with --gui. Browse to the actual permitted, writable Kilrathi Saga directory, review graphics/joystick choices and choose Launch WC1. Startup checks include GAMEDAT/MODULE.000, CAMP.000 and INSTALL.DAT and the Saga streams; they are not a full original-file identity audit. Portcove does not copy or authenticate those originals. The launcher and game run in the same process; cancelling setup is separate from successful gameplay.

steps.title: Preserve saves and the shared settings root
steps.instruction: The accepted upstream folder becomes the game working directory. Preserve the whole original tree, including SAVEGAME.WLD, unknown/custom files and any previous compatible runtime. Registry emulation also writes wc1-modern.cfg under the actual SDL preference directory for Origin Systems/WC Kilrathi Saga. These shared/external original, save and profile paths remain player-owned and outside Portcove-managed backups, restore and removal. A different engine folder does not isolate them; close all actual users before changing shared state.

steps.title: Keep this copy’s launch settings
steps.instruction: For an attached working copy retain its actual prepared working directory and established supported literal arguments. Starting without arguments opens the graphical launcher; existing direct arguments use the creating working directory unless --gui is included. Keep that choice truthful rather than starting a new engine folder with direct-game flags and no original data. Review exact intent/consent and choose Play separately. Do not substitute --check, a compiler, installer or historical reproduction binary for normal play.

steps.title: Keep runtime replacement and removal ownership separate
steps.instruction: Portcove manages replacement only for its separate managed engine; it does not adopt or move the original installation/profile. An attached copy keeps upstream/player ownership of preparation, runtime replacement, recovery and every external file. Preserve the old creating runtime and all actual state before updates; backward saves, alternate renderers, mods and controllers are not qualified here. Review/relink deliberate external executable replacement before Play. Removing a registration preserves external files; neither route promises to delete or back up outside originals, SAVEGAME.WLD or shared SDL preferences.

warnings: Use only game data and components you are already permitted to use. The engine license does not grant rights to unrelated assets, music or modifications.
External and shared player-data locations remain outside Portcove backups and removal. Preserve the creating runtime, every actual state root and unknown files before changes.

listings.name: Wolfenstein 3D (ReflectionHLE)
listings.summary: Play Wolfenstein 3D through ReflectionHLE with the matching original DOS game files.

steps.title: Use the matching original DOS edition
steps.instruction: Use your complete original DOS Wolfenstein 3D folder with WOLF3D.EXE and the matching WL1 or WL6 data. steps.title: Choose a fresh managed runtime or keep your external player
steps.instruction: For a fresh Portcove-managed runtime, use Install and then explicit Play. Keep the ordinary upstream launcher: choose this entry’s exact game/version and its complete matching original-data folder there. No automatic title dispatch or original authentication by Core is promised. The managed definition passes four separate literal arguments, -datadir, ., -cfgdir, ., with the actual player's parent folder as working directory (reflectionhle.exe on Windows, reflectionhle on Linux). On Mac, the official universal app runs with the same arguments from the folder containing reflectionhle.app. Upstream creates its version-specific writable directories after accepting the originals; no setup marker or helper is fabricated. Select reflectionhle.exe inside its wrapper folder and use that same folder as the working directory. Leave launch arguments empty to use the game/version picker. steps.title: Preserve the shared profile and each game version
steps.instruction: Windows normally stores ReflectionHLE settings and per-version writable data beneath %APPDATA%/reflectionhle. Preserve that whole profile, your original game folders and any custom data/config/mod locations with all copies closed before changing runtimes. Several game entries share settings; version-specific writable folders remain distinct. Changing a data/config argument redirects storage and does not migrate it. Retain the working runtime for existing saves; no cross-version or cross-engine save compatibility is established.

steps.title: Keep new private progress separate from old profiles
steps.instruction: The fresh managed runtime stores ReflectionHLE configuration, controller mappings, original-location references and per-version progress in the declared paths beside the player on Windows and Linux, or beside the app bundle on Mac. It imports no AppData, DOS or existing-player saves/configuration and adopts no populated external folder. Core manages that separate runtime and its declared data through the existing install/update, retained-runtime, backup/recovery and reviewed removal contracts. Keep originals and every external profile outside it unchanged. Existing user-selected registrations retain their creating runtime and old external ownership; they are not converted by this offer. Runtime rollback does not certify save compatibility. Preserve the creating runtime and actual progress before older-version use. Customized original/data/config argument overrides require separate upstream/external handling.

For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your WW2GI.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

Elsewhere, you and upstream replace this external player. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. steps.instruction: Install org.zdoom.Raze from Flathub for Linux x64 or ARM64. Make sure ~/.config exists in your home directory. Keep your original files and place a complete working copy of this game's data in its own subfolder under ~/.var/app/org.zdoom.Raze/.config/raze. Open Raze and choose this game if a picker appears. Close Raze and back up its actual configuration, saves and mods before updating through Flatpak.

Complete original-data and game selection through upstream before saving the player entry. steps.title: Choose the Windows nightly package
steps.instruction: In OpenXcom’s Nightly GitHub workflow, choose a successful upstream run. On Windows x64 download the Windows artifact, then extract the inner win64 ZIP into a dedicated folder. Keep its DLLs and data directories with OpenXcom.exe and open the player from that folder. The same artifact offers a separate win32 ZIP and an upstream installer.

steps.instruction: In the same workflow run, download the matching artifact. On Linux unpack the ZIP and start the AppImage. If the loader reports libjack.so.0 missing, install your distribution’s JACK runtime package. On Mac unpack the outer ZIP and use Mac Archive Utility on the inner Mac ZIP, then open openxcom.app on Intel or Apple Silicon. On Linux x86-64, select the complete official Nightly AppImage and its containing folder. Provide the host JACK and PipeWire libraries required by the package. If FUSE is unavailable, enter --appimage-extract-and-run as a separate first argument. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac, keep openxcom.app intact and select Contents/MacOS/openxcom with its containing folder. On Linux and Mac, enter -master and xcom2 as separate arguments, after --appimage-extract-and-run when you use it. Confirm the selected original and master game upstream before saving the registration. Use separate writable -user and -cfg folders for each game when you want to keep the profiles apart. Enter each option and its absolute path on separate lines.

steps.title: Prepare this title’s original data
steps.instruction: Copy the data subfolders from your X-COM: Terror from the Deep installation into TFTD inside the OpenXcom data or user folder. In the OpenXcom Mods menu, select the master game for this title.

warnings: Preserve every actual selected data/user/config folder, including UFO/TFTD resources, mods, savegames and screenshots. Keep the two original games and their campaigns distinct even if they share one player/profile. Back up with OpenXcom closed before changing runtime or mods.

listings.summary: Native Majora's Mask recompilation.
listings.original_game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask

source_editions.title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (Nintendo 64, USA 1.0)

steps.title: Run the Linux ARM64 package
steps.instruction: Extract the release ZIP, then unpack Zelda64Recompiled.tar.gz. Start Zelda64Recompiled from the extracted folder. The current ARM64 build needs glibc 2.34 or newer, SDL2, GTK 3, libatomic and a Vulkan-capable driver.

steps.title: Install the Linux x64 Flatpak
steps.instruction: Extract the Flatpak x64 ZIP to get io.github.zelda64recomp.zelda64recomp.flatpak. Install the file with Flatpak, then start io.github.zelda64recomp.zelda64recomp from the app menu or with flatpak run io.github.zelda64recomp.zelda64recomp.

steps.title: Select your original
steps.instruction: In the upstream game picker choose your own North American Majora’s Mask N64 cartridge dump. The game validates the matching original before play.

warnings: These packages use upstream or player-managed setup, replacement and data backups. Portcove has no native execution or populated-save result for these sibling packages.

references.title: Keep the external profile
references.instruction: Preserve ~/.config/Zelda64Recompiled on Linux, or your actual custom profile. For Flatpak also keep ~/.var/app/io.github.zelda64recomp.zelda64recomp. Back up the original, saves, mods and settings before replacing an upstream copy.

listings.name: Zeus: Master of Olympus (eZeus)
listings.summary: Prepare Zeus: Master of Olympus through its upstream player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use the matching original game
steps.instruction: Both Zeus: Master of Olympus and the Poseidon expansion original files are required, including for the base-game identity. Upstream currently supports English and Polish. Preserve the original installation and work in a separate complete copy; eZeus differs from the original and does not promise exact parity.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the player
steps.instruction: Prepare the full eZeus-0.8.2-beta.zip from its base release, then the later eZeus-0.8.2-beta.4.exe patch. The patch EXE alone is not a complete package. Follow the base release instructions: extract the eZeus folder under your working Zeus and Poseidon folder, perform upstream text conversion of Zeus_Text.eng and Zeus_MM.eng to the corresponding XML files, and place them where upstream specifies. Apply the patch player in the eZeus Bin folder, retaining all base resources. Register Bin/eZeus-0.8.2-beta.4.exe with Bin as working directory. engconverter-0.5.exe and VC_redist.x64.exe are preparation helpers, not players; run prerequisites deliberately only when needed.

steps.title: Prepare a separate upstream Linux build
steps.instruction: Use the tagged source and its submodules, with the documented Qt and SDL2 dependencies. Place the built eZeus player under your complete working eZeus/Bin folder and launch from that folder. Use the matching base preparation and text conversion from upstream. Keep both original games and the actual settings, Save and resource directories backed up before changing the engine.

steps.title: Choose the matching upstream-linked Mac package
steps.instruction: Upstream links separate Intel and Apple Silicon 0.8.1-Beta.8 packages from MacThings, which documents macOS 14 or later. Use the matching 0.8.1 base preparation on a separate working copy. Copy the eZeus player and its bundled libs together into the prepared eZeus/Bin folder. Place Zeus_MM.xml and Zeus_Text.xml in the eZeus root above Bin, as described by upstream. Keep the complete original Zeus and Poseidon files, settings and Save directory together. This build has its own resources and profile. Keep the later Windows patch separate.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Select the game executable and its working folder, and put each launch argument on a separate line. Choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, originals, saves and settings. Removing its registration leaves those external files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Close the game and keep a working copy and every data and profile folder before changing versions. Other platforms need their own setup instructions.
